documents.t: The three execution modes, the user's folder, the projects base and converting a project between modes. # decision 0066 Readable workspace folder name. Revises 0055: projectScopeRoot now receives workspace_dir_name, no longer the raw projectId, preserving the guarantee that api and engine agree on the project's root. User request: a readable physical folder (<slug>-<8 chars of the id>), with a unique id — PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT is ONE root for the whole instance, and slug alone isn't globally unique. Between the two options presented (lower-risk symlink vs. actually renaming the folder), the user explicitly chose the second. The id is born in CODE (crypto.randomUUID() in CreateProjectUseCase, no longer Postgres's defaultRandom()), because the folder name needs it BEFORE the INSERT. A project created before this migration kept the physical folder it already had — the backfill writes workspace_dir_name = id and NEVER renames any directory, and the name is FROZEN at creation: editing the slug afterward doesn't recompute the folder. A BEFORE INSERT trigger (the first ever in the product's migration history) applies the same id::text fallback for an insert that arrives without the field — a safety net, not the main path, and what avoids rewriting more than fifty test specs that insert projects with no knowledge of the concept. The engine reads the SAME column (Engine.Projects.Project.workspace_dir_name/1) to resolve Workspace.workspace_dir/1, never recomputing the name — the two derivations are, in practice, the same read against the same database. Outside the tool loop's hot path (which already receives ctx[:workspace_root] resolved once, at the agent worktree's creation); WorktreeCleanup switched from scanning disk to querying Project.all_workspace_dirs/0 in a single query, because the folder stopped being the project_id and there's no way back from one to the other without a query 0072 The project chooses where the code lives: the user's folder (Local) or a managed folder (Container). Revises part of 0065 and treads on 0055's ground — both had decided the OPPOSITE direction, heading toward the container wall, and that's why the consequences section is the most important part of this ADR. User request, with the variant explicitly chosen: freely typed path, aware of the warning that it only works mounted in the container. projects gains the pair (workspace_mode, workspace_path) with a CHECK tying them together — local with no path would be a terminal scope pointing nowhere, container with a path would be a second source of truth —, and the lock lives in the DATABASE because the column is read by two processes and written by scripts that don't go through the use case. container is the default: an existing project doesn't change location. projectScopeRoot now receives the LOCATION instead of the folder name and stays the SOLE derivation — no caller gained its own validation, for the same reason the function exists. The creation guard (RN-170) REJECTS with 400 and teaches: absolute path, no .., that exists, is a folder and is writable by the process (`W_OK 0104 ADRs 0072 and 0103 had never talked to each other: RN-170 requires a bind-mount at creation, RN-420 routes to the runner under the SAME workspace_mode == 'local' flag with no bind-mount at all — actually using the runner still had to pass the mounted-folder validation. workspace_mode (2 values) becomes execution_mode (3: container, mounted — the old local, RN-170 now conditional on it — and runner, with no bind-mount). A runner project is born with a DECLARED path and workspace: unverified state, promoted to verified only when a runner connects and confirms it on the HOST — the same spirit as the evidence-by-event gates docs/gates.yml already uses. Converting between the three values is now allowed, with no need to recreate the project. Product owner's prioritized backlog, recorded in this order: distributing the runner via npm publish (@brabo/runner, tsup), a long-lived account token (PAT) replacing the login replay in apps/runner/src/auth.ts — BEFORE distribution —, exclusivity by {project_id, machine_id} DEFERRED until a second real simultaneous dev, and guard.ts REAFFIRMED as best-effort — the real security boundary is authentication + approval + consent, never sandboxing 0107 Local folder navigation, revising (without editing) ADR 0072: the folder picker 0072 had refused because it required the api to enumerate the CONTAINER's filesystem now exists via the RUNNER (ADR 0103), which already has the right view — the user's real machine. Two new events on the SAME terminal:<projectId> channel (fs_list_dir/fs_home_dir), same pure-relay design as the PTY, correlated by ref. The api still enumerates no filesystem at all — no new routes. The security boundary stays the one from 0103 (authentication + no-effect reads + consent), not a path allowlist — guard.ts (which restricts an approved command's cwd) deliberately does NOT apply here, because the point is FREE browsing. Declared gap: on the project CREATION screen the ticket is per-project and the project is only born on confirmation, so "Browse folder..." there shows the declared state instead of faking an impossible connection — it works end to end where the project already exists 0108 Closes the gap ADR 0107 itself had declared: in runner mode, NewProjectWizard.tsx now creates the project when "Browse folder..." is clicked, not only on confirmation — using the path already typed, or a lexically valid, provisional placeholder (/workspace-a-confirmar, overwritten once the real runner connects, RN-423) when the field is still empty. Reused by an IDENTITY snapshot (name/externalId/adotando — never the path, whose refinement is the very point of browsing): unchanged identity reuses the same project, changed identity creates another. mounted mode doesn't change — path validation touches disk at creation, so it still waits for confirmation. Accepted side effect: an orphaned "unprovisioned" project if the wizard is closed before finishing, the SAME state any interrupted creation already produces today 0111 Converting execution_mode on an EXISTING project, correcting ADR 0104 item 4's claim that this was already possible "without recreating the project" — it wasn't; UpdateProjectDto kept excluding the two fields on purpose. A dedicated route (PUT :projectId/execution-mode, role:maintainer) orchestrates what a bare column write can't: refuses (409) while any dev agent of the project is non-idle in ANY session (engine.dev_agent_states, idle_tripped counts as active here, unlike RN-409's online count, because the agent still holds a captured workspace_root) — never draining or migrating a live agent; relocates permissions.json to the new scope root via a new PermissionsFileStore.move() (content never changes, only the physical path); retires the project_containers lifecycle row to removed (through stopped first if running) BEFORE the column flips when leaving container, and never auto-provisions when entering it; resets workspaceVerifiedAt on every real conversion. Declared, not hidden: conversion never copies code between scope roots — the engine re-derives the worktree from the project's bare repo on demand (Engine.Actions.Workspace.ensure!/4), so committed work is safe but an UNCOMMITTED diff in the abandoned old worktree is orphaned in place, not migrated and not deleted 0141 Creating a mounted project used to require hand-editing a bind-mount line into docker-compose.yml for BOTH api and engine and restarting them — which kills every in-flight agent turn, terminal socket and LLM call in the whole installation, to onboard ONE project. Tolerable while mounted was an escape hatch; disqualifying now that it becomes a first-class choice with a suggested path. So: ONE base, BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, configured once by the operator and mounted by IDENTITY ($X:$X) into api and engine, with every mounted project living underneath it and nothing edited per project, ever. Identity rather than a fixed mountpoint because projects.workspace_path is a string the user TYPES and the screen shows back: with host ≠ container the product would have to pick which of the two to store and either choice makes the screen lie to someone — and identity is exactly what lets projectScopeRoot (api) and Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/2 (engine) stay correct with zero new code, the leading-slash discriminator still deciding. A NEW variable, never PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR, for three reasons whose first has a data consequence: a managed workspace is named by workspace_dir_name (UNIQUE) and a mounted project is named by the USER, so <base>/loja and a container project whose dir name is loja would land in the SAME physical folder and init_from_bare! would git init inside someone else's project — nothing in the schema prevents it, since uniqueness is among workspace_dir_name values and never against a workspace_path basename. Absent is a NORMAL state: baseDeProjetos() returns null and never throws, GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base (maintainer, the same minimum as POST .../projects since deciding what that route offers is the only thing the value is for) carries the null to the client, and the wizard simply doesn't offer Mounted mode — never offer a mode the installation can't honor. And the /workspace blind spot finally gets a guard where one is possible: scripts/dev/preflight.mjs REFUSES to bring the stack up when the base overlaps the Brabo checkout in either direction, because it runs on the HOST — the api compares against process.cwd(), /workspace inside its own container, so someone who clones Brabo into $HOME/brabo and points the base there passes every existing validation and has dev agents executing inside the product's own tree, the ADR 0055 failure entering through a door it doesn't watch. Two declared costs: a symlink under the base resolves differently on the two sides (the folder browser refuses to descend into symlinks and counts them; the disk check at materialization is what catches the divergence, as a NAMED failure), and code outside the base requires moving the folder — v1 supports one base, and the refusal message says so instead of hinting at a hidden setting 0142 ADR 0141 decided WHERE a mounted project lives and explicitly left the other half to the next PR: WHEN that folder comes into existence. The product owner's requirement is literal — "if it's Mounted folder, the bind-mount must be created AFTER the architect's decision" — and today's code makes it impossible: validarCaminhoDeWorkspaceLocal runs at project CREATION and asks three disk questions (does it exist? is it a directory? can this process write to it?), refusing with 400 when any fails. Creation is the FIRST screen of the flow; the architect's decision happens many sessions later, so requiring the folder to be ready at creation is requiring it before any decision exists at all — and it is what keeps mounted from being a first-class choice, since a path the wizard SUGGESTS is by construction a path that does not exist yet. So mounted adopts the discipline runner already had (RN-423): only the LEXICAL predicate at creation, plus one new rule of its own — the path must sit inside BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE, the only folder of the machine the api and engine containers can see, with no base configured meaning the MODE is not available on this installation and the refusal saying so. The deferred verification comes back in materializarWorkspaceMontado (mkdir -p plus the same three disk questions, with the out-of-base refusal BEFORE the mkdir so a path written outside the product can't make the api create folders anywhere it reaches), called from two places: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase, the normal one, where Infra starting the container creates the folder and stamps workspace_verified_at — failure there is a NAMED failed, never a throw, and the lifecycle is NOT marked provisioning, because marking it and only then finding out you cannot write would leave the row asserting a state that never existed; and ConvertProjectExecutionModeUseCase, the declared exception, which has no container step to hang the work on and moves permissions.json into that very folder right after. What deliberately does NOT change is caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido: the base rule stays out of it because that predicate runs on EVERY READ via projectScopeRoot, and a LEGACY mounted project outside the base would start exploding when merely read. No migration, and the (execution_mode <> 'container') = (workspace_path IS NOT NULL) CHECK is untouched — deferring VERIFICATION never touches the PAIRING invariant 0146 The Mounted mode was finished and unreachable: ADR 0141 built the single base and ADR 0142 made it possible to suggest a path that does not exist yet, but nothing in the product ever asks the operator to configure BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE — so GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base has no caller in the web and the mode is simply never offered. So pnpm bootstrap gains a consent step: it proposes $HOME/projetos-brabo (under $HOME because that is what Docker Desktop shares BY DEFAULT — a default that first requires opening Docker's settings is a question in disguise), and NOT $HOME/brabo-projetos, because .env.example already uses that exact name as the commented example for PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR, the root the PRODUCT manages — the very conflation ADR 0141 refused, since <base>/loja would collide with a container project whose workspace_dir_name is also loja and bootstrap would git init inside someone else's project. The name is only the dodge; the protection is MECHANISM: the script refuses any base equal to, containing or contained in that root, reusing the dentroDe that already backs baseSobrepoeOCheckout. Written by scripts/dev/consentir-base.mjs in Node and never in bash, for two measured reasons: bootstrap.sh has no helper that writes a variable (garantir_env only copies the example, the only in-place writer being escreverEnv in preflight.mjs), and — decisive — a menu item CANNOT ASK, since every menu command runs in background with stdin from /dev/null so that nothing steals the user's arrow keys; a consent step written there would by construction be a step that cannot consent. Docker Desktop file sharing is PROVED BY MOUNTING (docker run --rm -v <base>:/sonda ... ls /sonda), never by reading settings.json: that file is undocumented, differs between macOS and Windows, changes across versions, and describes what the user configured rather than what the daemon will do — the same rule the product already applies to LLM providers, where a capability is declared only when proved by execution (ADR 0041/0042). This becomes the product's SECOND platform guard, next to validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux, and the two are symmetric in principle: each restricts only where the restriction means something. And the broker leaves profiles: ["container-broker"] in the LOCAL compose only — ADR 0130 chose that profile because "nothing calls it to write yet... in exchange for nothing", and that premise is dead: ADRs 0133/0136 gave it four real callers and ADR 0144 made mounted bring its container up THROUGH the broker, so with mounted as the local default the broker is what separates the default mode from BrokerIndisponivelError. The asymmetry is what carries it: whoever runs pnpm dev already holds the Docker socket — they are running docker compose — so the broker receiving it grants nothing the operator lacks, while in production the socket is a real privilege boundary and the operator is not the developer. The five containment layers are untouched: this changes WHEN the broker runs, never WHAT it accepts
documents.s: Where the code lives — execution modes

documents.t: The project container's lifecycle, the image decision, the Docker port and the broker that talks to the daemon. # decision 0065 Container per project: the boundary stops being policy. Revises 0055, which had declared its own pending item: path scope is POLICY, not isolation — as long as the Brabo monorepo is mounted in the same container that executes commands, the boundary depends on the policy getting it right, and a symlink from inside pointing outward isn't detected. Findings Z and AD (verb allowlist doesn't converge — verb, form and invocation are distinct spaces) reinforce Phase 13's same conclusion: the path to autonomy doesn't go through loosening policy, it goes through changing the boundary. The user's decision, verbatim: each project gets its own container, inside it the agent is FREE (read, write, install, build, test, run), and Code only unlocks once the ARCHITECT decides which image goes up — they're the one who knows which runtime the stack calls for. The image is born as an ARTIFACT (artifact.project_image in the event log, versioned, no table — revising means emitting again), with an explicit OCI tag (latest rejected) and mandatory rationale; the gate (RN-105) makes the Code tab respond 409 while sem_decisao, in the SAME function that already contains the path (RN-092), never duplicated across the four routes. What's left as the boundary is OUTSIDE: git push, PR and deploy don't go through the terminal — not even inside the project's scope —, and the rule is deny, not require_approval, because "always allow" writes the pattern into allow and one click would reopen the door forever; the message redirects to the TYPED action (git_push/git_merge/pr_open), which is already the dev agent's real path. Network is decided ONCE in the artifact (network: none by default, egress authorized by the user) and not command by command — repeating the allowlist for egress would repeat the mistake Z and AD proved doesn't converge; spend (cpus/memory/pids) has a cap that REFUSES instead of silently downgrading. HONEST, declared cut: the container's lifecycle (provisioning, recycling, cleanup, what survives a restart) is left for the phase with a migration slot — container state is mutable and needs a table, and a container that comes up without recycling is worse than none. Consequence: the "inside is free" half of the terminal policy has NOT changed yet; 0055 keeps holding as-is until the wall really goes up 0081 Container lifecycle: a state table, no orchestrator. Closes the cut 0065 declared about itself ("What this ADR does NOT do") — project_containers (migration 0046) records mutable STATE (status, image_version pointing at the Architect's decision without duplicating it, container_id, DECLARED resource caps, failure_reason), one row per project like dev_agent_states in the engine (0045), with a pure state machine (provisioning → running ⇄ stopped, failed reachable from all three, removed only exits by reprovisioning) in the same shape as session-state-machine.ts. Prior investigation confirmed NO product service mounts /var/run/docker.sock or runs privileged — and that's why the two use cases (Registrar/ObterCicloDeVidaDoContainer) only WRITE and READ, no real Docker call: mounting the socket to "actually make it work" would be a security decision (a root-escalation vector) nobody asked for in this slice. The first transition (provisioning) requires the image already decided (RN-105, same gate as the Code tab) and FREEZES version/resources onto the row; a project in workspace_mode: 'local' (0072) is refused, because it doesn't stand up its own container. No new HTTP route — with no real consumer yet, exposing one would be guessing a contract 0083 The Terminal tab gets the lifecycle's real consumer, not the terminal itself. Revises the part of 0081 that deferred the HTTP route until a real consumer existed — this piece (PROGRAM 28, Wave 5/F2) was that consumer. The original plan was the full interactive terminal, but Phase 25b stays cut: no service mounts /var/run/docker.sock, and nothing in production transitions project_containers (ADR 0081 created the table, not an orchestrator). Implementing a fake terminal — or one running in the same container as the Brabo monorepo, the debt 0055 already describes as policy — would invent capability, the same mistake ADRs 0041/0042 refuse for provider and model. The real delivery: GET /projects/:projectId/container/lifecycle (RN-267), a faithful mirror of ObterCicloDeVidaDoContainerUseCase, and CodeBottomPanel.tsx showing that state (translated badge, failure reason) UNDER the explanatory text that already existed — never replacing it —, fetched only while the Terminal tab is open (RN-268). null (never provisioned) is today's honest, most common result 0128 Docker access in the runner goes behind a PORT with exactly five operations (start/stop/remove/inspect/exec), and the implementation was chosen by a PROOF that failed. dockerode was installed, imported, instantiated and exercised (ping()) through a --self-test-docker flag run against the real artifacts — never an import a bundler could tree-shake. tsup passed (it leaves dependencies as an external require, so dockerode never entered the bundle); bun build --compile (ADR 0112, the standalone binary) REPROVED, with the error recorded verbatim: Could not resolve: "../build/Release/cpufeatures.node". The chain is mandatory, not accidental — docker-modem/lib/modem.js requires ./ssh at module top level, ssh2 requires cpu-features, and that optional native binding is wrapped in a runtime try/catch the BUNDLER does not have. Same class of problem ADR 0112 documented for node-pty, with the difference that decides it: there the binding is ESSENTIAL, here it accelerates an SSH transport this runner never uses (it speaks to the local unix socket). Measured and NOT adopted, so nobody redoes the investigation: --external cpu-features compiles (280 modules against 79, +1.7 MB per binary × 5 platforms) and dockerode works inside the binary — it is exactly the creative workaround the product owner excluded in advance. So the runner uses execFile('docker', …), dockerode is gone from the lockfile, and the BROKER (PR 1.2) does not inherit the decision: it ships in an image we build and never becomes a standalone binary. Containment is the TYPE, not caller discipline: no field for privileged/cap_add, RedeDoContainer is `'none' 0130 The container BROKER is born — a new Node/TS service (apps/broker), the only process in the product that talks to a Docker daemon on the SERVER, and the api never receives the socket. Three inseparable decisions. First, the port MOVES: docker-port.ts and docker-cli.ts (and their two specs) leave apps/runner/src/ for a new workspace package, packages/docker-port, consumed by runner and broker — exactly what ADR 0128 wrote it would do, never copied, because "a second file with the same five operations and a sixth 'broker only' is the beginning of the end of containment". packages/shared was refused for the invariant it declares and packages-shared-so-tipos.spec.ts keeps honest (100% type, and the api's production image dies with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING if a runtime value survives tsc); the new package has NO build step and is BUNDLED by both consumers (tsup, bun build --compile), which is why the api cannot consume it and why validarDecisaoDeImagem does NOT move. The standalone binary survived the move, measured: build, build:bin, smoke and smoke:bin green, Bun bundle 79 → 83 modules, npm pack --dry-run unchanged. Second, and this is the point of the service: the broker does not accept a container spec. It takes a projectId plus one of the five operations, READS the Architect's decision from the api itself (GET /internal/projects/:projectId/container-spec, RN-485) and COMPOSES image, network, resources and the single mount — there is no field in which to write privileged, cap_add, network: host or a free -v, because there is no field. It revalidates what the api returned, since containment that depends on the caller being correct is not containment, and the two validations answer different questions (the api's is about the ARTIFACT being reviewable; this one is the parse of untrusted JSON into the closed type). One check exists only here and is new: an image reference starting with - would be read by the CLI as a FLAG — execFile without a shell solves command injection, not ARGUMENT injection. Third, the api sends NO path at all: -v is resolved by the daemon against the HOST filesystem, so a path from inside the api container would silently mount an empty folder; the broker joins workspaceDirName (RN-109) with its own PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT and refuses start when that is missing rather than guessing. pidsLimit joins the port for a reason worth naming — the artifact always carried three numbers and dropping one would make it promise a cap the container does not get. Contained by five independent layers: no published port, an internal: true network only the api joins, the shared service token compared in constant time, five operations, and the computed spec. It ships under profiles: ["container-broker"] in both composes and is therefore OFF by default, and its image is NOT published to the GHCR — docker-bake.hcl and ALVOS keep the four images of ADR 0119. The api gains a port and an HTTP client whose only CALLER is inspect: the container lifecycle route now returns the OBSERVED state beside the RECORDED one, never fused, with naoObservado naming why when there was no way to look (RN-486) — so the table can now lie, and the read says so. Nothing brings a container up: no loop, no queue, no container_start proposed_action, and RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase is byte-for-byte unchanged, mode guard included 0131 The Architect gains a seventh tool, route_modules_to_infra: one item {modulo, imagemCandidata, porque} per module of the CURRENT module_map, recorded as artifact.module_routing — no table, same design as artifact.module_map/artifact.project_image/artifact.c4_diagram, the event IS the artifact. The Architect only CANDIDATES; electing among the candidates (or refusing all of them) is Infra's job, in a later PR — this one only produces the auditable list. Each item's image goes through the SAME rule choose_project_image already applies (validarDecisaoDeImagem: explicit tag/digest, latest rejected, a real rationale), reused rather than reimplemented per item; the new domain (module-routing.ts) only adds what's proper to the LIST — empty is refused (not a decision), a repeated module is refused (ambiguous: which of the two images wins?), and each modulo must name one that exists in the current module_map, refused by naming the VALID ones, same rule as assign_story_modules. :direct, never proposed_action: routing has no external effect. build_kickoff/1 — the Architect's only source of tool ORDER — lists the new tool right after create_module_map 0133 ADR 0131 left half a sentence hanging — "the Architect only candidates, Infra elects, in a separate PR" — and this is that PR, wired to the other hanging sentence, in the broker's own port comment (ADR 0130): "starting is external effect and doesn't happen without a proposed_action; Infra proposes it, with the user's final authority — another PR." The join between the two exposes a question neither ADR answered: the broker takes no spec, it reads GET .../container-spec, which reads artifact.project_image (RN-105) — not artifact.module_routing. So an election that doesn't become a new version of artifact.project_image is auditable and INERT — the container that comes up is whatever choose_project_image said, unrelated to what Infra just elected. Decision: the election REUSES DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase whole, called now with decidedBy: 'infra-lead' instead of the default 'arquiteto' — same validation (validarDecisaoDeImagem, same resource ceiling), same single "current" artifact, same precedent module-routing.ts's own comment already set for reusing instead of reimplementing. The elected image MUST be one of the routing's imagemCandidata — never invented — checked before touching the artifact, refused by name with the valid candidates listed when it isn't. New container_start proposed_action (maintainer, deliberately outside the absolute-ceiling block in decide.ts, same reasoning already recorded there for propose_execution_plan/assess_implementability — first election, not a ceiling raise) is the FIRST real caller of ContainerBrokerPort.start — of the five operations ADR 0128/0130 declared, only inspect had one before. RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase gets its first non-test caller too, transitioning provisioning → running (or straight to running from stopped, since the ADR 0081 state machine refuses stopped → provisioning) only after the broker confirms. Dev agents still do not run inside the container that comes up — that's a later PR 0134 Closes what ADR 0133 left declared: "dev agents still do not run inside the container that comes up — that's a later PR." Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 gains a FIFTH outcome, :executar_no_container — execution_mode: container with a project_containers row REGISTERED running (Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1, a new read-only Ecto schema mirroring Engine.Projects.Project's pattern) — and the terminal command crosses engine → api (POST internal/projects/:projectId/container-exec, a new route in InternalProjectsController, not the broker-facing InternalContainersController, since the caller here is the engine and nothing is WRITTEN to the lifecycle table) → broker (ContainerBrokerPort.exec, the last of the five ADR 0128/0130 operations to gain a real caller), running via docker exec instead of System.cmd inside the engine process. cwd, when present, is translated from the HOST path (inside PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT) to /work by the engine before the call — verified in code, not assumed: the broker's raizDoProjeto (PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT + workspaceDirName) and the engine's PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT + workspace_dir_name resolve the SAME physical directory, so Workspace.ensure!/4 needed zero changes — the container is just a second observer of the worktree the dev agent already had. A running row is only ever the REGISTERED state (RN-486: registered and observed never merge); a dead or externally-removed container turns the broker call into an ordinary failed_result — never a crash, never a silent fallback back outside the container, which would reopen the isolation gap this PR closes. Terminal actions scoped to the project's real container also gain an auto-approval FLOOR — containerExecutionActive in DecideContext, set by ProposeActionUseCase only for terminal in execution_mode: container — that changes decide()'s INITIAL value from require_approval to auto_approve; it is a floor, not a new ceiling: agent_autonomy/permissions.json can still lower it exactly as they already lower the old default, and the five absolute ceilings (path scope, external-effect git/privileged command, protected-branch merge, instruction_patch, parallelism) keep running on top unchanged. The safety argument is a second, stronger boundary, not the absence of the first: decide() never sees a /work path (that translation happens later, in the engine), so the lexical path-scope cap keeps operating on the same host paths as always, redundant with — not replaced by — the Docker mount namespace and the broker's own /work revalidation 0135 Executes decision #5 of the "real container execution" plan, already accepted before this PR existed: the RN-105 image gate — 409 on the Code tab until someone decided artifact.project_image — stops being dispensed for mounted/runner (ADR 0072/RN-169, revised by ADR 0104/RN-421). ReadProjectCodeUseCase.portaoDoContainer drops its executionMode !== 'container' early return; the gate becomes unconditional across all three modes, and ProjectCodeTab (web) stops treating mounted/runner as a special case — same useQuery, same four states, modoLocal branch removed, which SIMPLIFIES the component rather than adding a case. Accepted cost, stated plainly: every EXISTING mounted/runner project without a decided image — including this repo's own dogfooding projects, exp001/exp002 — loses Code-tab access the instant this ships, until the Architect (or Infra's election, ADR 0133) decides one; that is operator action required AFTER deploy, so the branch is breaking/, not bugfix/, even though the change reads as a fix, and the version bump to MAJOR is mechanical, not manual. RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase also drops its 400-by-mode rejection — project_containers can register a row for all three modes now — but investigated and confirmed unchanged: reaching running for real stays impossible for mounted/runner, enforced in exactly one place, ContainerBrokerPort.start()'s ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError (the broker runs on the SERVER and cannot see the user's folder), which ExecuteContainerStartUseCase already turns into an ordinary container.start_failed — never a crash, never a silent fallback — BEFORE any lifecycle transition is even attempted, so no row is born for those modes through the real approval path despite the 400 being gone. No second mode check was added at the api/propose layer on purpose: duplicating the broker's would-be gate creates a second place to drift from the first, the exact lesson the broker's own comment already recorded while pointing at this ADR. Also investigated, and left declared rather than fixed here (out of this PR's API/domain scope): neither propose_container_start (the Infra Lead's tool) nor GetInfraContextUseCase restrict by executionMode today, so the Infra Lead can still propose container_start for a mounted/runner project — pre-existing gap, wastes one approval cycle, fails loud and named rather than silently 0136 The global containers page (/containers, cross-project) closes the ADR 0130 port comment's other declared gap — "stop/remove have no caller yet" — with two decisions the plan didn't specify. First: the page reads the REGISTERED state in three constant queries (ContainersOverviewRepository, same no-N+1 shape as ProjectsSummaryRepository), but asking the broker for the OBSERVED state is a network call per project — so only provisioning/running rows are eligible, capped at TETO_DE_VERIFICACOES_POR_CARGA (20) per load, in parallel; what falls outside either rule carries its OWN naoVerificado reason, never confused with the broker's own naoObservado (RN-468/486 discipline extended to a new screen). Second: container_stop gets container_start's exact calibre (maintainer, configurable auto-approve, never seeded); container_remove — the only one of the three that discards the container and forces a full reprovision — joins the SAME absolute ceiling as external-effect git/privileged commands (RN-418): never auto-approvable, "always allow" refused at the source. ContainerBrokerPort.remove was already docker rm --force (removes even running, one call); rather than widen the state machine with a running -> removed shortcut, ExecuteContainerRemoveUseCase records the two real hops (stopped, then removed). "Start again" reuses container_start verbatim — zero backend change — building its payload from the project's current image decision instead of a fourth action type 0137 Closes the other half ADR 0135 left declared: mounted/runner now require a decided image (RN-105 gate, all three modes) but still had no way to bring a container up — the server-side broker refuses those two modes outright, because their code lives in a folder only the USER's machine can see. container_start/container_stop/container_remove gain a SECOND execution path, branched by executionMode only at EXECUTION time (never at propose or approve, both still mode-agnostic): container keeps going through the broker unchanged; mounted/runner now ask the ENGINE to relay to the connected RUNNER, over three new event pairs on the same Phoenix channel — container_start/_result, container_stop/_result, container_remove/_result — replicating the exact exec/exec_result pattern rather than inventing a new one. The runner answers with DockerViaCli (@brabo/docker-port), the SAME port the broker uses server-side, proven so far only by --self-test-docker and now with a real caller; the image it starts is READ from the current decision (ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase, the same use case the broker's own spec route already calls, invoked directly since both run in the api process), never re-elected. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor gained NO new outcome: it already routed every command of a connected runner project to the channel unconditionally (RN-423) — host-vs-container is a decision the RUNNER makes internally (EstadoDoRunner.containerAtivo, tratarExec switching to docker exec with cwd translated by prefix swap, cwdParaContainer). guard.ts's $HOME containment (RN-434) needed zero new code to cover the new mount — verified by reading the file whole: the bind IS estado.dir, the same root already validated at CLI startup, before any channel connects. "No runner connected"/timeout (RunnerNaoConectadoError) and "the runner tried and refused" (RunnerRecusouContainerError) are both ordinary failed outcomes, never an uncaught exception — same discipline as BrokerIndisponivelError/BrokerRecusouError 0143 A real exp001 run had ten dev tasks lock up at once, and the finding was not the particular folder that failed — it was that nothing ordered container before dev agent: no container_start was ever proposed, and ten dev agents started anyway. So Engine.Dev.AgentIo.try_claim/2 — the SINGLE claim point — now asks ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1 (the predicate ADR 0134 already introduced, no new machinery) BEFORE calling the api, and without a REGISTERED running row the agent falls to :idle, persists, and emits dev.blocked_by_container. In the ENGINE and not only at the api's activate-execution gate, because claiming has one path no route covers: REHYDRATION does no :work cast — DevAgentServer.init/1 -> finish_restart_recovery/1 -> try_claim/2 claims on its own, so an HTTP-only gate would let every rehydrated agent go back to work containerless, in exactly the situation where nobody is watching. :idle and not a new status, for the reason try_claim/2's own docblock had recorded back in Phase 12b: it is the only state a wake still rescues, and every handle_info/2 guard is keyed to it — a :blocked_by_container would be a state nothing rescues. What distinguishes "the queue emptied" from "there is no container" is the EVENT, never the status. Waking is by outbox: RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase appends container.running in the SAME transaction that records the arrival, under a container aggregate (the third Engine.Outbox.Drain reads, next to session/task) rather than borrowing task to save a query line, with the PROJECT as aggregateId; the delivered message is the EXISTING {:wake, :became_claimable}, whose semantics already are "there may be work now" — a new one would need a new handle_info/2 clause in both servers with an identical guard and no different decision to make. Second half, same rule seen from the other side: TerminalExecutor.decisao_de_execucao/1 stops degrading silently — container with no running container used to fall through to System.cmd INSIDE the engine process, so ADR 0134's isolation held only on the happy path. It now refuses (:recusar_container_ausente), mirroring the runner mode's two existing refusals, with mounted in the same branch, and the catch-all shrinks to what it should always have covered alone: nonexistent project or malformed id. Declared cost, and the reason this can only ship AFTER mounted gets a container: a project without one stops working — loudly, which is the point 0144 A project in Mounted mode could not have a container at all, blocked twice over: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase sent every non-container mode to the RUNNER (which requires a connected brabo-runner), and the broker refused any non-container mode at the source. Both refusals were about GEOMETRY rather than the mode's name — a mounted project's folder sat somewhere arbitrary on the operator's disk that the server's Docker daemon had no reason to see — and ADR 0141 changed exactly that geometry by putting every mounted project under ONE base mounted by identity. So the broker gains a SECOND root, BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE, and the api starts sending a DISCRIMINATED locator that says which root a segment belongs to: gerenciada (the managed folder, named by workspace_dir_name), montada (the RELATIVE path under the base) or indisponivel (no root here reaches it, with the reason). The ADR 0130 invariant is untouched and is the reason for the shape: what crosses the wire is still only the half the broker's root does not cover, the api never learns where those roots are on the host, and the broker never learns anything about the project — neither side alone can write an arbitrary path, and sending an absolute one would put the containment of a root-equivalent process back in the caller's hands. Three variants and not two because indisponivel has two DIFFERENT fixes — a runner project (fix: the runner, on the other side) and a LEGACY mounted project created outside the base (fix: move the folder) — and a null would send whoever operates to the wrong place half the time; a folder that IS the base lands there too, since <root>/ would mount every mounted project inside one project's container. Neither root ever stands in for the other: whichever is missing is named in the refusal (BaseDeProjetosNaoConfiguradaError, mirroring RaizDeWorkspacesNaoConfiguradaError), because the managed root is named by workspace_dir_name and the base is named by the user, so falling back would mount someone else's code with nothing indicating why. Three barriers stand over the concatenation, not one — the api refuses what is outside the base, packages/docker-port refuses a segment that is not relative (.., absolute, empty, NUL), and raizDeProjetoValidada still runs over root + segment before it becomes a -v. On the api side the branch becomes one of DESTINATION: container and mounted go to the broker, only runner to the runner, and container_stop/container_remove move with container_start necessarily — bringing a container up on the server and then asking the user's machine to stop it would leave running, with no way to stop it, what is running. And mounted ELECTS the image like container rather than reading the current one like the runner path: the broker composes from artifact.project_image, which it FETCHES from the api, so an election not written to that artifact would be inert — the ADR 0133 argument applied to a second mode 0180 The project container runs as the FOLDER'S OWNER (--user uid:gid, measured by the api, revalidated by the broker, never from a request body), so dev agents can write to /work under --cap-drop ALL (AT-247). Adds one field to the spec, opens no containment door 0190 The Infra brings the container up ON ITS OWN when its handoff is accepted (AT-260, owner decision 01/10), revising ADR 0133's "never seeded" without editing it: the accept seeds container_start: auto_approve for the Infra agent, and the Infra Lead's SERVER — not the model, not a new tool — elects the routing candidate covering the most modules (first one on a tie) and proposes container_start before the first model call, through the SAME path as the tool, with the mode/state refusals (RN-566/610) and the no-broker 409 intact. runner keeps container_start_via_runner with approval, container_remove stays in the absolute cap, and the RN-668 closing stays true. Same owner decision (AT-262): the Dev Lead is offered BY THE INFRA, only with the project container running — the Architect's double handoff goes away, and ADR 0053/0085's "the Dev Lead comes from the Architect" changes without being edited 0199 The container's MINIMUM resources are DERIVED from the module_map (AT-261, owner decision 01/10): each module may declare resources (cpus, memoryMb, pidsLimit — all three or none), and container_start with resources omitted — always the case for the server's start on handoff acceptance (ADR 0190) — starts with the SUM over modules, because they all share ONE container. A module without a declaration floors the container at today's default instead of inventing a number; a map with no declarations gives exactly today's default. A sum above the ceiling is 400 to the Architect when the map is created; a request below the minimum is a named failed 0208 The Infra INHERITS the network the Architect declared in artifact.project_image (AT-392, owner decision 02/10): the server start on handoff acceptance and the propose_container_start tool without network use the Architect's egress/none instead of a literal none, and still start without a click; revises ADR 0190 point 3, departs from ADR 0065 §4, and declares the price (egress reaches the host's published ports, ADR 0189).
