documents.t: Chunks and hybrid search, its measurement, the Neo4j graph and the artifacts projected from the event log. # decision 0079 chunks table for the Chat RAG: vector(768) and tsvector on the SAME row (not two tables with a JOIN), an HNSW index (vector_cosine_ops, not IVFFlat — the table starts empty) and GIN, three honest scopes (docs/adr/session) mutually exclusive via CHECK. Migration 0045 creates CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector itself, because docker/postgres/init.sql only runs on the volume's first initialization — and that's why it's born on a breaking/ branch: creating the extension may require a privilege the application's role doesn't have in production 0080 Hybrid search: weights, threshold and what counts as a citation. docs/adr are indexed from the project's OWN git repository (via ReadProjectCodeUseCase, the same credential/gate/path check as the Code tab); session indexes only chat.message/agent.response (the rest of the event log is mechanism, not citable knowledge). Chunking by paragraph/heading, 1200 characters with 150 of overlap — a documented starting point, not calibrated against real data. When the embedding provider (fixed: ollama/nomic-embed-text, same dimension as RN-222) doesn't respond, the pipeline saves the chunks WITHOUT a vector instead of failing outright — search_vector is GENERATED ALWAYS AS and depends on no provider at all — and declares the gap in the report, never faking full indexing. Hybrid search is TWO independent queries (searchByVector/searchByLexicalQuery, each on the index made for it), merged by a weighted sum (0.6 vector, 0.4 lexical — normalized ts_rank and cosine scales aren't comparable by nature) and cut at a threshold (0.2); weights and threshold are an adjustable starting point, not science. A citation is chunkId/content/separate scores (null, not zero, when a signal found nothing)/origin as a union discriminated by kind (file with sourcePath/headingPath, or session with sessionId/eventId). Reindexing is always MANUAL (POST .../rag/reindex, an idempotent full rebuild) — no watcher on push, no watcher on session close 0082 Chat RAG becomes its OWN tab (key: 'rag'), without renaming sessions. 0080 left the pipeline and the three routes ready; 0078/RN-202 had deferred the "Chat RAG" label because the capability didn't exist — now it does, and the question was only WHERE it lives. sessions is conversation with an ACTIVATED agent (spends the owner's key per turn, RN-058); RAG is search over an already-built index, with no agent in the middle and read-only by nature — merging the two would force the same thread to express structurally different things, so the answer was a new tab (ordem: 28, between Code and Backlog) instead of renaming the existing one. The screen consumes the three 0080 contracts with no guessed shape (searchRag/getRagCoverage/reindexRag, types mirrored 1:1) and shows the two honest degradations the backend already declared and no screen was reading yet: vectorAvailable: false becomes a visible warning (RN-252) and coverage never invents "reindexed Xmin ago" — the response carries no such data. Citation from a session origin navigates to the exact EVENT reusing useNavigate + highlightEvent, the SAME mechanism the Psychologist's evidence chips already use (RN-253); a file origin shows path/heading as text, no link — the Code tab has no deep-link by path today, and building one is out of scope for this piece. The reindex button only shows for owner/maintainer on the client, mirroring the maintainer rule the route already enforces (RN-238/RN-254) — the api is still the one that guarantees it 0099 Neo4j comes in as a KNOWLEDGE graph — memory DERIVED from the event log, never a source of truth — for versioned prompt templates (PromptTemplate/PromptVersion) and relational memory (interactions, Psychologist hypotheses with evidence, Anamnesis profiles, handoffs). pgvector STAYS the chunks' vector index — the graph stores no embedding. The neo4j-driver lives in the API (not the engine): the API already owns all persistence and the existing RAG, the engine consumes it over internal HTTP with a service token as always. GraphStore.onModuleInit never throws — the three env vars are mandatory in production and optional outside it, unavailability becomes a GraphUnavailableError/503, never a raw 500. A pattern explicitly inspired by the ErickWendel/neo4j-ai-experiments repository (graph as agent memory + prompts as files separate from code) 0100 New rag_search tool for the engine's agents — closes the biggest gap in the existing RAG (pgvector, hybrid search): no agent had ever queried it, only the "Chat RAG" web tab. Calls POST /internal/rag/search (reuses HybridSearchUseCase with no duplicated logic), formats hits with citation (path + snippet), degradation (degraded: true) always visible at the START of the text. Its own caps (RN-150): top_k clamped to 10, a 16 KiB byte cap. A new one-shot ollama-model-loader service (dev and prod) closes a separate real bug: nomic-embed-text was never pulled automatically, and RAG silently degraded to lexical-only in any clean environment 0101 Consuming the graph foundation: InstructionFiles gains a :graph source (precedence db > graph > dir > root, reusing the existing ETS cache), with no change to any GenServer's contract — ux-designer, Psychologist and Anamnesis now TRY resolving a template from the graph before the inline text, which becomes the fallback. Two separate flags (graph_templates_enabled?, graph_instruction_templates_enabled?) on purpose — a single key would clash with OPPOSITE defaults between parallel workstreams. Psychologist/Anamnesis compose "recent"/"time window" with RELEVANT snippets via rag_search (never a replacement, always additive — with no hit, behavior is identical to before). The graph writes itself: GraphProjector drains a SECOND outbox lane (aggregateType: 'graph_projection', never matched by the engine's filter) and calls the already-existing write use cases — the engine NEVER writes to the graph directly, preserving the event log as the single source of truth 0113 Attach a local folder from the user's OWN machine as read-only reference material — WITHOUT the brabo-runner CLI, explicitly distinct from execution_mode: runner (ADR 0104), which needs a real host path. The browser reads file CONTENTS (File.text()) and RELATIVE paths (File.webkitRelativePath) — never an absolute host path, because the File API doesn't expose one to any site; there is no path to route through the Runner (ADR 0107) or validate like ADR 0072's guard, because there is no path at all. chunks.scope gains a fourth value, 'local' (migration 0052, additive ALTER TYPE, zero new CHECK — the existing constraints already split on "is it session or not"), reusing the whole RAG pipeline (chunking, embedding, hybrid search, citation) instead of a parallel mechanism. One-shot upload: aggregate caps (file count, summed bytes) REJECT (400) the whole batch instead of truncating silently, an individual oversized/unrecognized file is only skipped; re-uploading is the ONLY resync mechanism, deliberately never wired into the generic "Reindex now" (which re-reads from a source the server can revisit — this scope has none) 0129 The RAG hybrid search finally leaves a trail — but as TABLES (rag_searches/rag_feedback), not session events: session_events.session_id is NOT NULL and a search from the RAG tab is a project search with no session, so the event log would silently drop exactly the searches a human judged (same class of problem that cut embedding metering in ADR 0075). The weights are FROZEN on each row, like the frozen price in metering (ADR 0042), so a later calibration cannot silently rewrite what every earlier measurement meant. rag.search/rag.feedback exist only when there IS a session, and are narration, never the source of the measurement. Recording telemetry never brings the search down — and never fails silently either: origin infra in the log and an explicit searchId: null. Nothing is calibrated here; this step only instruments. 0132 The RAG's turn for a golden-set: same shape as the QA Automation agent's (ADR 0123) — a permanently-excluded ExUnit tag (:golden_set_rag), a ratchet floor keyed by MODEL, a seed script called through System.cmd — copied on purpose rather than re-derived, with the one adaptation the domain forces: RAG's hybrid search runs entirely inside the api (HybridSearchUseCase), with no LLM chat judgment anywhere in the path, so seed-golden-set-rag.ts both provisions AND runs the search itself, and the Elixir side only invokes it and applies the floor — reimplementing the search in Elixir would test a second implementation, never the real one. The 17 questions are COMPOSED from real RNs/ADRs, not extracted — checked first: gh issue list on this solo-dev repo returns "No Issues", so there is no genuine question corpus to mine, and that is stated rather than faked. The corpus indexed is real, though: 22 curated files from this repository's own docs/, copied verbatim and indexed by the same IndexProjectDocsUseCase any real project uses — curated, not the full 130+ ADR tree, for embedding cost in a manual run. The hit criterion — file path, never the exact chunk, inside the top 5, never rank 1 — is a pure, tested function (golden-set-criterio.ts), because chunking is exactly the parameter this whole program exists to be free to revise, and the Chat RAG cites several chunks per answer, not just the first. New gate rag-acertivo in docs/gates.yml, warn (there is no CI running a real LLM), evidence tipo: teste — what proves this gate is the golden-set itself, not an event. Measured for real, twice, deterministically: 17/17 questions found their file inside the top 5, in both runs, against a real Ollama nomic-embed-text and an isolated Postgres 0138 Stage 3 of the RAG-measurable program: the RAG golden-set (ADR 0132) starts running for real in CI, on a new .github/workflows/golden-set-rag.yml — but SCHEDULED (nightly cron + workflow_dispatch), never on pull_request, a cadence the product owner chose given the ~3-6min a run costs (pulling nomic-embed-text plus indexing and 17 searches). rag-acertivo's severidade STAYS warn — deliberately, now for a cadence reason instead of a technical one, since a scheduled job blocks no merge. What makes this tractable where the QA golden-set (ADR 0123) still isn't: this one only calls the EMBEDDING model (CPU, deterministic, no sampling), never a chat model doing judgment — ubuntu-latest with no GPU is enough. A finding that simplifies the whole job: seed-golden-set-rag.ts never sets NODE_ENV, so the four secrets the api would refuse in production (RN-114) take their dev-literal fallback without complaint — unlike docker/smoke.sh, nothing here needs openssl rand. The Ollama service's health-check runs ollama list, not curl (the image guarantees the former, not the latter), reusing the exact wait pattern docker/ollama/pull-models.sh already validated with a real download. The QA golden-set gets zero changes from this ADR — still entirely manual, still a declared TODO(humano) 0148 Every artifact the agents produce — the Creative's brief, the PO's business rules, the Architect's C4 diagram and module routing, the six conversational agents' decisions — lives EXCLUSIVELY in the event log; emit_artifact.ex says it outright, "there is no artifacts table". That is the right decision for the SOURCE and is not touched here. The problem is that this memory reaches nowhere a person opens: it is readable one line at a time inside the product's session timeline, and whoever opens the project folder in an editor — where the code will be — finds none of the reasoning that produced it. Deferring git (the deferred provisioning (own PR)) widened the hole: between creation and the Architect's handoff the project has no repository at all, so everything the product accumulated sits in database rows while the user's folder is empty. So docs/ becomes a PROJECTION of the event log in the strict sense ADR 0101 gave the graph — the source stays the event, the folder can be deleted whole and rebuilt, and NOTHING in the product reads from it to decide anything; it exists to be opened by a person, and everything else follows from that. The mechanism copies GraphProjector piece by piece (own poller with .unref(), public drainOnce() for tests, draining flag, batch of 50, markProcessed only after success) — not code reuse but DESIGN reuse, since the two write to destinations with nothing in common, and copying the shape is what lets a reader who knows one understand the other without re-reading. Its own aggregate_type (artifact_projection) for the reason the graph's already documents: Engine.Outbox.Drain only drains session/task/container and marks the 'session' row every ~2s, so sharing it would be racing the engine and losing almost always — with one deliberate difference, aggregateId is the PROJECT rather than the session, sparing the projector one query per artifact for something the use case already held. An ALLOW list, not a deny list, so a new artifact type is born outside the projection rather than appearing unannounced in a folder the user reads; qa_verdict, secops_verdict, task_blocked and infra_delegation_files stay out as operational OUTCOMES rather than product documents — one gate verdict per task would fill docs/qa-lead/ with files nobody opens and cost the folder the very property that makes it useful, fitting in one glance. Layout is docs/<agent>/, so browsing answers "what did the Architect produce?" without opening anything; the four VERSIONED types overwrite one file (the folder shows the CURRENT one, history stays whole in the event log — projecting them per version would produce c4-diagram-v1.md, c4-diagram-v2.md and make the reader work out which one counts, exactly what reduction by version exists to spare), while append-only types each get their own file carrying the event's seq, because without it two artifacts of the same type and title would collide and the second would erase the first — the only way this projection could lose information the source has. Two barriers stand between an LLM-written title and the filesystem, and the second is not redundant: slugDeArquivo DERIVES a name from a closed alphabet (no return path lets a separator survive, and empty yields null since a name derived from nothing collides with every other), and FsArtifactFileStore checks again with relative() before opening — the two answer different questions, "what name do I derive" and "what am I about to open", and trusting only the first would make this write's safety depend on no future slug change ever letting a separator through, precisely the containment ADR 0130 refuses on principle. In runner mode the folder diverts to the managed root exactly as permissions.json does and for the same physical reason (the api writes from inside its container, a runner project is deliberately without bind-mount, and the runner channel carries COMMANDS with no primitive for writing file content) — declared cost: there, docs/ does not sit beside the code. And the write does NOT go through proposed_action, which is not an omission: that pipeline is the origin of every external effect of an AGENT ASKING TO ACT, and here no agent asks for anything — the artifact was already emitted and is already in the event log; routing this through approval would fill the queue with one routine decision per artifact and corrode the very ceiling that gives the click its meaning on the actions that really are external effects 0196 The Anamnesis is TURNED BACK ON with fixes (AT-277, owner decision 01/10). A round does not run without an eligible SUBJECT — an EFFECTIVE project member (projectRole ?? workspaceRole, RN-471; project creation writes no project_members row, which is why every round of the 29/09 real use paid the model to conclude "no eligible member"), outside the opt-out, with their OWN interaction in the window: no LLM call, no RAG search, the reason named in the engine log, and anamnese.run_skipped only for the round asked by hand. A Psychologist hypothesis ACCEPTED by the person the session belongs to becomes a PROFILE FACT in the graph — translated from psychologist.hypothesis_accepted by the same GraphEventTranslator, so grafo:reprojetar rebuilds it — and reaches the agents that talk to that person: the api reads it through QueryUserContextUseCase (project-scoped, 5 most recent, total alongside) and the engine appends it as an ephemeral system message on the author's turn, through the same path as the response language. A third party's acceptance and a dismissal stay only recorded. ANAMNESE_ENABLED defaults to true again; the Psychologist stays paused 0200 The contract between modules becomes a versioned ARTIFACT of the Architect, and dev agents read it instead of another module's worktree (AT-276, owner decision 01/10). artifact.module_contracts, no table, the current version replaces the previous one: per module, only what it EXPOSES (funcao/rota/evento/dado + signature, 1–40 items); what it consumes is derived from the current module_map's dependsOn on read. A SEPARATE artifact, never a field of the module_map. The Architect gets declare_module_contracts; dev agents get listar_contratos_de_modulos (no parameter, project-scoped, own module and its dependencies in full, 120-item cap) and their kickoff says to read interfaces there; with no contract, report_blocked naming what is missing 0205 What the Anamnesis sees as an AGENT deviation — a loop, a turn cancelled by the user, a user message repairing an agent failure — becomes a PRODUCT improvement signal (AT-356 part 2, owner decision 02/10): the durable anamnese.agent_deviation event, written by the new report_agent_deviation tool, separate from the user profile and WITHOUT personal data (only agent, closed-vocabulary deviation type and eventId evidence; no free text). Not projected into the user graph; read from the event log, no new screen
documents.s: RAG, knowledge graph and artifacts

documents.t: Screens, navigation, themes and the structure of the web app's largest files. # decision 0036 Auth screens faithful to the approved mock: the design system's three fonts self-hosted (the CSP blocked the CDN and typography fell back to a system font in production), the tag version baked into the artifact, contrast calculated from the tokens instead of measured by axe, and the six deliberate divergences from the mock 0060 The Code tab's code-reading surface, contained and budgeted. 26a put listTree and getPullRequestDiff into the contract and installed the check that fails an operation with no consumer; this ADR is the consumer, and deciding to write it forced resolving three things no prior route had faced, because none received a FILE PATH from the client. Where the search lives: outside the contract. None of the three providers has it — GitHub and GitLab have platform-level code search with their own semantics, and LocalGitProvider is a bare repo —, so declaring it would either be a 13th operation with false capability on local (a tab that vanishes on one provider) or leaking a platform's vocabulary into the normalized contract that exists precisely to prevent that; it stays composed at the application level, over listTree + getFileContent. How much it can spend: three budgets (directories walked, files opened, matches returned) plus a short-TTL cache, because it's the only read whose cost grows with the repository's SIZE and not with the request's, and who pays is the OWNER's credential (RN-058/RN-082) — with no cap it's the same failure family as the dashboard's 3,824 req/min, with 429 turning into a blank screen. Breadth-first scan: cut off midway, it delivers the shallow files, which is where one usually looks. How the path is contained: a single function, in the RN-092 file, reusing the scope primitives from 0055 — and returning the NORMALIZED path, because returning the original would allow checking one string and sending another. The vector isn't reading the wrong file: on a remote provider the path becomes a URL segment of the API and a .. SWITCHES ENDPOINT with the owner's token in hand. CodeQL will keep flagging it, and the price is the one already accepted in the POST-PHASE 15 — duplicating the check would silence the alert and create four copies that one day diverge. The four routes are GET/role:viewer and the controller has NO write verb: reading isn't an external effect and doesn't become a proposed_action (it would flood the queue with noise), and when writing arrives it's born as one — the absence of a verb is what makes this boundary verifiable instead of an intention 0074 Reachable theme, and the boot under CSP. The light theme existed in design/tokens.css, was measured by a parity test and referenced in design/README.md — and nothing in apps/web wrote data-theme: the only way to see it was typing the attribute into DevTools. Both contrast tests knew this and were right while it lasted (one asserted via expect that three light-theme pairs FAIL, "a record of what's inherited, not a guarantee of what's rendered"); with the theme button coming, measuring only the primary theme would start hiding half the visible surface. The boot is a FILE (public/theme-boot.js), not an inline script: the image is served under script-src 'self' (ADR 0058), and inline would work in pnpm dev:web and get blocked in production — 0036's failure with a different subject, since the handoff calls for exactly the inline version. Synchronous and before the bundle, or else a light-theme user would see a dark flash on every load; plain ES5 because vite's public/ doesn't go through a build, locked by a test; localStorage that throws degrades to "paints and doesn't persist", and an unknown value falls back to the default instead of turning into a data-theme the CSS doesn't know. Six light-theme tokens changed value because the theme's most demanding background is paper's --code-bg: --accent 3.56 → 4.81, --warning 3.15 → 4.98, --success 3.89 → 5.12, --violet 4.16 → 4.95, --text-muted 2.76 → 5.17 (at 2.40:1 over --surface-2 it failed even the 3:1 floor — a bug, not debt), and --accent-hover followed one step below. Recorded side effect: the five pairs that are known debt in DARK pass 4.5:1 in light, and the "known design-system exception" (--on-accent over --accent, 3.20:1) vanishes in light because the fix the test comment described — darkening down to --terracota-500 — is what light now does. Dark didn't change a single value. The syntax palette becomes the handoff's EIGHT roles with the --syntax-* prefix, and five of the handoff's eight values were rejected by measurement (--syn-cm 2.32:1 in light, --syn-kw 4.34, --syn-str 4.20, --syn-fn 4.14, --syn-op 4.00): where the handoff fails, the measured number wins, same rule as 0036. --font-display/--shadow-modal and --r-md/--r-lg/--r-pill enter as ALIASES, never renames — and --r-sm (7px) is NOT a synonym for --radius-sm (4px) 0078 Screen frame, and the tab registry deliberately diverges from the handoff. The handoff's "screen frame" checklist (60px header, tab bar with box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 var(--accent), horizontal scroll, content container with a 960–1040px max width) had all four defects in ProjectPage.tsx, and all four were fixed — --header-h became min-height, not height, because the PROJECT header (identity + compact TokenMeter) is richer than the handoff's generic header for the 6 inner screens, and forcing 60px would cut off the budget alert, the same class of mistake RN-088 forbids. The part that needed a decision, not just CSS: the handoff lists 7 tabs and the registry (project-tabs.ts) has 10. executores (RN-121), backlog (RN-048) and insights were born AFTER the handoff, with real data and their own RN, and STAY — the handoff is a reference for VISUAL fidelity, not a ceiling on how many tabs the product has (RN-203). And the sessions key stays labeled "Chat", never "Chat RAG" as the more recent handoff asks (RN-202): "Chat RAG" describes a feature that doesn't exist — no indexing pipeline, no citation UI, just the contract's foundation (embeddings, 0075) —, and renaming the tab today would announce a capability before it existed, the same mistake 0042 already refuses for catalog models. The tab bar spacing values that lived as a descendant CSS override in ProjectPage.module.css — a pending item declared since PHASE 16 — moved into Tabs.module.css, which now owns them. No export SHAPE changed (AbaDoProjeto, ABAS_DO_PROJETO); only code's label went from "Code" to "Código" 0097 The dashboard's "N agents online" (RN-409) reads engine.dev_agent_states DIRECTLY — raw SQL batched per workspace, inside the SAME Promise.all that already sums eleven queries of RN-090's read model —, instead of exposing a new internal HTTP route on the engine. api and engine share the SAME physical database, split only by Postgres schema ("engine" vs public), and there's already precedent for cross-schema reads (apps/api/scripts/medir-execucao.ts already reads engine.oban_peers) — this decision raises the bar from a manual script to TESTED production code, with a minimal, declared fixture of the engine table in test/support/global-setup.ts. Accepted consequence: the query assumes whoever operates the product migrates both sides together (db:migrate AND engine:migrate), and fails loudly/visibly if only the api migrated — no try/catch hiding the error 0116 apps/web's ActionType stops being hand-copied — it is now generated by openapi-typescript from docs/reference/openapi.json (already a drift-checked artifact), reusing that same freshness gate instead of duplicating it. Fixes a copy that already diverged from apps/api/src/domain/actions/decide.ts TWICE in production (the three Gitflow bootstrap types crashing ApprovalCard; later parallelize/raise_max_parallel), both times unnoticed by the compiler because apps/api isn't a dependency of apps/web. Only ActionType migrates — api-types.ts's other ~1600 lines stay hand-written, one type at a time, not a wholesale regeneration. aprovacoes.test.ts (FASE 19) stays: exhaustiveness is now also compiler-checked via Record<ActionType, ...>, but the test's content assertions (sentence quality, not just existence) aren't a type-level property 0122 apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx — 3 807 lines, 169 KiB, 25 test files importing it, under active churn (50 commits, zero prior extraction attempts) — declares the WHOLE 5-PR decomposition upfront so each PR executes it instead of re-deciding it: pure timeline/turn helpers → lib/session-timeline.ts (PR 1), StorySlide (PR 2), StructuredQuestionCard + permiteOutra (PR 3), backlog-tree helpers + ItemDeBacklog + ContextAside (PR 4), a useSessionReadiness hook — the only non-file-move, ordered last (PR 5). SessionPage.module.css has exactly one importer today, so PRs 2–4's new sibling files safely import it directly — no CSS split forced. Explicitly OUT of all five PRs: the turn-channel state cluster (turnoViaCanal/statusAgent/pensandoVisivel/atividadeDoTurno, read and written by four different turn-entry handlers, the in-code comment's "ONE place that ends a turn") and ProjectSettingsTab.tsx (separate scope). Every PR's acceptance bar is the SAME 25 SessionPage.*.test.tsx files passing unedited 0124 The turn-channel state cluster ADR 0122 deferred ("its own, later, separately-numbered ADR") moves into useTurnoDoAgente (apps/web/src/lib/session-turno.ts): streaming/streamingText/streamingAgent/turnoViaCanal/statusAgent/pensandoVisivel/atividadeDoTurno/optimisticUser, the connectSessionHeartbeat channel effect (verified 100% turn-lifecycle machinery), and iniciarTurnoDoAgente/finalizarTurnoDoAgente/cancelarTurnoOtimista. A line-by-line re-read found ADR 0122's own count stale — four turn-entry handlers named, seven real write-entry-points exist, including handleReturnStory/RN-174, never mentioned there — and built on a prior mechanical-dedup PR (not itself ADR'd) that first made three duplicated inline arms call the pre-existing iniciarTurnoDoAgente (which gained { comStatus } there) and introduced cancelarTurnoOtimista. That function is built to cover only two of five differently-shaped reset-on-failure blocks found in the file (handleReadiness/handleArchitectureReadiness's identical 4-field blocks) — NOT handleAcceptHandoff's 2-field block (its kickoff is an async GenServer.cast, so it never armed the other two fields; coupling it to cancelarTurnoOtimista would repeat the exact silent-coupling trap ADR 0122 already named) nor handleSend's two distinct shapes (optimisticUser belongs to handleSend's own lifecycle, not the arm). SessionPage.tsx goes from 2 681 to 2 479 lines; the object-shaped hook return (13 fields, positional destructuring rejected as unreadable) keeps every call site's variable name unchanged. Closes the turn-channel item from ADR 0122's "Explicitly out of scope" section specifically — ProjectSettingsTab.tsx, the other file in that debt row, stays untouched and separately scoped 0125 apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSettingsTab.tsx — 2 532 lines, 89.9 KiB, the LAST open half of the technical-debt row ADR 0122 and ADR 0124 both named and both deliberately deferred — splits into one file per section under apps/web/src/routes/settings/: 17 sections plus a two-symbol settings/shared.ts. ONE PR, not five like 0122's, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of taste: the parent held NOTHING (17 JSX children, no hook, no query, no t, no queryClient, no role check), no section took more than {projectId} (MatrixSection/CredentialsSection take no props at all), and 11 of the 17 were already exported — so every file is a contiguous, byte-identical block, and the churn argument that forced 0122's five-PR shape does not apply. ProjectSettingsTab.tsx STAYS at its path as entry + barrel (2 532 → 77 lines), and that is load-bearing, not cosmetic: ProjectSettingsTab.test.tsx imports 11 names from the path, ProjectPage.test.tsx and project-tabs.test.tsx both vi.mock it BY PATH, and ProficiencySection.test.tsx renders the barrel itself — the only test that mounts all 17 at once. Same barrel shape as ADR 0121, but with the exports NAMED instead of export *: a section is a component with a prop shape, and an explicit list is what lets the compiler catch one that stops matching its call site. Helper placement is mechanical and grep-verified — one caller means the caller's file (ten of twelve), two or more means shared.ts (ORIGIN_TONE, formatarCustoMicros) — which corrected a drive-by expectation: iniciaisDe/gradienteDe belong to MembersSection alone, not ProficiencySection. The 6 private sections gain export on their own module (mechanical; the barrel must import them) but are NOT re-exported by the barrel, so the public surface stays byte-identical in shape — widening it would be an observable change in a PR claiming none. ProjectSettingsTab.module.css stays ONE shared stylesheet, now 15 importers, same answer 0122 gave for SessionPage.module.css. Deliberately preserved: useTranslation('settings') ~14×, useQueryClient() 11×, useToast() 10×, useQuery(['project', projectId]) 7× — React Query dedupes them, and hoisting them into a parent or a context would be a design change disguised as cleanup. Closes the LAST declared open debt item in docs/architecture.md; the four UI improvements that land in these same files are later PRs of the same plan, explicitly out of this one 0126 The project page's two-level horizontal tab strip (components/ui/GroupedTabs.tsx) becomes a VERTICAL RAIL (apps/web/src/routes/ProjectRail.tsx), with all three groups open at once. Only one of the design review's three arguments survived verification and it is the only rationale recorded: 12 tabs in a bar built for ~6 does not scale. The other two were false and are written down so nobody re-litigates them — the second level was an inline row, never an overlay (GroupedTabs.tsx:143), and a closed group DID sum its children's counters (somarContagens, :33, tested at :141). Geometry is borrowed from routes/code/CodeShell.module.css — the only rail in the repo with an active state drawn (--surface-1 band, right divider, 32px item at --radius-sm, active tinted color-mix(… 12%)) — never from the sidebar's .trilha, which has no active item and no keyboard. One declared divergence: 180px wide instead of 48px, because this rail carries labels and group HEADINGS, which is the mechanism that keeps three groups open. The five counters stay SEPARATE and no group sums them; the badge stays solid --accent/--on-accent against the handoff's 18% tint, per the contrast debt of ADR 0074. onKeyDownDaLinha's tested keyboard contract is PORTED, axis swapped (ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End, wrapping) and improved — refs by key instead of positional [role="tab"] DOM queries, which only existed because the Tabs primitive exposes none. GroupedTabs is deleted with its test; Tabs STAYS despite losing its only caller, because ds-bundle/_ds_sync.json publishes it as components/primitivas/Tabs and a DS primitive without a consumer is stock, not dead code. Revises RN-201: the Code tab's auto-collapse (AutoCollapseContext/useAutoCollapseSidebar) is REMOVED, because a permanent project rail beside the Shell's icon rail would be two adjacent vertical rails on the heaviest tab. The accepted price, measured: 492px of chrome before the first character of code (264 sidebar + 180 rail + 48 code rail) against ~110px before. What is bought is that collapsing goes back to being the user's decision — still manual, still persisted; the double rail survives under manual collapse, which is said out loud rather than pretended away 0176 apps/web/src/routes/SessionPage.tsx goes below 1,000 lines in ten stacked, MECHANICAL PRs, and only then gets a CI ceiling (AT-138, BRB-015, maintainer's decision: "yes, and lock it afterwards"). The debt row closed by ADRs 0122/0124 at 2,479 lines closed by a NUMBER that nobody re-measured: on origin/dev at 018b8cd24c the file was 2,637 lines, grown back by legitimate features. The program moves, without editing any of the 28 SessionPage.*.test.tsx files: the fio passes (session-fio.tsx), the 762-line timeline useMemo body (session-timeline-montagem.tsx, called from inside the SAME useMemo with the SAME dependency list, byte for byte), the three JSX strips (SessionTopbar, SessionFio, SessionComposer), the handoff derivations (lib/session-handoffs.ts), the scroll refs and effects (useRolagemDoFio), story promotion (usePromocaoDeHistorias + DevolverHistoriaModal) and the non-turn handoff/execution actions (useAcoesDeHandoff) — 2,637 → 834. The turn-entry handlers stay: they are the door of ADR 0124's cluster. The last PR adds SessionPage.teto.test.ts, failing the file at 1,000 lines or more; raising it takes a new ADR 0181 The dark theme becomes NEUTRAL BLACK with a SOFT terracotta accent, and light becomes the neutral of the same family (AT-283/AT-284). Semantic VALUES change, names don't; a raw --neutro-* scale enters. The final numbers came from MEASUREMENT, not the draft (--text-muted #86868f dark / #696972 light, dark --on-accent becomes neutral black), and the five dark-theme debt pairs 0074 locked by number now pass 4.5:1 and are asserted as FLOORS; the primary-button exception is gone without moving the brand hue. Color outside tokens moves into tokens: one checked copy of fallbacks for Mermaid/xterm/minimap, three agent tokens per theme, --overlay, and a test that fails on any var(--x) nobody declares 0210 Text animation with motion (AT-401): the AI Elements Shimmer, adapted to CSS Modules and tokens (--text-secondary base, --text-primary sweep), lives in components/ui/Shimmer.tsx — the only importer of motion, loaded through LazyMotion + domAnimation in its own vendor-motion chunk (26.5 kB gzip, outside the initial load); reduced motion keeps the text static. 0211 One navigation only (AT-404): the project's vertical rail (ADR 0126, ProjectRail.tsx) is removed and the sidebar's per-project list (AbasDoProjeto) absorbs everything it had — groups, active tab, the five SEPARATE counters (same useContagensDoProjeto hook as the frame, no new request), keyboard, a flyout when collapsed and the drawer on phones. Code tab chrome drops from 492px to 312px (110px collapsed).

documents.t: Production images, Kubernetes, observability, backup, the dev compose and the one-line installer. # decision 0024 Multi-stage, non-root production images, compose.prod, CI with scan and smoke test 0025 Kustomize base+overlays (not Helm), engine HPA by Oban queue depth, local overlay 0026 Graceful shutdown with drain, session registry in :global, OpenTelemetry with per-session trace, metrics and dashboards as code 0027 Tested backup/restore, rate limiting in Postgres (no Redis), classified HTTP surface and versioned release 0035 Instrument and export kept separate (trace with a real trace_id with no collector), the cross-layer path via AsyncLocalStorage + @Traced, readable log in dev and one line of JSON in production, and the three correlation gaps that were dead 0070 Observability in the local Compose: metrics and logs, no trace. 0026 set up Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Alloy, Collector and Grafana only for Kubernetes — the acceptance criterion said "in Grafana local" and "local" there meant the k3d cluster. The practical consequence is that whoever develops with pnpm dev has the whole instrumentation running (the api exposes 102 series, the engine exposes oban_queue_depth, all three stamp trace_id in the log) and NONE of it is observable, because seeing a panel required standing up a cluster that by design doesn't coexist with pnpm dev (same ports, ADR 0025). The docker/docker-compose.observability.yml overlay is opt-in, not part of pnpm dev: that's four more containers on a machine already running Postgres, Ollama and three apps, and whoever isn't investigating shouldn't pay for them. It delivers the two telemetries that DON'T need a collector — metrics is scrape, logs is read from stdout, exactly the split from decision 9 of 0026 — and leaves trace out, with no OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set, because 0035 already established that not exporting is the normal state in development and pointing at a nonexistent address only produces an export error on every turn. The artifacts are the SAME ones from the cluster, not a copy: the Compose mounts deploy/k8s/observability/dashboards/ directly and the datasource UIDs are identical, because a dashboard references a datasource by UID and a dashboard copy diverges the first time one side gets a panel fixed; for the same reason the scrape emits the app/pod labels the panels group by, and the collector emits the app the cluster's Alloy derives from app.kubernetes.io/name. Log parsing is by regex and not stage.json because in dev pino-pretty draws the readable tree and the engine uses PrettyLogFormatter — a good decision that doesn't get swapped to please the collector; the collector adapts instead. Only api, engine and web go to Loki: Postgres and Ollama are noise, and the observability stack itself is left out because it runs in the SAME Compose project and would ingest its own log in a loop that feeds itself. trace_id is STRUCTURED metadata and never a label (cardinality), which required allow_structured_metadata and schema v13 in Loki's own config. Records three modes of silent failure that cost time, all with the same signature — valid config, zero error in the log, wrong data on the panel: stage.replace substitutes CAPTURE GROUPS and with no parenthesis substitutes nothing; escaping \x1b in a River string is processed before the regex compiles, and [[:cntrl:]] doesn't depend on that layer; and a Go template with a missing key renders the literal <NO VALUE>, which turned into a level value in the selector 0150 The one-line installer, and the three disk facts that shape it. docker-compose.prod.yml is not an installation manifest: every service points at brabo-*:prod with a local build: block, there is not one ghcr.io reference under docker/, and the file says of itself that it is the "VALIDATION compose" and "what this file is NOT: a hardened production manifest". The only consumer of .release/images.json is the kustomize overlay. Decision: invocation is sh -c "$(curl -fsSL …)" and **never `curl 0152 Backup and restore that run against compose — born because FASE 29 must migrate an existing installation and the documented path does not serve: make test-restore is a Kubernetes path (needs kubectl, a cluster and the brabo-backup CronJob), docker-compose.prod.yml has no backup service, and backup.sh covers only Postgres while demanding five S3 variables. The decision starts by REFUSING the easy move ("back up every volume") and classifying the seven instead: pgdata and git_local_repos are source of truth; neo4j_data and project_workspaces are derived; ollama_data is re-obtainable; brabo_projects_base belongs to the user. git_local_repos is the real hole and the finding of this ADR — a local-provider project keeps its bare repo there, losing that volume loses the code the agents produced, no backup covers it today, and it is NOT reconstructible from Postgres: the event log holds the narrative, not the git objects. Neo4j gets reprojection, not backup — restoring a possibly-stale projection beside a Postgres restored at another instant yields two derived states from different moments with nothing reconciling them; this phase declares the path and accepts that a migrated install starts with an EMPTY graph, which is known degradation (the RAG lives in pgvector, inside the dump), not data loss. Disk becomes a valid destination so migrating does not require a bucket. The compose restore reuses the SAME three validations of restore.sh:139-224 — the wrapper changes, the judgement does not — and deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh stays untouched. The installer only earns the right to delete volumes because it proved it can bring them back 0153 DEPLOY_ENABLED is cited as the activation trigger by ten documents — ADRs 0089/0091/0092 in their own Status field, fluxo.yml in three places (platform.ativacao, area-infra.gate_saida, and the TWO gap deliverables of secops-runtime), gates.yml on the operavel gate, plus business-rules.md, backlog.md, modelo-de-time.md, auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md, historico-de-fases.md and CLAUDE.md — and it exists nowhere in the code: the only two occurrences are COMMENTS (external-effect.ts:144, listar_metricas_de_produto.ex:185). Ten documents point at a switch with no wall behind it. A finding that is not about deploy at all: the deployavel gate is declared as area-infra’s gate_saida in fluxo.yml:247 and is absent from the registry gates.yml, which is exactly the inconsistency the (still backlogged) cross-check between the team model’s three pieces would catch — the second such finding. Decision splits in two with a hard boundary: Stage A, decidable today, adds deployavel to the registry as planned/warn (RN-070/071 forbid promoting to block without a verification script), leaves the two anticipated scripts untouched, and stops the prose from treating DEPLOY_ENABLED as a variable, naming instead the MILESTONE it always meant; Stage B is blocked by an operator, not by code — a production environment with real traffic, after which platform leaves planned and the gaps become possible. The infrastructure is NOT the bottleneck (overlays, GHCR images by digest since 0119, smoke/rollout/restore scripts all exist) — what is missing is someone running and maintaining it. The alternative CONSIDERED AND REFUSED was creating the variable now with a false default: a variable no code reads is the same empty promise this ADR denounces, now with a config line propping it up; the flag is born in the PR that has the first real consumer. Refuses explicitly: creating a platform/secops-runtime agent in the engine (repeating 0091/0092’s refusal, which still holds), and marking MTTR/change failure rate as permanently unmeasurable when they only depend on an environment 0155 The installer creates the first account, in the terminal, and brings the local agent up already paired. The finding that forces it: a fresh one-line install lets nobody in. The generated .env carries no mail variable at all, MAIL_TRANSPORT falls to log (docker-compose.install.yml:200, whose own comment says the behaviour "stays log-only even here"), and registration requires verifying an e-mail — which, as provisionar-usuario.ts's docblock already recorded, "with the log-only MailSender does not close by itself". So the installation ends saying "Pronto" and the only way forward is fishing a verification link out of docker compose logs api. provisionarUsuario exists for exactly this hole — it creates a user with the password ALREADY verified — and its two callers are the demo seed and the smoke, neither of them a real installation. Decision: the step runs only when there is no user at all, through an internal route authenticated by the BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN the installer just generated and wrote at mode 600; no public "create first owner" route is born, because a public route that creates an owner is a race between whoever installed and whoever scanned the port. The account is born verified, and the reason is what authorizes it: what e-mail verification proves is "this person controls this mailbox", while whoever is running the installer has already proved something stronger — they control the MACHINE, the .env with all five secrets, and the Docker daemon. Demanding the weaker proof, over a channel the installation knows is switched off, is theatre — and the installer SAYS so in its output rather than letting the person discover their account differs from everyone else's. Consent is explicit and without a TTY the step does not happen (RN-511's rule, consentir-base.mjs's shape): no path exists where an account is born with a password the script chose, neither generated nor default. The password is read without echo, confirmed, used and discarded — never in the .env, never in the marker, never in a log; the marker gains the owner's e-mail, which is identification, not a secret. With the account made, a machine device key is registered and the per-machine unit installed; the pair is generated ON the machine and the private half never travels, keeping true the sentence RN-519 used to refuse the maintainer view. The agent then comes up with NO project, and that is the normal state — it waits, emits no failure, and status says "up, no project in runner mode", one of the four states RN-518 already distinguishes rather than a fifth. Refuses: creating an account when one exists, a public first-owner route, a script-chosen password, loosening the normal registration, turning SMTP on by itself, and asking for an LLM credential 0160 The installer's compose travels with it, as a signed Release asset. The first clean-machine run of the installer (RN-549) found that the published install.sh brought nothing up by itself: it ran docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.install.yml, a path relative to wherever it ran, and that file was not a Release asset, was not in the signed checksums.txt, and was downloaded nowhere — so whoever followed the runbook's one-liner died with "no such file or directory" after the .env with five secrets was already written. Decided by the maintainer: four files become assets in the same signed manifest — the compose, the two files it bind-mounts (postgres/init.sql, ollama/pull-models.sh) and, measured while implementing, the backup/test-restore-compose.sh the migration path executes, which the E2E's manual workaround never carried because a clean machine has nothing to migrate. Names carry a brabo-install- prefix because a Release is flat and generic names would collide. The table lives on two sides — scripts/ci/assets-do-instalador.ts for whoever publishes, a case in install.sh for whoever downloads (bash 3.2, no Node) — and a spec fails when they diverge and derives every relative bind-mount from the compose, which is exactly how the defect was born. The checksums job publishes them from the tag's checkout and now runs sha256sum -c --strict on the manifest before attaching. The installer downloads and verifies the four right after verifying itself, against the SAME manifest, by exact name match, with three distinct named refusals, all on an untouched machine; COMPOSE_DE_INSTALACAO is born empty and only becomes an absolute path when the verified copies are placed under the install folder, replacing — never reading — whatever was there. The E2E drops its manual step and asserts its absence. Refuses: cloning the repository at the tag (trades the signature chain for trust in git transport, plus a dependency a clean machine may lack), a tarball (one manifest line covering four unnamed files), embedding them in install.sh, a flag pointing at another Release URL, and running the E2E on pull requests. Declared: proven end to end only at the next final tag; no already-published Release gains the assets; and, measured and not fixed, test-restore-compose.sh calls Compose without --env-file, so the migration's restore proof tends to fail safely 0161 The screens only offer the execution mode this installation can run, and an installation from a Release has no container broker. A real v6.1.0 install (AT-085) created a project in mounted — PRE-selected, because install.sh always writes BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE and RN-513 pre-selects that mode when the base is known — and got six dev.blocked_by_container plus two container.start_failed: container and mounted only start a container through the broker (ADR 0144), the installation compose has no broker service at all (not a disabled profile — ADR 0150 decision 7), and without a running container no dev agent works (ADR 0143). The maintainer decided "both": the installer asks whether to enable the broker, and the screens stop offering what does not run. The installer half was measured and stopped: the broker image is not obtainable by a Release install — four bake targets, no broker in images-manifest.ts or in the v6.1.0 images.json, docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/daneiel/brabo-broker:6.1.0 answers denied while the same anonymous call for brabo-api resolves, and the one-liner runs in a folder with no source to build from. A question whose "yes" has no image is worse than none; publishing the broker as a fifth image comes first, as its own front. The screen half ships: brokerConfigurado (from ContainerBrokerPort.configurado(), the same source the observed-state read uses) joins GET .../projects-base and every row of GET .../containers — no new route. The wizard has three states that never collapse: confirmed broker keeps RN-513; confirmed absence keeps Container and Mounted on screen but inert, says why once in text, and pre-selects Runner; unknown neither pre-selects Mounted nor locks anything. /containers gains a fourth local refusal, sem_broker_na_instalacao, for container/mounted, before the image check. RN-512 and the five containment layers are untouched. Out of scope, declared: mode conversion, stop/remove, the Infra Lead not knowing about a missing broker, and the parallelization suggestion that ignores blocked agents 0162 The container broker becomes the fifth published image, and the installer asks whether to turn it on. The installer half of ADR 0161's "both": in a Release installation container and mounted projects never ran, because the broker brings their containers up (ADR 0144) and the installation had no broker service — measured, ghcr.io/daneiel/brabo-broker answered denied, the bake had four targets. The Dockerfile.prod already existed and passed hadolint; nothing built it. Now the broker bake target goes through every gate the other four do — built, Trivy-scanned and refused as root on every PR, proven healthy read-only with no network, published, recorded in images.json, signed and verified by digest on every tag. The installation compose gains the service off, under the container-broker profile, with ADR 0130's five layers intact; the Kubernetes overlay does not know it. The installer asks after the base, says in text that turning it on hands the machine's Docker socket to the service, turns it on only on a typed "s", measures the socket's gid from inside a container (a named refusal otherwise, never a guessed 999), writes COMPOSE_PROFILES/BROKER_URL/DOCKER_GID/the managed root together, and checks after startup that the api reaches the broker and that the computed root is the volume's. RN-512's argument (whoever installs on their own machine already holds the socket) is why it can be offered; the installer's reader never having opened this repository is why it is asked, not assumed. Price, declared: a root-equivalent image is public, and a user installation mounts the Docker socket when it consents 0169 The local overlay's S3 backup destination stops being MinIO and becomes SeaweedFS (docker.io/chrislusf/seaweedfs 4.47, pinned by INDEX digest, server -s3 -s3.port=9000). MinIO stopped publishing its community image — the pinned digest answers 401 on quay.io and the Docker Hub repository 404 — so the bootstrap died at rollout status and no property proof ran (issue #633). Measured against the maintainer's criteria in order: SeaweedFS passes all four (official, anonymous, amd64+arm64 index; the real lib.sh flow through aws-cli — auth, mb, 30 MiB multipart stdin upload, head-object, download by sha256, server-side copy, list-objects-v2, rm; only the server changes; Apache-2.0); Garage is discarded on the third (config file plus post-boot layout and key import); Bitnami, its frozen legacy mirror and Chainguard's :latest-only MinIO on the first. Resources get a neutral name (s3-local); the client, the backup scripts, the Secret and the port are unchanged. Declared: a digest guarantees immutability, not availability; S3 compatibility is per operation, so a new operation in lib.sh is measured against it first 0170 The dev compose becomes the Docker project brabo-dev, and dev refuses to come up next to an installation. Measured on 2026-09-19: the dev compose and the installation compose were both name: brabo — ONE Docker project on a machine with both, sharing containers, network and volumes (brabo_pgdata…); an installation's database received a dev migration, and reset-total.sh would have dropped its schemas. The installation stays brabo (renaming it would unbind every existing installation from its volumes); dev renames, and the observability overlay repeats the name because the last -f wins. preflight.mjs and reset-total.sh REFUSE, naming the containers and the down (without -v) of each file, while any container whose config_files label points at the installation compose exists (in any state, under any -p), or while the dev compose would resolve to brabo; the reset's guard runs before anything else. Old brabo_* dev volumes are only WARNED about — dev-only keys derived from the two compose files prove them, shared keys stay ambiguous and the warning says so — and the runbook carries the copy-or-start-over procedure. Price declared: developing on a machine with an installation requires bringing the installation down first 0209 The engine moves to Elixir 1.20.4 / OTP 29.1.1 on Alpine 3.24.2 in dev, production and CI (AT-398): OTP 27 aborted at boot with sys_sigaltstack(): Internal error under Alpine 3.24's musl 1.2.6 on hosts with AMX (erlang/otp#11349), fixed only from OTP 29.1; the price is rebuilding the dev _build/deps volumes.

documents.t: The pipeline, the published images, signing, scanning, pinning, the test layers and the repository's own structure. # decision 0039 actionlint pinned in the engine's Dockerfile (same pattern as gitleaks/hadolint), CI pipeline validation at GENERATION time instead of a new post-PR gate, and the documented gap of .gitlab-ci.yml having no equivalent offline static linter 0119 release.yml stops building the four production images just to prove the tag is buildable and PUBLISHES them to GHCR on every final tag, public, logging in with the job's own GITHUB_TOKEN (packages: write) — no new secret. The registry prefix and the build output become bake variables (REGISTRY/OUTPUT), both empty-by-default so ci.yml keeps building the short local names it scans; type=registry is not an optimization, it is the only mode in which bake returns containerimage.digest, because the digest is born from the push. What each tag published is recorded BY DIGEST in .release/images.json — an asset of the Release, riding the CHANGELOG PR into the repository, with NO third push exception. The overlay keeps REPLACE_WITH_DIGEST as a marker and make imagens-do-release applies the digest with kustomize edit set image; the repository never declares which release is in production. Found while doing it: the overlays listed three images, not four — the backup CronJob inherited brabo-backup:prod, a name that resolves in no registry 0120 A browser E2E layer (e2e/, Playwright, chromium only) closes the one hole left at the top of the pyramid: nothing exercised a real browser, and the mechanisms that carry the session are browser mechanisms — httpOnly refresh cookie paired with a readable brabo_csrf, cross-origin calls from :8088 to :3000 (preflight, SameSite, credentials: 'include'), and the single-use socket ticket of RN-108 handshaking against the engine on a THIRD origin. jsdom can enforce none of those, so a test asserting them there would pass while proving nothing (main.ts already says it: "teste não faz preflight"). It runs against the PRODUCTION compose that docker/smoke.sh already brings up (SMOKE_KEEP_UP=1) and in the SAME images job, because the four images are most of that job's wall clock and a separate job would rebuild them to reach the identical stack. e2e/ is NOT a workspace member — own pnpm-workspace.yaml and lockfile, same shape as website/ (ADR 0117), for the same reason: Playwright's tree reaches no image and has no business in the product's pnpm audit. Specs assert MECHANISM (the httpOnly flag as the browser reports it, document.cookie as the page sees it, survival across a reload, ticket= in the WebSocket URL) with structural selectors, never text — the interface language is the server's decision. Seeding goes over HTTP, mirroring the smoke. Declared as not covered: cross-browser differences, inline approval and streaming 0121 apps/api/src/db/schema.ts — 2 452 lines, 51 tables, 34 enums, the repo's most-changed file — splits into one file per DOMAIN AGGREGATE under db/schema/, mirroring src/domain/* instead of inventing a taxonomy the file was already keeping by hand in // --- section --- comments. The old path becomes a 25-line barrel of export *, so all 144 modules importing …/db/schema change nothing, drizzle-client.ts's import * as schema sees the identical export set, and drizzle.config.ts keeps pointing at it (verified: drizzle-kit follows the export * chain and reports "No schema changes, nothing to migrate"). Purely mechanical — no table, column, enum value, index name or constraint expression changed, and the acceptance bar is the ZERO-diff migration, stricter than the suite because Drizzle diffs the inferred SQL. Enums live with the table that calls them, not with their subject: a cross-file FK is safe under a cycle (.references() is a lazy callback), a cross-file ENUM is not (it runs at module evaluation), so project_execution_mode/story_promotion sit in iam.ts with their only consumer and failure_origin in backlog.ts, keeping the import graph a DAG. backup.ts is the one file with no domain/ counterpart — infra with no business rule, and a wrong boundary would cost more than a small file. docs/.docmap.yml grows schema/** alongside the barrel: without it the rule would go blind to constraints, which is what it exists to watch 0140 On 2026-09-04 the npm advisories endpoint (POST .../security/advisories/bulk) went intermittent for hours and failed the dependency-audit job on FOUR separate PRs with an identical signature (error (503) then TimeoutError) — reproduced outside CI from another machine, where a plain registry GET answered in 130ms and the bulk POST never answered at all. The cost was not the wasted minutes but the habit it teaches: every such red is cleared by re-running until green, and someone who learns that re-runs through a real red too. Product owner's decision: three attempts with no answer from the registry is an ACCEPTED RISK — the job goes green with a loud warning that says the tree was NOT audited, never that it is clean. What the decision does not loosen is what makes it defensible: a reported vulnerability still fails on the FIRST attempt with no retry, and an unrecognized failure fails too (fail closed). The precedence is the heart of it — classificarAudit tests the FINDING signatures before the network ones, so a report that happens to mention timeout (a package by that name, a timeout CVE) is never forgiven as downtime, and there is a test for exactly that. Logic lives in a testable script (11 cases, using the REAL output of run 33838507158 rather than paraphrases), not in YAML bash. Only the pnpm side changes; mix hex.audit/mix deps.audit stay as they were, since widening the exception to who did not ask for it would turn a pointed decision into general policy. Declared and unresolved: nothing alerts when the risk is assumed repeatedly — three timeouts on one PR is third-party noise, three on every PR for a week is the gate switched off in practice, and today nothing tells the two apart 0149 The product signs nothing it publishes: searching .github/, scripts/, docker/ and Makefile for cosign, sigstore, slsa and attestation returns one real hit, and it covers neither image nor binary (npm publish --provenance for the npm package, publish-runner.yml:188). release.yml builds and pushes the four images (:286-303) and records their digests in .release/images.json (:308-319) while declaring only three permissions (:40-43) — no id-token: write, which keyless signing requires. build-runner-binaries.yml uploads five binaries with gh release upload (:227) and no checksums.txt — while the sha256sum -c calls that DO exist (ci.yml:201, Dockerfile.prod:95) verify third-party binaries, the very pattern the repo knows and never applied to itself. And GET /runner-releases/binary is @Public() and streams GitHub bytes straight through with no integrity check at all. That is BRB-005, and it is what blocked the one-line installer in FASE 28. Decision: cosign keyless (Actions OIDC) signing the four images by digest — never by tag, a moving pointer — plus ONE signed checksums.txt covering the five binaries rather than five separate signatures (five artifacts to verify is five ways for verification to be half-done). Three named consumers, each with a refusal, never a warning: the installer, the download proxy, and the local build. Keyless and not a managed key pair for the reason the repo already learned the hard way — a private key means custody, rotation and one MORE CI secret, and a PAT expiring unnoticed already failed two tag-release runs (0139). The cosign binary that verifies is itself pinned and checked with sha256sum -c against a hash written in the versioned script. Refuses: managed keys, "sign now verify later", signing by tag, and full SLSA/SBOM attestation as a separate axis. Declares that the broker stays unsigned because it stays unpublished — the bake has four targets. Amended in session 3, which split the download proxy's row in two: it verifies integrity (sha256 against the release's checksums.txt, refusing — never warning — when the manifest is absent) and not provenance, because both ways for the api to check the signature were measured and refused — cosign in the image is 155 MB against an Alpine+Node runtime, and @sigstore/verify is cheap (2.5 MB) but would make a @Public() route depend on a second third-party host to verify what no Release carries yet, which ADRs 0041/0042 forbid declaring unproven. So BRB-005 closes for producing signatures and stays open for that half of the proxy (RN-525) 0159 Third-party images are pinned by digest, with the tag in a trailing comment, and a lint fails the next regression. This revokes a decision this repository had written down: the supply-chain page called tag pinning "a deliberate stop, not an oversight", buying day-to-day reproducibility "without the maintenance cost of digests on images we don't publish". Both halves of that sentence fall to measurement. There are 37 third-party references, and three of the places they run are not the day to day: thirteen are Dockerfile FROM lines, which are the base of the four images we publish to GHCR and sign with cosign (RN-524); four are in docker-compose.install.yml, which runs beside the Postgres of whoever installed the product, in the same file where the four own images already arrive by digest through a variable; and four are services: in ci.yml/golden-set-rag.yml, which is literally the runner the action rule exists to protect, reached by the other door — none of the three was in BRB-004's own evidence. The maintenance cost is real and is the SAME one already accepted for the action SHAs. The check is a sibling of actions-pinadas.ts, not an extension: uses: is one syntax in workflow YAML, images are three others across composes, kustomize manifests and Dockerfiles, and one function answering both questions answers both badly. It fails on a mutable reference, on a digest with no tag comment, and on the same tag carrying two different digests — that third one turns a promise written in a comment (golden-set-rag.yml claiming to run the "MESMA versão pinada" as the dev compose, because the golden-set floor is keyed by model, not environment) into something verifiable. The digest is the index digest, never a platform's: pinning linux/amd64 would break linux-arm64 with no warning. In a Dockerfile the tag comment goes on the line above, and that was learned by getting it wrong: Docker's parser only takes # at the start of a line, so a trailing one is a FROM with three arguments and the build dies — while hadolint passed the same file, because a linter agreeing is not the build agreeing. The check recognizes the trailing form only in order to refuse it, since a pattern that simply failed to match would make the reference vanish from the sweep instead of turning red — trading an error for silence, which is the defect it exists to prevent. The comment is one token in both shapes, which is what separates a tag from the prose already sitting above nearly every FROM. The check deliberately does not cover the four images the product publishes, for three independent reasons — no third party can move them; brabo-api:prod is a local tag whose digest does not exist before the build and changes with every build; and where they do cross a registry, ADR 0119 already resolves them by digest, with the overlay deliberately holding the MARKER rather than a frozen release, so demanding a literal there would fail the correct state. Same for interpolated references and multi-stage stages. The exception list is by name and fails closed. The observability compose was an open TODO(humano) and goes in: excluding it costs a named exemption inside docker/, which is the exact shape of hole the sibling's docblock diagnoses ("a new workflow is written by copying a neighbour, and the neighbour had a tag"). Declared and not fixed: a digest receives no security update until someone bumps it by hand — the action-SHA debt again — and Dependabot's docker ecosystem is not enabled, a separate decision; the dev bases (node:24-alpine) freeze harder than the production ones, which is the least comfortable consequence and is accepted; and otel-collector-values.yaml, where image: opens a map whose tag the chart chooses, stays uncovered. No RN is born: the sibling rule has none either, and both live in CLAUDE.md and the supply-chain page. BRB-004 stops reproducing 0172 The release runs Trivy on what it PUBLISHES, by digest and before signing (AT-179): until then only ci.yml scanned, and it scans a LOCAL PR build, while a tag builds cold in another run (AT-110) — the image the installer downloads was the one nobody scanned. The gate sits between recording .release/images.json and cosign sign, so a failing image is never signed; it uses the ci.yml flags byte for byte (--severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed --exit-code 1, the same .trivyignore.yaml, no new allowlist) and Trivy's exit code is the verdict. HIGH/CRITICAL with no fix is REPORTED — job summary and a trivy-sem-correcao.md Release asset built by scripts/ci/trivy-do-release.ts — and does not block. Declared price: the push already happened, so a failed tag leaves unsigned images in the GHCR with no Release; and version, hash and flags live in two workflows, guarded by a spec. Measured against v6.1.0's digests: api and web would fail today on CVE-2026-45447 (openssl, fixed in 3.3.7-r1). 0178 A third-party image reference becomes image:tag@sha256:<index> — the tag moves from a comment INTO the reference, before the digest (AT-139, over ADR 0159; the maintainer's decision called it "ADR 0171", a number that was never written and stays vacant). Measured on 2026-09-27: Dependabot reads no tag comment in any format and moves a digest-only pin to the digest of latest, which would have taken pgvector, neo4j and node to another major with the comment still lying and the lint green. The 39 references migrate with the SAME digests (29 in docker/, 4 in deploy/k8s/, 6 in workflows), comments dropped; imagens-pinadas.ts derives the tag from the reference and fails a digest with no inline tag (the ADR 0159 shape included), a tag comment that disagrees, a comment at the end of a FROM and the same inline tag with two digests — each rule proved by mutation. NOT done, and declared: enabling Dependabot docker/docker-compose, because the decided step that aligns the workflows' services: on the bot's PR would have to push to .github/workflows/, which the GITHUB_TOKEN can never do — the way out is the maintainer's. The CNPG imageName and the golden-set QA image stay manual either way 0197 The workflows' services: read their image from the dev compose, and Dependabot's docker/docker-compose ecosystems are switched on (AT-246, owner decision 01/10, over ADR 0159 and ADR 0178). The six literals (pgvector and ollama in ci.yml and the two golden-sets) give way to ${{ needs.imagens.outputs.<image> }} from a reusable imagens-do-compose.yml that runs scripts/ci/imagens-do-compose.ts — one source of digest, so the bot's PR never touches .github/workflows/, and golden-set-rag.yml's "same Ollama as dev" goes from promise to construction. imagens-pinadas.ts now fails, in a workflow, any image literal, any expression other than exactly that one (a literal, `
documents.s: CI, release and supply chain

documents.t: How documentation is generated, verified and published. # decision 0029 Continuous documentation synchronization: generate > verify > remember, responsibility map validated in CI, and a mandatory escape hatch 0033 The API reference comes out of the code: response DTOs that mirror the entity by type, a table test covering the summary and the real response (the one synthesized by Swagger doesn't count), and a hash manifest instead of regenerating on --check 0034 Documentation published by stage in a Pages subdirectory: baseUrl by variable, noIndex outside of main with forceIgnoreNoIndex in local search, and the third exception to direct pushes 0071 Symmetric publishing per stage, and a root that chooses. 0034 had each permanent branch publish its own documentation, but left the ADDRESS asymmetric: main at the root, qa and dev in a subdirectory. The asymmetry charged three prices — the three sites couldn't see each other (whoever landed on /brabo/ had no way to reach qa), the root's special case forced a workflow step that only ran for a third of the publishes, and there was nowhere to declare maturity. The three now go to /brabo/<branch>/, and the root becomes a generated INDEX, not a redirect: redirecting would be simpler and would swallow the question that leads someone to look at more than one stage ("does qa already have what I need?"). The page offers what EXISTS in the tree, never a fixed list, and shows the stamped version read from the tags. A 404.html at the root catches every old deep link (/brabo/architecture → /brabo/main/architecture), with a loop guard for a 404 that happens INSIDE a stage. The tree is assembled for all three (not keep_files: true, which never removes an orphan), which brings the migration for free: the trash main left at the root isn't in the assembled tree and goes away on the first push. And the transition seeds /main/ from the old root — without it, dev's first push would leave /brabo/main/ nonexistent right while 404.html redirects there 0073 The published path names the ENVIRONMENT, not the branch. Revises 0071: it put the three stages at /brabo/<branch>/ by interpolating $GITHUB_REF_NAME, and with that the stable documentation ended up at /brabo/main/ — main is a committer's word, and a reader is choosing maturity, not branch. main now publishes at /brabo/prd/; qa and dev coincide by accident, not by rule. The branch→path map now EXISTS in one place per process (the workflow step, the docusaurus.config.ts DEGRAUS table and the one in landing.mjs, the latter separating the tree's directory from the branch the version TAG comes from). E_PRODUCAO stays DOCS_BRANCH === 'main' — item 4 of 0071 exists precisely for the day the path changes, and this is that day. Two traps handled: /brabo/main/ is published and vanishes with keep_files: false, so 404.html REWRITES the prefix (its own case, not the generic redirect, which would produce /brabo/prd/main/…) and the anti-loop guard now only covers existing paths; and the transition seeds /prd/ from gh-pages:main, otherwise /brabo/prd/ would return 404 for days between dev's first push and the next promotion 0117 website/ leaves the root pnpm-workspace.yaml and gets its own pnpm-lock.yaml, so pnpm audit at the root stops reporting Docusaurus's dependency tree, which never ships. Auditing all 13 root security overrides with pnpm why <pkg> -r (not by re-reading their comments) found most attributed to website/ alone are actually MIXED — mermaid/dompurify/uuid also resolve through apps/web's own runtime mermaid (ADR 0068), postcss/nanoid through apps/web's vite, js-yaml/fast-uri/lodash through apps/api's eslint/ajv/@nestjs/swagger chains — so those stay at the root AND get duplicated into a new website/package.json pnpm.overrides block; only serialize-javascript and the yaml@1.x range were truly website-exclusive and moved out entirely; esbuild stayed root-only, absent from website/'s tree. pnpm --filter website (root-only, requires workspace membership) becomes pnpm --dir website in every docs:* script and in docs-deploy.yml/docs-check.yml, which each gain a second, separate pnpm install step scoped to website/ 0202 The ADR index is grouped by THEME, with the theme OUTSIDE the ADR (AT-137, owner decision 01/10, finding BRB-026): docs/adr/temas.yml holds the closed list of 15 themes and one main theme per ADR, so no accepted ADR is edited, not even to gain frontmatter. The index is CHECKED, not generated — its one-line descriptions stay curated — and docs:check (scripts/docs/temas-de-adr.mjs, each rule proved by mutation) fails an ADR without a theme, a theme not in the list, a theme with no ADR, and an index row under the wrong section, outside any section or out of numeric order. The taxonomy comes from the product's fronts, not from the phases or the code folders, and is the lane's proposal for the owner to review; a new ADR's author picks its theme in the same PR, and going past 15 themes takes an ADR 0206 The API reference becomes ONE server-rendered Redoc page (redocusaurus) at /reference/api/, revising the publishing half of 0033: the OpenAPI plugin and theme dragged postman-collection → @faker-js/faker@5.5.3 (High alert #43) with no fixable path. The per-operation pages, tag sidebar, per-operation URLs, playground and cURL snippets go away by owner decision; api-render-check.mjs now asserts the title and one SSR section per operation 0216 Four languages for docs and UI — pt-BR becomes the SOURCE and default, with English, Russian and Simplified Chinese as translations in phases, measured parity and a per-page notice for untranslated or stale pages (AT-545, owner decisions 15/10)
documents.s: Documentation

documents.t: One file per decision, at docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md, with sequential 4-digit numbering. No number reuse, not even when an ADR is superseded — the next one is 0218. One theme per decision, chosen by whoever writes the ADR, in the same PR: a line in docs/adr/temas.yml and the index row under that theme's section, in numeric order. The reviewer confirms it. A new theme is a change to the list in temas.yml, justified in the PR that adds it; going past 15 takes an ADR that revises 0202. Three sections, only those: Context (the problem or force that motivated it), Decision (what was decided), Consequences (the accepted trade-offs and what's left for later). No third-party template — no Nygard, MADR or variants. The three sections are enough. In Portuguese, like the rest of the project. An accepted ADR is not edited. One superseded by a later decision stays as it is; the new ADR references the old one and explains what changed. What gives these ADRs their value is recording what did not work: 0020 documents nine failed executions in a row, and 0027 records a justification that was revised within the same session that produced it. An omitted bad consequence is the part that's missed six months later.
documents.s: The convention

documents.t: Phase 2 (CLAUDE.md) calls for a normalized GitProvider interface in packages/shared covering 8 operations (createRepo, getRepo, createBranch, protectBranch, commitFiles, listBranches, openPullRequest, mergePullRequest), with types that never leak the shape of Octokit (GitHub) or the GitLab REST client (@gitbeaker), plus a capabilities object through which the domain degrades when an operation isn't supported by a provider. Before this session, apps/api already had a GitProvider — but as an abstract class used as a NestJS dependency-injection token, with a single operation (createRepository), consumed by the repository provisioning pipeline already in production (ProvisionRepositoryUseCase, GitProviderRegistry, GitInfrastructureModule). This session is scoped only to the "foundation" (types + contract suite + complete LocalGitProvider) — finishing GithubProvider/GitlabProvider for the 8 operations is left for a future session.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Two contracts deliberately coexist for now: GitProvider (unchanged, apps/api/src/application/ports/git-provider.port.ts) — remains the Nest DI token, with createRepository. Nothing in it changes this session; GithubProvider/GitlabProvider/the registry/ the provisioning use case are not touched. GitProviderContract (new, packages/shared/src/index.ts) — the normalized interface with 8 operations + capabilities, types GitRepo/GitBranch/GitPullRequest/GitCommitResult. Not wired to any DI token yet. Only LocalGitProvider implements it for now (in addition to continuing to implement the old, unchanged GitProvider). Named GitProviderContract instead of reusing the GitProvider identifier — this avoids a name collision in the file that implements both (LocalGitProvider) and matches the "contract suite" vocabulary that CLAUDE.md itself already uses to describe the tests.
