ProjectSettingsTab.tsx — the other file named in the same technical-debt row as SessionPage.tsx — is unaffected by this ADR and remains a fully separate, still-open scope decision with no date; nothing here changes its status. The nine tests named as regression coverage for this cluster (SessionPage.pista-e-status, .cancelar-turno, .turno-preso, .readiness-turno-preso, .handoff-devlead-e-colapso, .ideacao-automatica, .arquiteto-modelo-icone, .agente-mais-recente, .promocao-inline-e-volta — the last one is the only file covering handleReturnStory/RN-174, which ADR 0122 never named) all pass unedited, alongside the full SessionPage.*.test.tsx suite, proving the move changed no observable behavior. The five-shapes finding above (Decision, "why cancelarTurnoOtimista covers only two of five") is now written down once, here, instead of living only in code comments — a future change to any of the five reset blocks has this ADR as the reference for why they are not the same function today.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: A sixth function covering handleAcceptHandoff's 2-field reset (block #5 above), so every handler would call a named function instead of two raw operations. Rejected: it would have exactly one caller, and the two lines it would wrap (turnoAgentRef.current = null; setTurnoViaCanal(false);) already say what they do without an intermediary name to look up. Widening cancelarTurnoOtimista to also reset atividadeDoTurno, on the theory that a failed turn should always clear the activity strip. Rejected: none of the three await-dependent failure paths (handleReadiness, handleArchitectureReadiness, handleSend's agent branch) reset atividadeDoTurno today, even though the call can take up to 120s and channel deltas/tool-calls may have already fed the reducer in the meantime. That is an accepted gap in the code as it stood before this ADR, not something this extraction was asked to fix — adding a new dispatchAtividade({ tipo: 'reset' }) here would be a silent behavior change riding along on a move that is supposed to have none. One PR instead of two. Rejected for the reason under Decision above: the dedup and the module move are different kinds of risk, and conflating them would have made a regression in either harder to isolate in review.

documents.t: Status: accepted Date: 2026-08-30 References (without editing): ADR 0121 (the closest sibling — a barrel-backed decomposition whose acceptance bar was "the importers change nothing"; this ADR reuses that shape on the web side), ADR 0122 and ADR 0124 (both named this file and both explicitly deferred it — "a fully separate, still-open scope decision"; this ADR is that decision, taken).
documents.s: ADR 0125 — ProjectSettingsTab.tsx split into one file per section, behind a barrel

documents.t: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSettingsTab.tsx is 2 532 lines and 89.9 KiB. It is the last open half of the technical-debt row in docs/architecture.md and docs/explanation/backlog.md: Decompose SessionPage.tsx / ProjectSettingsTab.tsx | G | SessionPage.tsx was 169 KiB with 25 test files importing it; ProjectSettingsTab.tsx is 90 KiB The SessionPage.tsx half closed across seven PRs and two ADRs (0122, 0124). Both of those ADRs named ProjectSettingsTab.tsx in their "out of scope" sections rather than quietly narrowing the row — which is exactly why it is still here, and why closing it needs a number of its own instead of a drive-by refactor. This file is structurally much cleaner than SessionPage.tsx ever was, and that difference is the whole reason this is one PR instead of five: The parent holds nothing. ProjectSettingsTab (lines 217–239 before this change) is 17 JSX children and a props interface. No hook, no useQuery, no useQueryClient, no useTranslation, no role check, no useState — nothing at all to distribute or to reconcile against React's render cycle. No section takes more than { projectId: string }, and two (MatrixSection, CredentialsSection) take no props at all. There is no prop-drilling of data, no context, no shared useState, and no callback passed down. Each section calls its own hooks and owns its own queries. 11 of the 17 sections are already exported — the test suite had already drawn most of the boundary, the same argument ADR 0122 made for SessionPage's five timeline helpers. The duplication between sections is deliberate, and stays: useTranslation('settings') appears ~14×, useQueryClient() 11×, useToast() 10×, useCurrentWorkspaceWithRole() 5×, and useQuery({ queryKey: ['project', projectId] }) 7×. React Query dedupes those at runtime — that is what makes the pattern safe, and what makes each section independently mountable. Hoisting them into a shared parent or a context would be a behavior change dressed as cleanup, and it is not done here.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: One file per section under apps/web/src/routes/settings/, plus one shared helper module — 18 new files — and ProjectSettingsTab.tsx stays at its current path as the entry point and barrel.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Three test files depend on the path or the export names, and all three must pass unedited — that is this PR's entire acceptance bar: apps/web/src/routes/ProjectSettingsTab.test.tsx (1 356 lines, 62 its) imports 11 named exports from ./ProjectSettingsTab. apps/web/src/routes/ProjectPage.test.tsx and apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.test.tsx both vi.mock('./ProjectSettingsTab', …) by path — moving or renaming the file breaks both mocks silently. apps/web/src/routes/ProficiencySection.test.tsx imports ProjectSettingsTab itself and renders it, making it the only test that mounts all 17 sections at once — the end-to-end proof that the barrel is wired in the right order with the right props. Same reasoning as ADR 0121's db/schema.ts: the old path keeps working, so nothing downstream changes. Where 0121 used export *, this barrel names each export explicitly, because a settings section is a React component with a specific prop shape, not a table — an explicit list is what lets the compiler catch a section that stops matching its call site. New sections go into the barrel in subject position, never appended at the end — the same rule 0121 set, and here the position is literal: the barrel's import list, its re-export list and its JSX all follow render order.
documents.s: The barrel is load-bearing, not decorative

documents.t: file lines exported by the barrel settings/RepositorySection.tsx 80 no settings/ExecutionSection.tsx 88 yes settings/ExecutionModeSection.tsx 174 yes settings/ParallelismSection.tsx 121 yes settings/BudgetSection.tsx 132 yes settings/PromotionSection.tsx 85 yes settings/MelhoresModelosPorCapacidadeSection.tsx 194 yes settings/ModelsSection.tsx 334 yes settings/AreaModelsSection.tsx 143 yes settings/CatalogoDeModelos.tsx 17 no settings/MembersSection.tsx 184 no settings/PersonalAccessTokensSection.tsx 284 yes settings/ProficiencySection.tsx 256 yes settings/InstructionVersionsSection.tsx 161 no settings/MatrixSection.tsx 65 no settings/CredentialsSection.tsx 269 yes settings/GastoDasChaves.tsx 22 no settings/shared.ts 30 — A subfolder, not 18 siblings in routes/: the precedent is routes/code/, and 17 files for one tab is precisely the size at which a folder earns itself. This differs from ADR 0122's PRs 2–4, which put single extracted components next to SessionPage.tsx — one or two siblings do not justify a folder; seventeen do.
documents.s: The 17 files, in render order

documents.t: The 6 sections that are private today (RepositorySection, CatalogoDeModelos, MembersSection, InstructionVersionsSection, MatrixSection, GastoDasChaves) each gain an export on their own module — that is a mechanical consequence of the move, not a decision: the barrel cannot compose a function it cannot import. They are not re-exported by the barrel. That part is a decision, and the reason is that the barrel's export list is the public surface of this tab, and a mechanical move should not widen it. Making the barrel uniform across all 17 would have been defensible too, but it would mean this PR changed something observable — the module's export set — while claiming to change nothing. A later PR that genuinely needs one of the 6 imports it from its own file, which is now possible and was not before.
documents.s: Exported by its own file, private to the barrel

documents.t: Twelve module-scope helpers moved. The rule applied is mechanical: a helper used by exactly one section moves into that section's file; a helper used by two or more goes to settings/shared.ts. Verified by grep, not assumed — and the check corrected one expectation: iniciaisDe, PARES_DE_GRADIENTE and gradienteDe are called only by MembersSection, never by ProficiencySection. settings/shared.ts (2 helpers): ORIGIN_TONE (ModelsSection + AreaModelsSection) and formatarCustoMicros (ModelsSection + BudgetSection). Into their single caller's file (10): USO_TONE → MelhoresModelosPorCapacidadeSection; MATRIX_ROWS → MatrixSection; iniciaisDe, PARES_DE_GRADIENTE, gradienteDe → MembersSection; siglaDoConector, COR_DO_CONECTOR → CredentialsSection; LEVEL_TONE and identidadeDe → ProficiencySection; DEFAULT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_BLOCKED → ExecutionSection; MODOS_DE_EXECUCAO → ExecutionModeSection. A two-symbol shared.ts is small on purpose. The alternative — one shared module holding all twelve — would put ten helpers one indirection away from their only reader for no benefit, and would make the next person guess whether a given constant is shared. Two symbols in shared.ts means exactly what it says: these two, and only these two, are actually shared.
documents.s: Shared helpers: only what more than one section calls

documents.t: ProjectSettingsTab.module.css keeps its current path and is imported by all 15 section files that use it (CatalogoDeModelos and GastoDasChaves render only a delegate component and reference no class). One stylesheet, fifteen importers, where before there was one. This is the same answer ADR 0122 gave for SessionPage.module.css, and for the same reason: there was never a second copy, so there is nothing to drift. Forking the file per section would create fifteen chances for the .section/.sectionHead/.title/.eyebrow frame — which every section renders identically — to diverge, in exchange for nothing.
documents.s: The CSS module stays single and shared

documents.t: ProjectSettingsTab.tsx goes from 2 532 lines / 89.9 KiB to 77 lines / 4.1 KiB. The 17 sections plus shared.ts total 2 639 lines across 18 files, the largest being ModelsSection.tsx at 334. The growth over the original (2 532 → 2 716 including the barrel) is entirely import headers and the barrel itself; not one line of a section body changed. This closes the last declared open technical-debt item in docs/architecture.md. The row that named SessionPage.tsx and ProjectSettingsTab.tsx closes on both halves; the remaining rows in that table are other debts (the api↔engine four-file contract, the TerminalExecutor sandbox, Phase 4a's unclosed criterion), not this one. The acceptance bar is zero observable behavior change, proven by the full web suite — 142 files, 1 537 tests — passing with zero test files edited, including the three that constrain the path and the export names. A mechanical check backs the review: every block in every new file was matched verbatim against the pre-change file from git show dev:…, and every non-blank line of the original from the import header down was confirmed to land either in a section file or in the barrel. The only edits the move made are the added export keywords listed above and the per-file import headers. Two people can now edit two settings sections without touching the same file — the same benefit ADR 0121 claimed for the schema, at 17 units instead of 16. Four UI improvements land in these same files in later PRs of this same effort (the accepted 8-PR plan this is PR 0 of): a table of contents with anchors for the tab, one unified phrasing for inherited values across the four places that word it differently, save-per-section granularity for ParallelismSection/BudgetSection/CredentialsSection only (the three autosave sections keep autosave, deliberately), and a readable model-origin chain in ModelsSection/AreaModelsSection. None of them is in this PR. Doing the move first is what makes each of those four a small diff in one named file instead of a large diff in a 2 500-line one — which is why the plan ordered it first. The duplication stays, and stays deliberate. Fourteen useTranslation('settings') calls are now spread across fourteen files instead of concentrated in one, which makes the pattern more visible, not less. It is not a defect to fix later: the sections are independently mountable precisely because none of them depends on a parent having called a hook first.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Splitting into five PRs, like ADR 0122 did for SessionPage.tsx. Rejected: 0122's five-PR shape was forced by active churn (50 commits, 25 dependent test files, interleaved control flow) and by PR 5 not being a file move at all. Here every section is already independent, the parent holds no state, and each file is a contiguous byte-identical block — the churn argument does not apply and five PRs would be five reviews of the same trivial diff. Deleting ProjectSettingsTab.tsx and pointing project-tabs.ts at a settings/index.tsx. Rejected on evidence, not taste: two test files vi.mock the module by path and a third imports 11 names from it. The route would still work; three test files would break for a rename that buys nothing. Hoisting the shared queries (['project', projectId], useToast, useTranslation) into the parent and passing results down. Rejected: it converts 17 self-sufficient components into 17 components with a parent contract, which is a design change, not a move — and React Query already dedupes the fetches, so the "duplication" costs nothing at runtime. It would also make each section unmountable in isolation, which is exactly how ProjectSettingsTab.test.tsx exercises 11 of them today. Putting all twelve module-scope helpers in shared.ts. Rejected: ten of the twelve have exactly one caller, and a shared module that holds private helpers stops answering the question it exists to answer.

documents.t: Status: accepted Date: 2026-08-30 References (without editing): ADR 0078 (the screen frame and the tab registry — it moved the tab strip's spacing into the Tabs primitive, which this ADR now retires from the project page), ADR 0074 (the contrast debt that keeps the counter badge solid instead of tinted), ADR 0125 (PR 0 of the same accepted 8-PR effort this is PR 1 of). Revises: RN-201 — the auto-collapse half is removed; the brabo.project/brabo.tab persistence half is untouched.
documents.s: ADR 0126 — The project page navigates by a vertical rail, and the Code tab stops auto-collapsing the sidebar

documents.t: The project page has 12 tabs in 3 groups plus 3 loose tabs (apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.ts), rendered by a two-level horizontal strip (components/ui/GroupedTabs.tsx over the Tabs primitive). A design review of the product's UI ranked "replace the tab strip with a rail" first. Two of that review's three justifications were factually wrong, and are recorded here so nobody re-litigates them: "The second level opens on top of the content." False. It is an inline row below the top row — GroupedTabs.tsx:143, a sibling <div> inside the same column wrapper. Nothing ever overlaid anything. "The counter disappears when the group is closed." False. A closed group summed its children's counters and showed the total — somarContagens, GroupedTabs.tsx:33, covered by GroupedTabs.test.tsx:141. The surviving argument is the only rationale for this change: 12 items in a horizontal bar does not scale. The strip was designed for the handoff's ~6 tabs; grouping bought room by hiding 9 of the 12 behind a click, which is a compression, not a fit. On a narrow window the top row already scrolled horizontally (Tabs.module.css, overflow-x: auto). A third claim of the review — that the five counters should be summed into group totals — is rejected here as it was rejected before: the five queues (insights, PRs, approvals, backlog, architecture) stay separate, because summing them hides which queue is asking for attention. That is a standing product decision, already written into ContagensDeAba's doc comment and into ProjectPage.tsx.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: GroupedTabs is replaced by apps/web/src/routes/ProjectRail.tsx, a vertical rail sitting between the project header and the tab panel.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: That is what the change buys, and it is why a group header stopped being a selectable button and became a heading. There is no "open group" state left, and therefore no "last child visited per group" memory (ultimaFilhaPorGrupo) either — a deep link into a group tab now needs no plumbing at all to reveal it, because it was never hidden. Group headers reuse the existing i18n keys groups.*.label and tab labels reuse tabs.*.label, both in the nav namespace. project-tabs.ts does not change: it was already the single source of the structure, and the rail consumes the same GRUPOS_DO_PROJETO the strip did. (Its known asymmetry — registry key arquitetura mapping to i18n key tabs.architecture.label — is left exactly as it is.)
documents.s: The three groups are open at the same time

documents.t: routes/code/CodeShell.module.css (.rail/.railItem/.railItemAtivo) is the only rail in the repository with an active state drawn: a --surface-1 band with a right divider, a 32px item at --radius-sm, and the active item tinted color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 12%, transparent) over --accent text. The sidebar's .trilha (Shell.tsx:444-477) could not be the model: it has no active item and no keyboard navigation, so it answers neither question this component has to answer. One divergence, declared: the width. CodeShell's rail is 48px because it is icon-only. This one is 180px because it carries tab labels and group headings — which is the whole mechanism by which three groups stay open. Everything else (band surface, divider, item height, radius, active tint, hover, :focus-visible ring) is the same treatment. The counter badge stays solid --accent/--on-accent, not the handoff's 18% tint. That divergence is deliberate and already recorded in design/SCREENS.md: the tinted pair falls inside the contrast debt (3.88:1) and this is 10px text.
documents.s: Geometry borrowed from CodeShell's rail, not from Shell's

documents.t: GroupedTabs.onKeyDownDaLinha (GroupedTabs.tsx:49-71) handled ArrowRight/ArrowLeft/Home/End with wrap, and two of its seven test cases covered it (GroupedTabs.test.tsx:102,124). Deleting tested accessibility without replacing it is a regression, not a refactor, so the same contract reappears on the rail with the axis swapped: ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End, wrapping, selecting as it moves (automatic activation, the same as before). The implementation is better than what it replaces. GroupedTabs correlated positionally, querying [role="tab"] out of the DOM, because the Tabs primitive exposed no refs. The rail owns its buttons, so a Map of refs keyed by tab key gives the correlation without consulting the document. Arrow keys traverse the whole flattened list, crossing group boundaries — in a rail there is no "outer row" and "inner row" to separate. ARIA: the rail is role="tablist" with aria-orientation="vertical"; the group wrappers and their headings are role="presentation", which keeps all 12 tabs as direct owned elements of the tablist while grouping them visually.
documents.s: The keyboard contract is ported, not dropped

documents.t: Both were single-use — GroupedTabs only by ProjectPage, Tabs only by GroupedTabs — but they are not the same kind of thing, and the deciding evidence is ds-bundle/, the design system generated from this app (.ds-build-meta.json: source: web@0.1.0, 66 components, namespace BraboDS): Tabs is in it, as components/primitivas/Tabs — three entries in _ds_sync.json (.jsx, .d.ts, .prompt.md) and a story in .stories-map.json. Deleting it would shrink the design system as a side effect of one screen's layout change. A generic primitive with no current consumer is stock, not dead code. It stays, with a comment saying why. GroupedTabs is not in it — zero hits anywhere under ds-bundle/. It was project-page-specific composition over the primitive, with exactly one caller, and it goes, together with its stylesheet and GroupedTabs.test.tsx.
documents.s: GroupedTabs is deleted; Tabs stays

documents.t: The Code tab force-collapsed the Shell sidebar through AutoCollapseContext / useAutoCollapseSidebar (apps/web/src/lib/sidebar-state.ts), registered by ProjectCodeTab.tsx — the only caller — and OR-ed into the Shell's collapse at Shell.tsx:369-371,412. All of it is removed: the context, the hook, the autoColapsado state, the Provider around <Outlet />, the disabled state of the collapse button that existed only to protect the auto path, and the sidebar.collapseButton.autoCollapsed string in both locales. The reason is structural: with a project rail always present, keeping auto-collapse would put the Shell's .trilha icon rail immediately beside the new project rail — two adjacent vertical rails, permanently, on the heaviest tab in the product. The cost is real and was reviewed and accepted before this was written. Measured in the browser, not estimated: the Code tab now renders with the Shell sidebar expanded (264px) + the project rail (180px) + CodeShell's own rail (48px) = 492px of chrome before the first character of code, against ~110px before (62px collapsed sidebar + 48px code rail). That is a loss of editor width, and it is the price being paid. What is bought: auto-collapse was the system deciding for the user; manual collapse is the user deciding. Removing the system's decision while honoring the user's is the trade. Manual collapse still works and still persists in brabo.sidebar.collapsed. The double rail is not gone — it is relocated to a user-chosen state. Collapsing manually still produces the Shell's icon rail beside the project rail. The difference is who chose it. Saying otherwise would be pretending. RN-201 is rewritten in place, keeping its number and its {#rn-201} anchor (anchors are the contract). Its brabo.project/brabo.tab persistence half is untouched.
documents.s: RN-201 loses its auto-collapse half

documents.t: Shell.tsx renders its own per-project tab list in the sidebar (LinhaDeAba, RN-196), reading the same ABAS_DO_PROJETO. With the rail, the project page shows those same 12 tabs a second time, a few hundred pixels to the right. This is pre-existing, not introduced here — the horizontal strip duplicated the sidebar list in exactly the same way — but the rail makes the duplication visually parallel (two vertical lists of the same 12 labels) where before it was a row against a column. Reconciling the two is a separate product decision and is not taken here.
documents.s: Tab navigation now exists in two places — and already did

documents.t: GroupedTabs.test.tsx (7 cases) is deleted with its component. Its two keyboard cases reappear as five on the rail (ProjectRail.test.tsx, 17 cases: groups open together, the tablist's vertical orientation and 12 owned tabs, active marking, deep link, the five separate counters with no group sum, a counter-less tab showing no badge, and ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End with wrap in both directions). Two cases in apps/web/src/routes/project-tabs.test.tsx were rewritten rather than left, and this is the one place this change edits a test that was meant to survive. Both asserted the dying component's contract through ProjectPage, not the registry: 'a régua de TOPO mostra os grupos e as abas soltas … nunca as 12 chaves achatadas' asserted that exactly 6 elements had role="tab". The rail's entire purpose is that all 12 do. Rewritten to assert the same declared order, flattened, plus that the three group headings exist and that none of them is a tab. 'o selo do GRUPO é a SOMA dos selos das filhas' asserted a summed group badge. There is no closed group left to summarize, and summing is the thing this product deliberately does not do. Rewritten to assert that each queue keeps its own badge and that no group heading carries a number. Every other case in that file, and all four in ProjectPage.test.tsx, all of Shell.test.tsx, and the 'projeto e aba ativos' describe in sidebar-state.test.ts, pass unedited. The useAutoCollapseSidebar describe in sidebar-state.test.ts is deleted because the hook is. Full web suite green: 142 files, 1 540 tests.
documents.s: Tests

documents.t: A 48px icon-only rail, literally mirroring CodeShell. Rejected: 12 tabs would need 12 distinct icons that do not exist, and the three group headings — the mechanism that makes simultaneous groups readable — have no icon form at all. The result would be a row of unlabeled squares needing a tooltip each, which is worse than the strip it replaces. Keeping GroupedTabs and making it vertical. Rejected: what would survive is its top-level/second-level split, and that split is exactly what is being removed. The remaining code — the DOM-positional keyboard handler, somarContagens, ultimaFilhaPorGrupo — is all machinery for hiding children. Keeping auto-collapse and letting the two rails sit adjacent. Rejected: it hands the user a permanent, system-imposed double rail on the tab where horizontal space matters most, and the user cannot undo it (the collapse button was disabled precisely while auto-collapse was on). Deleting Tabs too, since it now has no caller. Rejected on evidence: it is a published design-system primitive, and one screen's layout change is not a reason to change the DS inventory.
documents.s: Discarded alternatives

documents.t: ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject has been, since Phase 1, projectRole ?? workspaceRole: when there is a row in project_members, it wins, without comparing it with the workspace role. The override applies in BOTH directions — up and down. This was discovered by the review of #444, which closed the role gate of the Members section, and is recorded in RN-471. The finding has two halves. The first is documentary: FOUR places promised the opposite — "the EFFECTIVE role is the higher of this one and what the person already has in the workspace", "associating someone as viewer here doesn't downgrade a workspace owner" — three OpenAPI descriptions and a comment in apps/web/src/lib/roles.ts. RN-471 fixed the web one (it was the worst: it lived in the module that exports roleAtLeast and ROLE_ORDER, that is, in the code the next person in this family opens before anything else) and DECLARED the three in the api as not fixed, because they are a contract change. The second half was not kept anywhere, and it is the reason for this ADR: with the override applying downward, AddProjectMemberUseCase was a one-line passthrough to the repository upsert and RemoveProjectMemberUseCase only checked whether the project existed. Neither of them looked at WHO the target is nor at the relation between actor and target. Two consequences reachable by any maintainer, today: downgrading the workspace owner. A maintainer writes viewer for the owner in a project and the owner loses their own project — the dashboard read, the decisions, everything. Restoring it requires maintainer, which the owner just lost in that scope; irreversible self-downgrade. A maintainer writes themselves as viewer and cannot undo it, because undoing is the same route, which requires maintainer. There is no way back through the screen. None of this is privilege escalation — nobody gains a role they did not have. It is loss of access, and the difference matters: a maintainer could already do damage in the project, but could not produce a state from which NOBODY leaves without going to the database. The obvious path would be to make forProject return "the higher of the two" and erase the problem at the root, aligning the code with the three descriptions instead of the other way around. It was considered and REJECTED: restricting someone in a sensitive project — a workspace developer who becomes viewer in project X — is a deliberate product capability, and it is the only way that exists to contain access per project. "The higher of the two" eliminates it, and resolve-effective-role.use-case.spec.ts has always pinned the upward half ("project role overrides the workspace one").
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The override stays in both directions, and the two dangerous moves are now refused. forProject does NOT change: it remains projectRole ?? workspaceRole, and remains the only composition of that role in the system. Ceiling 1 — nobody downgrades whoever is workspace owner. The role requested for someone whose workspace role is owner must be owner; anything below is 403. Writing project owner for someone who is already workspace owner is redundant and passes — only the downgrade is refused. The owner is read from workspace_members.role, never from workspaces.created_by. Both exist in db/schema/iam.ts and are not the same thing. created_by is a historical fact: who created the workspace. It is the role that authorization uses EVERYWHERE else in the system — ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forWorkspace is workspaces.findMemberRole, and created_by appears in no authorization path (it appears in get-credential-spend.use-case.ts, to know whose LLM key is being spent, which is another question). A ceiling that read created_by would protect the wrong person in two concrete and opposite cases: the creator who already transferred ownership and is now developer would be shielded without being owner, and the current owner who created nothing — the normal case of a workspace with more than one owner, and that of transferred ownership — would be unprotected, which is exactly the hole the ceiling exists to close. Ceiling 2 — nobody downgrades THEMSELVES. If the target is the caller themselves and the requested role is lower than the effective role they have TODAY in the project, it is 403. That is the formulation, with no threshold. The alternative considered was "do not self-downgrade below maintainer", with the argument that maintainer is the role that undoes. Both refuse the dangerous move, but the one with a threshold is a domain rule that copies a number from a controller's @RequireRole: it ages silently the day the route changes its minimum, and it cannot be stated without explaining where the maintainer came from. "Nobody downgrades themselves" is a clause, has no number to age, and is the SAME shape as ceiling 1 — who, not how much. The price is a harmless move that falls along with it: an owner setting themselves as maintainer in their own project would be reversible, and is now refused. It remains reachable by another maintainer, and the cost of stating the rule with an exception is greater than that of losing the move. Raising one's own role is not a downgrade and is not touched here. Where the ceilings live: in the use case, with the rule in the domain. Not in RolesGuard. The guard answers another question — it authorizes the CALLER against the route's @RequireRole — and sees neither the body (dto.role) nor the target (dto.userId), while both ceilings are about the TARGET and about the actor↔target relation. A guard that needed the body would have to know each route's DTO, which is the boundary it exists not to cross. The SHAPE follows the precedent the repository already has for an absolute ceiling: domain/actions/decide.ts (RN-154, and RN-418 which revised RN-106) — pure function, in the domain, message next to the condition, no configuration key and no "always allow". The new apps/api/src/domain/iam/tetos-de-rebaixamento.ts is that shape applied here, and AddProjectMemberUseCase calls it before writing. What does NOT carry over from the precedent is the outcome: in decide.ts the ceiling becomes require_approval on an agent proposed_action, because there is a human approval queue on the other side. Here the call already IS human and synchronous, there is no queue to send it to, and the outcome is refusal. Status: 403 in both. It is an AUTHORIZATION refusal — the caller has the route's role and lacks authority for this specific move. It is not 409, because it is not a conflict with a state that passes (waiting changes nothing); it is not 400, because the body is valid and the same body with another target would pass. ForbiddenException with its own message is what the other policy uses in the api already do (ActivateAgentUseCase, CreateSocketTicketUseCase, RegisterUseCase), and the message reaches the screen: #444 put a try/catch with mensagemDaApi in the two actions that failed silently. The three OpenAPI descriptions that RN-471 declared now describe what the code does — those of POST :projectId/members, of AddMemberDto.role and the summary of GET :projectId/members, which promised "includes whoever inherits access from the workspace" while listMembers is an innerJoin on project_members. openapi.json and api-types.generated.ts come from the generator. The web side stays OUT of this PR, and not because of size. The screen can compute ceiling 2 on its own (userIdDaSessao() and the effective role are already there since #444), but it cannot compute ceiling 1: listProjectMembers returns the role of the PROJECT ROW, and the target's WORKSPACE role is within reach of no client query. Disabling half of the options would produce a Select that is honest about one refusal and silently wrong about the other — the second role source invented on the screen that RN-471 itself writes against. Meanwhile, the refusal SHOWS: handleRoleChange already shows mensagemDaApi(erro, …) in a toast, and it is the api's sentence that explains WHICH ceiling was hit.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The override remains a double-edged sword, and that is what was bought. Neither of these two ceilings makes projectRole ?? workspaceRole safe in general; they refuse two named moves. A maintainer can still downgrade anyone who is NOT workspace owner and who is not themselves — including another maintainer, including in a way the victim cannot undo. That is the capability, not an oversight: it is the same mechanics that restricts a developer to viewer in a sensitive project, and there is no way to keep one without the other. What changed is that the state from which NOBODY leaves (owner out of their own project; the only maintainer erasing themselves) is no longer reachable. Still possible, by name: downgrading another maintainer who is not workspace owner, without their consent and with no way back by their hand; self-downgrade through REMOVAL. RemoveProjectMemberUseCase did NOT gain a ceiling, and that is one more move, outside the two chosen. Removing one's own row drops the effective role to the workspace role: when the workspace holds (maintainer there), it is benign and is precisely how someone leaves the list; when it does NOT hold — the maintainer whose authority came from the project row, with viewer in the workspace — it is irreversible self-downgrade through the other door. The premise that "removal is always benign" is false, and it stays written here so it is not rediscovered. Both cases are PINNED in tests (tetos-de-rebaixamento.use-case.spec.ts), including the one that remains open, so the next person knows it is a decision and not forgetfulness. Closing it costs the signature of RemoveProjectMemberUseCase.execute, which today is called by list-projects-and-members.use-case.spec.ts with two arguments; self-PROMOTION. A maintainer can write themselves as project owner. It was already possible before this ADR and still is; the ceilings are about going down, and opening the question of going up here would have changed, in passing, a capability nobody asked to change; downgrading the workspace owner in the workspace. Ceiling 1 is about project_members. POST workspaces/:workspaceId/members remains an upsert with no ceiling at all — same class of defect, scope above, not addressed here. The screen offers what the api refuses, for now. It is exactly the defect that the last PRs of this family closed, and it comes back through one PR, on purpose: half of the gate is impossible on the client today (see Decision). The web PR needs to decide between exposing the target's workspace role in GET :projectId/members — a contract change, and RN-471 already recorded that the route promises an innerJoin it does not do — and erasing only what it knows. Until then, the refusal is told by the toast, with the api's sentence. A 500 became a 404. AddProjectMemberUseCase now calls projects.findById (it needs the workspaceId to read the target's role) and throws NotFoundException when the project does not exist, as ListProjectMembersUseCase and RemoveProjectMemberUseCase already did. Over HTTP it is unreachable — RolesGuard refuses earlier with 403 —, but the use case stopped presuming the caller. Two more queries per association. findById, findMemberRole in the workspace and the actor's forProject (which redoes the findById). It is an administration route, called once per invitation, and the alternative — reusing the request.effectiveRole the guard already computed — would tie the use case to the guard's state, which is the coupling the choice of WHERE the ceiling lives exists to avoid. The three OpenAPI descriptions change without changing any response. Whoever integrated by reading the old promise ("higher of") was already wrong since Phase 1; the generated contract now describes the real behavior, and the 403 of the two ceilings is genuinely new for whoever calls the route.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: The real-container execution plan has two places that need to talk to a Docker daemon: the runner (the Docker of the user's machine, for a project in runner mode) and a server broker yet to be born (PR 1.2, for a project in container mode). The api never receives the socket, and that is a closed decision. The choice of library was conditioned on a proof, not on a preference. dockerode is the de facto Node client for Docker, but the runner is distributed through THREE paths — cloning the monorepo, npm install -g @brabo/runner (ADR 0106) and a standalone binary via bun build --compile (ADR 0112) — and the third is the most fragile of the three: it already needed its own manifest generator (scripts/build-bin.mjs) to embed the .node of node-pty, because Bun only embeds a file reached by a STATIC specifier. The tree that dockerode@5 drags in is large — docker-modem, ssh2, @grpc/grpc-js, protobufjs, tar-fs — and ssh2 carries an OPTIONAL native binding (cpu-features). Hence the order the product owner set: prove first, design later, with the decision already written for both outcomes — green, dockerode stays; broken, the runner falls back to execFile('docker', …) and this ADR records the exact error as the reason. No bundler patch or shim: a creative workaround here becomes debt nobody understands later.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: dockerode@5.0.1 + @types/dockerode@4.0.1 went into apps/runner, with an adapter that IMPORTS, INSTANTIATES (new Docker()) and CALLS (ping()) — exercised by a --self-test-docker flag run against the artifacts, never by an import the bundler could erase. step result pnpm --filter runner build (tsup) passed — but tsup leaves dependencies as external require (that is how jose already lives today), so dockerode did not even enter the bundle pnpm --filter runner smoke passed — node dist/index.cjs --self-test-docker resolved dockerode from node_modules and talked to the daemon pnpm --filter runner build:bin (bun build --compile) FAILED The error, pasted whole: 3 | const binding = require('../build/Release/cpufeatures.node'); ^ error: Could not resolve: "../build/Release/cpufeatures.node" at /…/node_modules/.pnpm/cpu-features@0.0.10/node_modules/cpu-features/lib/index.js:3:25 The chain is mandatory, not accidental — it was read in the installed code, not assumed: dockerode → docker-modem (lib/modem.js, linha 6: require('./ssh')) → ssh2 (lib/protocol/constants.js, linha 7: require('cpu-features')) → cpu-features/lib/index.js → require('../build/Release/cpufeatures.node') lib/modem.js does require('./ssh') at the top of the module: the SSH transport enters the graph even in this runner, which only talks to the local unix socket. The require of cpu-features is wrapped in try/catch inside ssh2 and degrades gracefully at runtime — but whoever resolves the graph here is the BUNDLER, at build time, and a bundler has no try/catch. It is the same class of problem ADR 0112 documented with node-pty, with one deciding difference: there the binding is ESSENTIAL (without it there is no terminal, and so it was worth building the embedding mechanism), and here it is optional acceleration of a transport we do not use. Measured and NOT adopted, for the record: bun build --compile --external cpu-features compiles (280 modules against 79), produces a binary of 84 473 032 B (+1.7 MB) and dockerode WORKS inside it — the ping answers against the real daemon, because the try/catch of ssh2 swallows the stub Bun leaves in place. This is written so that nobody needs to redo the investigation, and it is exactly the workaround the product owner's decision excluded in advance: it drags an optional .node from a dead SSH tree into five binaries per platform, and the debt would be illegible six months later. Therefore: the runner uses execFile('docker', …). dockerode was removed from package.json and from the lockfile; nothing of it remained in the tree. The broker (PR 1.2) does NOT inherit this decision — it runs in an image we build and never becomes a standalone binary, so dockerode remains a candidate there, and that is precisely why the port below exists.
documents.s: The proof, and what it returned

documents.t: artifact before after delta dist/index.cjs 91 843 B 106 221 B +14 378 B (+15.7 %) dist-bin/brabo-runner-linux-x64 82 777 288 B 82 789 576 B +12 288 B (+0.015 %) The growth is the new code (port + adapter + self-test), not a dependency: execFile comes from node:child_process, and there is no tree to embed. For comparison, the rejected alternative cost +1.7 MB per binary, times five platforms.
documents.s: Sizes, measured

documents.t: apps/runner/src/docker-port.ts, in the same shape as the two contracts the repository already uses to isolate an external vendor (LLMProvider from ADR 0041 and the GitProviderContract from Phase 2): abstract class, the domain's own types, errors normalized by CLASS — whoever consumes decides by the error type, never by a substring of a vendor message. Five operations, not six: start, stop, remove, inspect, exec. Containment is the TYPE, not the caller's discipline. What the port does not let you WRITE is the half that matters: privileged and cap_add — there is no field, and no library type crosses the port: the specification is CLOSED and the adapter is who assembles the payload. There is nowhere to copy the option from; network: host — RedeDoContainer is the union 'none' | 'egress', the same boundary posture as ADR 0065. host is not a value of the type, so it is not a sentence that can be said; free bind-mount — there is no LIST of mounts. There is ONE folder, the destination is the constant PONTO_DE_MONTAGEM (/work), and the folder's type is a BRAND (RaizDeProjeto): only raizDeProjetoValidada() produces a value of that type, and it refuses a relative path, with .., with NUL, the filesystem root and the system folders (/etc, /var — which is where Docker's own socket lives —, /dev, and the others). Mounting / is not "discouraged" here: it does not compile. No operation receives a container id. All of them start from the workspaceDirName (RN-109, frozen at creation), derive brabo-<workspace_dir_name> and resolve through docker ps FILTERED by name and by the label brabo.managed=true. "Stop container X", with arbitrary X, is not a sentence this port knows how to hear — and a namesake without the label returns ContainerNaoGerenciadoError, never null: treating it as absent would make start try to create over it and fail with "name already in use", a message that says nothing about the only thing that actually happened. Where the port lives, and why. In apps/runner/src/, because the runner is the only consumer that exists today. packages/shared was considered and rejected because of an invariant the package itself declares and an api test keeps honest (packages-shared-so-tipos.spec.ts): it is 100 % TYPE, nothing there can survive tsc, because main points to raw .ts and the api's production image would die with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING. A port with error classes and a validation function is runtime code. Splitting the contract into "types there, errors here" would create two sources for a single thing — which is the defect the port exists to avoid. When apps/broker is born, the file MOVES to a workspace package; it is not COPIED, and that is written in its docblock, because a second file with the same five operations and a sixth "only in the broker" is the beginning of the end of the containment above.
documents.s: The port

documents.t: Three named outcomes, in the product's vocabulary (infra | modelo | código | política), and a fourth deliberately WITHOUT origin: class origin when DockerIndisponivelError infra the daemon did not answer. The message says what to DO (docker info, docker group on Linux) and that no container was touched DockerCliAusenteError infra the docker executable is not in the PATH. It is its OWN error and not "daemon down": the two are fixed in different ways, and collapsing them is the lesson of RN-475 one floor down ContainerNaoGerenciadoError política there is a container with the derived name and WITHOUT the label brabo.managed=true ComandoDeDockerFalhouError none the daemon is alive and refused the command. Its message goes whole The fourth declares no origin on purpose: choosing between infra and code for "No such image" would be diagnosis by elimination, which is the defect ADR 0020 records as the one not to repeat. It says it is the rest, and shows what the daemon said. The separation between "daemon down" and "daemon refused" is made by the COMMAND, not by substring: any non-zero exit triggers a confirming docker version, and it is ITS result that decides the class. It costs one more call and only on the failure path — the price of not classifying by vendor text, which ADR 0002 (git) and ADR 0041 (LLM) already forbid on the other two sides.
documents.s: Failure classification

documents.t: Nothing brings up a container yet, and that is the scope. The port exists, the adapter exists, and nobody calls them: no new message on the Phoenix channel, no change of observable behavior. start/stop/remove/inspect/ exec are covered by a double in docker-cli.spec.ts and none of them was exercised against a real daemon — only ping was, through --self-test-docker. It is the same discipline as "a capability is only declared when proven": who proves the five is PR 1.3, which wires them to the channel. The runner now requires the docker BINARY in the PATH, not just the socket. On the machine of whoever runs Docker this is practically always true, and its absence has its own error. It is the most visible difference between this choice and the rejected one: dockerode talks to the socket directly and would not need the CLI. The CLI output is text, and text is not a versioned contract. Every read uses --format '{{json .}}' with a tolerant JSON.parse (an illegible line becomes null, never an exception), never column cutting. The CLI version is that of the user's machine, so no exotic flag is used — only options that have existed for many versions. Still: a change in the docker ps format would break the read, and that is a risk dockerode would not have. The exec timeout kills the client, not the command. A docker exec terminated by timeout leaves the process running INSIDE the container, and there is no way to kill it without a second exec and a PID this path does not know. The output SAYS so, instead of letting the reader assume the command died. No RN is born here, and that is declared. There is no observable behavior for a rule to describe: the product does not call the port. The rule to record — only the container with brabo.managed=true is stopped, removed or used as an exec target — is born in the PR that makes a container actually come up, together with the test evidence that covers it. The proof stays alive. --self-test-docker runs in both smokes (pnpm --filter runner smoke and smoke:bin) and passes in BOTH outcomes of the self-test — daemon answered, daemon did not answer —, because the question is about the ARTIFACT and not about the machine: requiring a daemon would make the smoke stop running exactly where it most needs to run (CI, which has no Docker for the runner). What it guarantees from now on is that the port arrives whole in dist and in the binary, and that absent Docker becomes a NAMED error instead of a raw stack trace. What nobody should redo. If someone one day proposes dockerode in the runner again, the answer is already measured above: it breaks build:bin, and the only known way to make it fit is the --external cpu-features that was rejected. In the BROKER the question is different and remains open — there is no standalone binary there, and the port is what makes that second answer an implementation instead of a rewrite.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: apps/api/src/domain/rag/rag-search-limits.ts declares, in its own comment, that the four numbers of the hybrid search — the two weights (0.6/0.4), the threshold (0.2) and the number of candidates per signal — come from no calibration at all: NENHUM dos quatro números abaixo vem de calibração com dado real: não há, ainda, um corpo de perguntas reais rodado contra este índice. ADR 0080 chose those values with the reasoning recorded (the scales of ts_rank and cosine are not comparable, and the larger weight on the vector side compensates for the shorter ruler of the lexical one) and said they would be revisited with data. The data never came, and the reason was not lack of use: the search left no trace at all. Zero table rows, zero rag.* events in the whole product. Without a trace, "calibrating" would be swapping one guess for another — and worse, it would be irreversible in practice, because there would be nothing to compare before and after. This is the first of the five stages of the measurable RAG program, and it is deliberately the only one that does not change search behavior: it gives the eyes, and stops.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The obvious way out would be a session event — the event log is already the measuring instrument for the rest of the product, and the CLAUDE.md rule says execution metrics are extracted from it by script, never by hand. But session_events.session_id is NOT NULL (apps/api/src/db/schema/sessions.ts), and a search coming from the RAG tab is a PROJECT one: it has no session at all. Recording the telemetry only as an event would lose exactly the searches in which a human looked at the scores and judged — which are the ones that carry the only real signal the measurement can have. It is the same class of problem that forced the cut of embedding metering in ADR 0075: token_usage.session_id is also NOT NULL, and indexing a repository does not happen inside a session. There the cut was declared and the spend was left out. Here the cut would be worse: half the searches would remain, and the ones that remain are the agents' — the ones nobody judges.
documents.s: The concrete obstacle

documents.t: 1. Two tables in apps/api/src/db/schema/rag.ts, not events. rag_searches (one row per search: hits with the 1-based rank of each chunk, degraded/vector_available, latency_ms, actor, and a NULLABLE session_id) and rag_feedback (the util/irrelevante vote on a chunk of a search). The aggregate's file already existed (chunks), so there is no change in the db/schema.ts barrel; the rag_verdict enum lives in the same file as the table that calls it, by the convention of ADR 0121, and actor_kind is reused from sessions.ts instead of redeclared. session_id NULL is information, not absence of data: it means the search came from the tab. 2. The weights go FROZEN in the row. pesosVigentes() (domain/rag/rag-telemetry.ts) copies {vector, lexical, threshold} from the moment of the search into the record. It is the same discipline as the price frozen in metering (ADR 0042) and the image_version of project_containers (ADR 0081). Without the copy, the first calibration that touched RAG_SEARCH_WEIGHT_VECTOR would make all previous measurement start meaning something else, silently — and "did it improve after the change?", the only question the telemetry exists to answer, would become impossible to ask with the data at hand. It is a function and not an exported constant on purpose: a shared constant would be the same object in every JSONB row in memory. 3. The event exists, and it is NARRATION. rag.search and rag.feedback enter the event log only when there is a session — the agent's path —, so the timeline can narrate what it did. The asymmetry is declared instead of hidden: the table is the source of the measurement, the event is narration, and medir:rag never reads the event log. Both types are written OUT IN FULL at the emission points, not by constant: the inventory of docs/reference/events.md is generated by grepping type: '<x>.<y>' over the api's code, and a type behind a constant is invisible to it — the doc would pass green over an incomplete list. It is the same form execution.activated already uses. 'rag' enters PREFIXOS_DE_EVENTO (scripts/docs/generate.mjs) in the same commit. 4. Recording telemetry never brings down the search, and never fails silently. The INSERT runs in a try/catch inside HybridSearchUseCase: whoever asks should not lose the answer because the measuring instrument fell. But the failure becomes a log with the origin classified (infra, ADR 0020) and searchId: null in the response — which is not the same as "found nothing": it is "there is nothing to attach a vote to", and the UI needs the two separated so as not to offer a control the api would refuse. 5. The vote requires the reference the search returned, and it is :direct. An unknown searchId, or a chunkId that was not among that search's hits, is 400. It is not decorative rigor: the rank of the voted chunk is what separates "the index is poor" from "the WEIGHTS are wrong" — a poor index does not return the right chunk at any position, a wrong weight returns the right chunk at rank 7 —, and a vote without a rank produces a meaningless number. The engine tool (rag_feedback) is category: :direct and does not become a proposed_action: rating a chunk has no external effect, and turning it into an action to approve would fill the queue with noise until nobody read the real ones anymore (the same rule that keeps rag_search/read_file out of the pipeline). The refusal comes back as an error tool-result, with the api's message, for the model to correct (RN-061/RN-163), never as a crash. 6. medir:rag fails for one thing only. vector_available: false over the whole window: then what was measured is not the hybrid search, it is its lexical half, and calibrating a vector weight against that would be calibrating against a system that is not the one running. Everything else — precision@k, degradation rate, searches without a hit above the threshold, p50/p95 latency, rank distribution of what was voted useful — is report: it comes out in the table, it does not fail. Same mold as medir-execucao.ts.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Calibration becomes possible, and is still not done. This stage does not change chunking, weights or threshold, on purpose: touching the numbers before accumulating measurement would destroy the baseline it exists to create. The item remains declared open in CLAUDE.md, now with the instrument next to it. degraded and vector_available are two columns, and today they are redundant. degraded = !vector_available at this moment. The redundancy is declared in the schema instead of hidden, and the reason not to derive one from the other on read is that they do not answer the same question: vector_available is a fact about the embedding PROVIDER at the instant of the search — it is what makes medir:rag fail —, and degraded is the word of the CONTRACT with the engine (POST /internal/rag/search), whose definition can grow to other degradations without the provider having fallen. Deriving would tie the two forever. The vote does not survive "Reindex now". rag_feedback.chunk_id references chunks with CASCADE. Reindexing deletes and recreates the chunks, so the judgment history goes with them. Keeping an orphan vote pointing to a chunk that no longer exists would measure nothing — but the price is real and is written in the schema: whoever reindexes loses the comparison base, and the measurement restarts. precision@k measures what was JUDGED, not what was returned. The denominator is the number of voted hits with rank ≤ k, never k. A hit without a vote is unknown, not irrelevant, and counting it as irrelevant would make precision plummet on its own every time someone voted on fewer chunks — measuring the willingness to vote, not the quality of the search. The accepted consequence is that the metric only exists where there are votes: with none, it is null and the table says "not measured", never 0. The internal contract with the engine grew in both directions. POST /internal/rag/search now accepts OPTIONAL sessionId/agent in the body (the api has no way to deduce either; a session it did not receive is a session that did not exist) and returns searchId plus a chunkId per hit. The chunkId is the only exception to the deliberate simplification of that DTO — without the searchId/chunkId pair the agent would have nothing to point to. When searchId comes null, the tool omits the ids and the invitation to vote, instead of offering the model a reference that would be refused. One more tool in the prompt of six agents. rag_feedback enters the six registries that already had rag_search (dev/tools.ex, gates/qa_tools.ex, qa_estrategia_agent.ex, qa_performance_seguranca_agent.ex, appsec_agent.ex, harness/tools.ex). Real cost: one more spec block in the context of each turn. The alternative — only human feedback — would leave out the path most searches go through. A viewer route that WRITES. POST /projects/:projectId/rag/feedback has the same role as search, and not maintainer: voting neither spends nor configures anything, it is observation, and restricting it would empty the only source of truth of the measurement. It is classified in docs/security-surface.md with this reasoning; the containment is the use case's reference validation, not the role. No new agent, and no gate. The golden set and the rag-acertivo gate are the next stage, and depend on this one having accumulated data before they exist.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0065 decided that a project's image is an ARTIFACT of the Arquiteto (Architect), and ADR 0081 created the lifecycle table (project_containers). Neither of them brought up a container: to this day CLAUDE.md records "FASE 25b segue cortada: NENHUM serviço chama Docker". ADR 0128 built the foundation — a DockerPort of FIVE operations (start/stop/remove/inspect/exec) and an adapter over execFile('docker', …) — inside apps/runner, and wrote, in anticipation, that that file would MOVE when the second consumer was born: "a second file with the same five operations and a sixth 'only in the broker' is the beginning of the end of the containment". This ADR is that second consumer. It decides three things that do not separate: where the port comes to live, what the broker is, and what prevents a root-equivalent service on the host from becoming arbitrary access to Docker. The previous decision it does NOT reopen: the api never receives the socket. Neither does the engine. The socket is mounted in a single service, which exists for that.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: apps/runner/src/docker-port.ts and docker-cli.ts (plus the two .spec.ts) become packages/docker-port/src/, in a new workspace package (@brabo/docker-port) consumed by apps/runner and apps/broker. None of the files was copied. packages/shared was rejected, and the reason is verified, not aesthetic. That package is 100% TYPE, and the invariant is kept honest by apps/api/test/packages-shared-so-tipos.spec.ts — its main points to raw .ts, and the api's production image dies on boot with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING if any value survives tsc. A port with error classes, constants and validation functions is runtime code. The new package has no build step, and that is what makes it consumable. Both consumers BUNDLE it: the runner through tsup and through bun build --compile, the broker through tsup. Neither of them resolves it from node_modules at runtime inside an image. In development, the .ts is executed directly by Node's type stripping — the pnpm link is a symlink and the realpath falls outside node_modules, so Node's refusal does not apply (measured, not assumed). Declared consequence: the api CANNOT consume this package. Its image's pnpm deploy --prod copies the actual package, without a symlink, and then the realpath falls inside node_modules — exactly the error the packages/shared test exists to prevent. That is why validarDecisaoDeImagem (the api's domain) does not move here, and why the broker does not import it. What the broker has is its OWN parse (especificacaoValidada), and the next section explains why it is not a second version of the same rule. Bundling, measured after the move. pnpm --filter runner build, build:bin, smoke and smoke:bin stay green; the standalone binary (linux-x64) loads the port and queries the daemon from inside it, which is what ADR 0128 already proved. The Bun bundle went from 79 to 83 modules. The package enters as a devDependency of the runner — same shelf as phoenix — because tsup leaves dependencies as EXTERNAL require and embeds a devDependency, and because the package published on npm cannot carry a workspace:* that nobody outside this repository resolves. npm pack --dry-run in apps/runner still produces the same four files.
documents.s: 1. The port MOVES to packages/docker-port

documents.t: apps/broker is a Node/TS service, of the same family as the runner: no web framework (there are six routes), plain node:http, its own image in docker/broker/. What makes it non-arbitrary is not an allowlist of anything. It is the SHAPE of the input: It receives a projectId and one of the five operations. It goes to the api to READ the Arquiteto's decision and the project context (GET /internal/projects/:projectId/container-spec). It COMPOSES the specification itself. There is no parameter in which to write privileged, cap_add, network: host or a free -v — because there is no parameter. If the spec traveled in the body, the containment of a root-equivalent process on the host would depend on the CALLER being correct. One more HTTP call is the price of containment depending on nobody, and it is a low price: the api is on the other side of the same internal network. Why the broker revalidates what the api itself returned. Because it cannot presuppose the correctness of whoever answers it — and because the two validations answer different questions. validarDecisaoDeImagem, in the api, asks "is this architecture decision reviewable?" (requires rationale, refuses latest, applies RECURSOS_MAXIMOS, returns the refusal to the MODEL through the tool-result). especificacaoValidada, here, asks "can I hand this to the daemon?" — it is the parse of an untrusted JSON into the closed type. The overlap is small and declared (tag/digest, a numeric ceiling), and it is not a mirror to maintain: the ceilings here are the BROKER's, the last resort it never exceeds wherever the request comes from. Today the numbers coincide with the api's on purpose; if they ever diverge, the smaller wins and nothing breaks, because neither claims to be the other. One check exists only on this side, and it is new: an image reference that starts with -. image becomes a POSITIONAL argument of docker run, and --privileged as an "image name" would be read by the CLI as a flag. execFile without a shell solves COMMAND injection; ARGUMENT injection is another thing, and it is solved here.
documents.s: 2. The broker does not accept a container specification

documents.t: ADR 0128's EspecificacaoDeContainer had cpus and memoriaMb, and the Arquiteto's artifact always had three numbers — RecursosDoContainer.pidsLimit is what contains a fork bomb without depending on recognizing the command. Without the field, the broker would read the artifact and discard the third: the artifact would promise a ceiling the container does not receive, which is the "an artifact that promises more than the container receives lies to whoever audits it" that the api's own domain names. Adding a field to the port is a move that deserves a note, because the rule of this design is not to add parameters. The rule applies to what LOOSENS. This tightens, and becomes --pids-limit next to --cap-drop ALL.
documents.s: 3. pidsLimit enters the port

documents.t: Its OWN network in Compose (broker, internal: true), in both files. The api participates in two networks; the engine and the web do not participate in this one, so they do not reach the broker. internal: true also removes the broker's outbound route to the internet, which it does not use. No published port. Nothing on the host needs to reach it. /var/run/docker.sock mounted only here. :ro on the socket would be cosmetic — Docker's protocol is HTTP over that socket and every operation writes — and so it was not used as if it were containment. Authentication by BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN, the same secret and the same header already used api↔engine in both directions, compared in constant time. In production the broker REFUSES to start with the variable empty, with the repository's public literal, or with fewer than 16 characters — the rule of ADR 0059/RN-114, which weighs more here than in any other service. The broker starts under profiles: ["container-broker"] in both composes, and therefore does not start by default. Nothing calls it to write yet; giving access to the host's Docker to every development machine in exchange for nothing would be a change of posture with no counterpart. docker/smoke.sh runs without a profile and keeps proving the same three images.
documents.s: 4. Network, port and socket

documents.t: The api sends no path at all — neither workspace_path, nor the managed root. The -v of a docker run is resolved by the DAEMON, against the HOST's filesystem; /data/project-workspaces/<x> is a path from inside the api's container, and sending it would make the daemon create and mount an EMPTY folder, with the dev agent working in a directory without code and nothing indicating why. The broker composes the path with PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT, ITS configuration, plus the workspaceDirName frozen at the project's creation (RN-109). Without that variable, start refuses naming it; the other four operations keep working. Refusing is the decision: guessing would produce the empty mount silently.
documents.s: 5. No path crosses the boundary

documents.t: It gains a PORT (ContainerBrokerPort) and an HTTP client. Of the five declared operations, one has a caller: inspect, through the container lifecycle route, which now returns the OBSERVED state next to the RECORDED one. The other four are external effects and do not happen without a proposed_action — whoever will propose is the Infra Lead, with the user's final authority, and that is another PR. Declaring the five now and wiring four later is the opposite of hiding a trigger: the method exists and nothing calls it, which any search for a caller shows in a second. It gains no new write. RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase remains byte for byte as it was, mode guard included — it falls together with the RN-105 gate in the three modes, in a PR that decides both things at once. As a consequence, the broker declares the same policy on its side: a mounted/runner project is refused with 409, because their code lives in a user folder the broker's host does not see. Changing only one of the two sides now would leave the api and the broker disagreeing about what exists.
documents.s: 6. What the api gains, and what it deliberately does not gain

documents.t: The broker is root-equivalent on the host, and that is the price. It is written, not hidden. Contained by five independent layers: no published port; an internal network only the api reaches; a service token in constant time; five operations with a closed surface; and the specification computed, never accepted. None of them trusts the others. One mechanism, not two. ADR 0128 left dockerode technically possible in the broker (it never becomes a standalone binary). The product owner's decision was CLI on both sides, and the reason is not technical: two mechanisms for the same operation mean two ways of failing, two error surfaces to classify and two versions of the spec → daemon translation. The price is the broker's image needing the docker binary inside it — docker-cli, only the client — and it is paid in the Dockerfile, with DockerCliAusenteError naming the day someone mounts the socket without installing the client. The project_containers table can now LIE, and the read says so. Before it could not: container_id was always NULL. Reconciliation is ON READ, not a background daemon — a container killed from outside appears as recorded running and observed exited. The two columns never merge, and "I could not look" has its own reason (broker-nao-configurado, broker-sem-resposta, broker-recusou) instead of inheriting the recorded one. It is RN-468 applied, and no broker refusal brings down the read of the recorded state, which is legitimate information on its own. Declared gap: an orphan container of a project that never had a lifecycle row does not appear in that route — it reads the recorded state first and only then asks the daemon. Whoever finds orphans is the sweep by brabo.managed=true, and the global page that consumes it is another PR. The broker image is NOT published on GHCR. docker-bake.hcl, scripts/ci/images-manifest.ts (ALVOS) and release.yml keep the FOUR images of ADR 0119. The broker starts under a profile, is not part of the default deploy and nothing calls it to write; publishing it now would put in the public registry an image nobody installs. When the Infra Lead PR makes it necessary, it enters through the same path as the other four — it is one line in each of the three places, and ALVOS has a test. PHASE 25b is no longer entirely cut, and only that. There is a service capable of calling Docker, and a READ path that calls it. No container comes up: there is no loop, no queue, no container_start proposed_action. The CLAUDE.md sentence changes to say exactly that, and nothing more. An operational novelty that did not exist: DOCKER_GID. The socket is root:docker on the host and the broker process runs non-root, so the compose uses group_add. The default (999) is the most common and is wrong in several distributions; getting it wrong produces "permission denied" on the socket, which DockerIndisponivelError already names with the group hint. It is in .env.example and in the runbook.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: The Arquiteto (Architect) already has six tools (create_module_map, assign_story_modules, choose_project_image, create_c4_diagram, propose_adr, emit_insight) and an image decision — choose_project_image (ADR 0065) — that is per project: a single image, for the container of the whole project. The real-container execution plan (ADR 0128/0130) asks for more granularity: a project with modules of different stacks (a Node service, a Python worker) does not fit in a single image when each module needs to come up separately. The design question is not "which image", it is "who decides what". The Arquiteto already sees the architecture (it is the one who wrote the module_map), but it does not see the fleet of images already in use, the cost of maintaining one more variant, or the operational conventions Infra follows — those are Infra's competences, not Architecture's. Giving the Arquiteto the power to FIX each module's image (as choose_project_image fixes the project's) would push an operational decision onto whoever only has the design side.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The Arquiteto nominates; Infra elects. This delivery is only the Arquiteto's half: a new tool, route_modules_to_infra, that produces a LIST — one item {modulo, imagemCandidata, porque} per module of the current module_map — and records it as artifact.module_routing, next to artifact.module_map/artifact.project_image/artifact.c4_diagram (same tableless design as ADR 0065, extended here: the event IS the artifact). The half that ELECTS (the Infra Lead reading this list and deciding, with its own proposed_action) is a separate PR — the routing exists and is auditable before Infra has a tool to consume it, the same kind of sequencing that already held for module_map arriving before create_c4_diagram needed it. :direct, outside the global @registry — not a proposed_action. Routing has no external effect: it does not bring up a container, it changes nothing outside the event log. It is an INTERNAL architecture decision, of the same caliber as choose_project_image and create_c4_diagram, which are also :direct. Turning this into a proposed_action would put a draft decision (which Infra will still review) in the same queue that approves git push. The candidate image goes through the SAME validation as choose_project_image, per item. validarDecisaoDeImagem (domain/containers/project-container.ts) already knows how to refuse an image without tag/digest, latest, and a short rationale — reimplementing that rule per module would create two versions of it to diverge. The new domain (domain/architecture/module-routing.ts) only adds what is SPECIFIC to the list: it cannot be empty (it is not a decision), it cannot repeat a module (ambiguous — which of the two images holds?), and each cited modulo must exist in the project's current module_map (same check as assign_story_modules/missingModules, and for the same reason: the refusal lists the VALID names, so as not to force the model to guess). Without a module_map, there is nothing to route — refused, not invented. The tool only makes sense after create_module_map; the build_kickoff/1 of ArquitetoServer (the only place from which the model learns the ORDER of the tools) now lists route_modules_to_infra as step 4, right after the module_map. Calling without a current module_map is refused with the same text as create_c4_diagram — "defina o module_map antes" — instead of routing against an empty or invented map.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Nothing brings up a container yet. This delivery does not change the RN-105 gate, does not touch RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase, does not introduce a new proposed_action. What exists after it: an auditable list of nominations, read by a human in the event log — Infra does not yet have a tool to act on it (next PR). The candidate image may diverge from the project image (choose_project_image). On purpose: a module can justify an image different from the one the Arquiteto fixed for the project as a whole — it is exactly the granularity this delivery exists to open. Reconciling the two (or retiring choose_project_image in favor of per-module routing) is a separate product decision, not taken here. EstadoDoRoteamento/GetModuleRoutingUseCase follow the same mold as GetC4DiagramUseCase — tableless read, current by highest version with a tie-break by seq. Existing as a separate use case (instead of inline in the write one) is what gives correct versioning without duplicating the logic of "which is the current one" — the same reason DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase uses ObterContainerDoProjetoUseCase.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0129 (Part 2, Stage 1) gave the hybrid search a trace — rag_searches/rag_feedback, with the weights FROZEN in the row — but deliberately measured nothing: it only instrumented. pnpm --filter api medir:rag reads that trace per project, when it exists. What was still missing is what rag-search-limits.ts itself keeps declaring: NENHUM dos quatro números abaixo vem de calibração com dado real: não há, ainda, um corpo de perguntas reais rodado contra este índice. This is Stage 2 of the same program — the second of five, in the order the product owner set. It calibrates nothing (that is a separate product decision, Stage 5, with its own give-up criterion); it provides the body of questions that Stage 1 left as a gap.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The regression golden-set of the QA Automation's SEMANTIC judgment (ADR 0123) solved an adjacent problem — "how to measure the reliability of something non-deterministic, without CI, with a ratchet floor" — and the decision here is to reuse the whole structure, not invent the same reasoning a second time: piece ADR 0123 (QA) this ADR (RAG) alias mix.exs "golden_set.qa" "golden_set.rag" permanent exclusion test_helper.exs :golden_set_qa :golden_set_rag ExUnit test test/engine/gates/qa_automacao_agent_golden_test.exs test/engine/rag/rag_golden_test.exs ratchet floor test/fixtures/golden_set_qa/floor.json test/fixtures/golden_set_rag/floor.json seed apps/api/scripts/seed-golden-set-qa.ts apps/api/scripts/seed-golden-set-rag.ts Permanent exclusion by TAG (never detection of "Ollama reachable") holds for the SAME reason as on the QA side: this development machine already has Ollama up all the time, and automatic inclusion would make the module fire inside ANY mix test, spending tokens without warning.
documents.s: The mold already exists, and it is ADR 0123

documents.t: The QA golden-set tests the judgment of a chat LLM, called through Engine.Gates.QaAutomacaoAgent.run/5. RAG has no LLM judgment at all on the measured path — the whole hybrid search (embedding + ts_rank + weighted fusion + threshold cut) runs inside the api (HybridSearchUseCase), not the engine. Reimplementing the search in Elixir just for this test would test a SECOND implementation, never the real one — the same error ADR 0123 avoided by using the real LLM client instead of simulating the judgment. The solution: seed-golden-set-rag.ts does BOTH things — provisions and searches —, returning the result ready; rag_golden_test.exs only invokes the script (via System.cmd, same mechanism as the QA side) and applies the floor over the JSON that comes back. The role of the Elixir side is not "to run the search", it is "to be the single point of mix test --only/permanent exclusion/ratchet floor" — the same golden-set discipline the rest of the product already uses, applied to a mechanism that happens to live entirely on the other side of the api↔engine boundary.
documents.s: Where the mold does NOT fit — and why that is not a deviation

documents.t: The original request asked for REAL questions from dogfooding. Checked before writing this ADR: gh issue list --repo daneiel/brabo --state all returns "No Issues" — it is a solo project, with no history of a question formulated by someone using the product, in an issue or PR (PR titles are all tipo(escopo): o que mudou, never a question). The 17 questions in seed-golden-set-rag.ts are therefore composed from REAL RNs and ADRs of this repository — never invented without grounding.
