Each one has an expectedPath that is the real file where the answer lives, and the composition was verified by directly reading the target file before writing the question (not by title/grep). It is the route the request itself foresaw for the case of there being no genuine corpus, and pretending they are "real" would be worse than declaring the composition.
documents.s: The questions: composed, not extracted — and that is said, not hidden

documents.t: Unlike QA (whose code skeleton is synthetic, purposely designed for each case), the RAG golden-set corpus is a REAL SUBSET of docs/ from this very monorepo — 22 files (ARQUIVOS_CURADOS in the seed), copied verbatim into the seeded project's repository, indexed by the SAME IndexProjectDocsUseCase any real project uses. Curated, not the whole tree (the real tree has more than 130 ADRs) — because of embedding cost in a manual run: searching among a few hundred chunks already exercises vector+lexical fusion just like searching among thousands, and reindexing more than a hundred ADRs on every manual run would multiply the time without improving what the golden-set measures.
documents.s: The indexed corpus is real, curated, not synthetic

documents.t: The QA golden-set provisions one repository per CASE, because each case tests a different business rule over DIFFERENT code — isolation is essential. The 17 RAG cases are 17 questions over the SAME documentation corpus: splitting into 17 projects would index the same content 17 times (17x the embedding cost) to isolate searches that are already, by nature, read-only and free of side effects among themselves.
documents.s: A single project, not one per case

documents.t: ReadProjectCodeUseCase.portaoDoContainer (RN-105) refuses with 409 any read of a container project until the Arquiteto decides an image — IndexProjectDocsUseCase calls that path to sweep docs/. The golden-set never triggers the Arquiteto (there is no execution at all to justify it, only documentation indexing), so the seed inserts the project with execution_mode: 'runner' — RN-169/RN-421 exempt mounted/runner from the whole gate, and it is exactly for this kind of case: a project without its own container has no reason to wait for an image decision to have its code read. The CHECK projects_workspace_path_casa_com_modo requires a non-null workspace_path for execution_mode <> 'container' — the seed writes a synthetic path (never used: no real runner connects to this project).
documents.s: execution_mode: 'runner', not the default container

documents.t: The expected hit is the file path, never the exact chunk — the same loose rule as ADR 0123 adapted to RAG: pinning the chunk would break the golden-set at every chunking adjustment, which is precisely the parameter this program exists to be able to revise without rewriting the cases. GOLDEN_SET_RAG_TOP_K = 5, and not rank 1: that is how the product actually uses the result — the RAG Chat cites SEVERAL chunks next to an answer (RagCitationCard, plural), not just the first. Measuring against rank 1 would measure a question the UI does not ask. 5 is also not the same RAG_SEARCH_RESULT_LIMIT (10) the real route uses by default — asking for 10 and measuring against 10 would test a looser k than most real searches use (the RAG Chat panel does not scroll to see the 10). The criterion lives in apps/api/src/domain/rag/golden-set-criterio.ts, pure and tested (golden-set-criterio.spec.ts), for the same reason as gate-registry.ts: the decision "this matched" should not depend on how the result arrived.
documents.s: The accuracy criterion: file path, top-K, never rank 1

documents.t: HybridSearchUseCase writes a row in rag_searches on every call, always — there is no parameter to turn that off, and there should not be. The right question is not "turn it off?", it is "does this pollute the real measurement?": no. medir:rag requires --projeto <uuid> (it never aggregates globally, see the script's own header), and the golden-set always creates a NEW project with a timestamp suffix — the rows it writes never appear in medir:rag of a real project, for the same reason the QA golden-set pollutes no metric of a real project. And actually writing is what makes this golden-set exercise the SAME code path the real RAG Chat uses.
documents.s: Telemetry: ON, on purpose

documents.t: - id: rag-acertivo fluxo: transversal # o RAG serve todos os fluxos, como acao-aprovada dono: usuario entrada: [golden-set-rag] entregavel: taxa-de-acerto-acima-do-piso verificacao: script severidade: warn aprovacao_humana: false status: active evidencia: tipo: teste arquivo: apps/engine/test/engine/rag/rag_golden_test.exs fluxo: transversal and dono: usuario are reused from the acao-aprovada gate, on purpose — neither field is validated against an enum (apps/api/src/domain/gates/gate-registry.ts), and inventing a new single-member category (instrumentos/medicao) would pass the validator without meaning anything. If a medicao owner is ever desired, it already exists as a ROLE in docs/fluxo.yml (camada_instrumentos), and introducing it is a separate decision, not a side effect of this gate. evidencia.tipo: teste, and not event_log — what proves this gate is the golden-set itself, not an event in the log (there is no proposed_action nor domain event associated with a golden-set pass). Precedent: merge-protegida already uses tipo: teste for the same reason — the guarantee does not come from the event log. severidade: warn is MANDATORY, not stylistic: RN-070 requires verificacao: script for block (which this gate HAS), but the warn decision comes from elsewhere — there is no CI with an LLM (same decision already recorded for the QA golden-set), so the gate runs MANUALLY, and promising block would describe an automatic lock that does not exist. docs/explanation/gates.md gains the fifth worked example of "why warn", following the same argumentative structure as the previous four (necessidade-validada, workspace-verificado, implementavel, paralelismo-autorizado). entrada: [golden-set-rag] is not a reference to another gate — the validator's heuristic (entrada ending in -verificada/-segura) does not match that name, so it does not trigger the orphan check. Confirmed by reading apps/api/src/domain/gates/gate-registry.ts (pareceGate), not assumed.
documents.s: The rag-acertivo gate

documents.t: Copy the structure of ADR 0123 (alias, permanent exclusion, ExUnit test, ratchet floor per MODEL — here, EMBEDDING model —, external seed via System.cmd) to the RAG domain, with the two adaptations the domain requires: the seed runs the search (not just provisions, because the judgment lives entirely on the api side) and the corpus is real and curated (not synthetic). apps/api/src/domain/rag/golden-set-criterio.ts — pure, tested — defines the accuracy criterion (file path, top-5, never exact chunk/rank 1) and is consumed both by the seed and by any future debugging call. docs/gates.yml gains rag-acertivo, warn, status: active, evidencia.tipo: teste pointing to the ExUnit test. floor.json keyed by the EMBEDDING model (RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL, today nomic-embed-text — the only one the product supports, RN-222), count and of, never a percentage, written only by a human.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: CI wiring is TODO(humano), same as QA. Without an API LLM secret or new infra (real Ollama in CI), the golden-set runs MANUALLY — mix golden_set.rag — and never in a normal mix test. The 17 questions measure retrieval over a 22-file corpus, not the 130+ real ADRs. A golden-set against the full corpus would measure a more realistic difficulty distribution (more plausible distractors, more chance of two files covering the same question) — an embedding-cost decision in a manual run, revisable if the real run shows an artificially easy ceiling. The golden-set measures RETRIEVAL, not ANSWER. It never calls a chat LLM to synthesize an answer from the hits — it only measures whether the right path appeared among the candidates. It is the metric Stage 1 (medir:rag) also uses (precision@k, rank distribution), so the two instruments speak the same language. About the real run and what the floor records: see test/fixtures/golden_set_rag/floor.json for the _comment with the measured result (or the statement that the measurement was left pending a human run, if this session's environment did not allow running against real Ollama).
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0131 opened the missing half of module routing: the Arquiteto (Architect) NOMINATES one image per module (route_modules_to_infra, recorded in artifact.module_routing) and declared, in so many words, that "the half that ELECTS (the Infra Lead reading this list and deciding, with its own proposed_action) is a separate PR". This is that PR. ADR 0130 (container broker) also left a dangling sentence, in the ContainerBrokerPort's own comment: "Bringing up, stopping and removing are EXTERNAL EFFECTS and do not happen without a proposed_action; whoever will propose is the Infra Lead, with the user's final authority, and that is another PR." This one too. The question both ADRs left open, and which only appears when one tries to CONNECT the two wires, is: the broker does not accept a specification — it reads GET /internal/projects/:projectId/container-spec (ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase), which in turn reads the Arquiteto's current decision in artifact.project_image (RN-105, DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase, ADR 0065). It does NOT read artifact.module_routing. So: if Infra elects a routing candidate and that does not become a new version of artifact.project_image, the election is auditable in the event log and inert — the container that comes up remains the one choose_project_image decided, which may not even exist yet, or may be a completely different image from the elected one.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Infra's election emits a NEW VERSION of artifact.project_image, reusing DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase whole — not a parallel path. This means: artifact.project_image stops being emitted only by the Arquiteto (choose_project_image). It now has TWO possible emitters — the Arquiteto, deciding from scratch, and Infra, ELECTING among the routing candidates the Arquiteto itself produced — and each event's decidedBy says which one it was ('arquiteto' vs. 'infra-lead', since DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase.execute already accepted that parameter, just never used with another value). The comment in the code of project-container.ts that calls the image an "ARTEFATO DO ARQUITETO" remains true in the sense that matters — it is an architecture decision, versioned, auditable, never hidden configuration — but stops being true in the sense of "only the Arquiteto writes to it". CLAUDE.md (Conventions section) is updated to declare this. Why reuse DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase instead of a parallel path that writes artifact.project_image directly: Same validation, only once. validarDecisaoDeImagem (explicit tag/digest, latest refused, minimum rationale, RECURSOS_MAXIMOS ceiling) is already the single source of that rule — reimplementing it on Infra's path would create the SAME divergence the comment in module-routing.ts already recorded when it decided to reuse that function instead of rewriting it per module. Same reasoning, one layer up. One current, not two. ObterContainerDoProjetoUseCase reads "the highest-numbered version" of artifact.project_image — if Infra's election wrote another event type, or its own table, the product would have TWO possible answers to "which image does this project run", and every existing consumer (RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase, the RN-105 gate of the Code tab, the broker via ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase) would need to learn to choose between them. Reusing the same artifact is what preserves "one current" without requiring anyone to change. The trail already exists. rationale is a free field — the election writes in it that the image was ELECTED among the routing candidates (citing the porque Infra gave), so whoever reads the history of artifact.project_image months later does not see an image appearing out of nowhere: they see the chain — the Arquiteto nominated, Infra elected, with each side's reason. The elected image MUST be one of the imagemCandidata of the current artifact.module_routing — never invented. ExecuteContainerStartUseCase validates this BEFORE calling DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase: if Infra proposes an image outside the list, the action fails with a message naming the refused image and the valid candidates — the same explanatory-refusal mechanism validarRoteamento/validarDecisaoDeImagem already use (RN-061: the whole reason goes back to whoever decides to correct). Without a current routing (status: 'sem_roteamento'), there is no candidate at all and every election is refused — the Arquiteto needs to run route_modules_to_infra first. The tension made explicit, not hidden: the Arquiteto remains the one who PROPOSES (via choose_project_image OR via route_modules_to_infra); Infra can now emit a new version of the SAME artifact when it ELECTS. It is not "Infra decides the image from scratch" — it is "Infra chooses which of the Arquiteto's proposals becomes reality", and the write reflects that: decidedBy: 'infra-lead' and a rationale that cites the originating nomination, never a rationale invented from scratch as if it were a new decision. container_start is a new proposed_action, with the user's final authority — never auto-approvable by default. Unlike open_infra_pr (which the Infra Lead can auto-approve for itself, because it only opens a PR a human still merges), bringing up the container is a real external effect — it calls the broker, which talks to the server's Docker daemon (ADR 0130). It stays require_approval by default (MIN_ROLE_FOR_ACTION_TYPE: maintainer, same caliber as open_infra_pr/parallelize), and does NOT enter the autonomy list seeded by the Infra Lead's accept-handoff — a deliberate decision, not forgetfulness. container_start stays OUT of the absolute-ceilings block of decide.ts (merge into a protected branch, instruction_patch, parallelize/ raise_max_parallel) — same reasoning already recorded there for propose_execution_plan/assess_implementability: it is the FIRST time this project's container actually comes up for this election, not an overrun of an already authorized ceiling. A maintainer CAN configure permissions.json to auto-approve container_start, if they decide they want that level of automation — the product does not force that door shut, just as it does not for open_infra_pr.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The RN-105 gate does not change. The Code tab stays closed until artifact.project_image has a decision — only now that decision may have come from two places. No existing consumer of ObterContainerDoProjetoUseCase needed to change. container_start is the FIRST real caller of ContainerBrokerPort.start. Of the five operations of ADR 0128/0130, inspect already had a caller (read, the lifecycle route); start gets its own here. stop, remove and exec still have no proposed_action at all — it is not a gap fixed entirely, it is one slice of the PHASE 25b cut closing. Dev agents do NOT YET work inside the container that comes up. Bringing up the container and moving the dev agent's worktree into it are different things — the second is a separate PR (1.6). This PR proves that the path proposed_action → approval → broker → project_containers works end to end; what runs inside the container, for now, is only what the broker brings up (the elected image, mounting the project folder) — with no consumer yet. RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase gets its first real caller outside tests. The state machine already existed (ADR 0081); the novelty is that now something other than a test actually triggers provisioning/running, after the broker confirms. The transition to provisioning is only possible when there is no row yet, or the row is in failed/removed — from stopped, the correct transition is directly to running (the ADR 0081 state machine does not allow stopped -> provisioning, and recreating the row from scratch for a container that was only stopped would destroy the imageVersion history needlessly). Alternative considered and discarded: a new event (artifact.container_election, or similar) separate from artifact.project_image. It would preserve a cleaner separation between "the Arquiteto proposes" and "Infra decides", but would create exactly the problem the Decision avoids: two artifacts competing to be "this project's current image", and every consumer (broker via ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase, RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase, the RN-105 gate) needing to know how to choose between them. Discarded because the cost of keeping two currents in sync outweighs the value of a "purer" separation between the two roles — BOTH roles still exist (Arquiteto proposes, Infra elects), only the output artifact is a single one.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0133 (PR 1.5) closed the container_start path (proposed_action → approval → broker → project_containers) end to end and declared, in so many words: "dev agents do NOT YET work inside the container that comes up [...] what runs inside the container, for now, is only what the broker brings up — with no consumer yet." This is the PR that provides the consumer. Today, even with a real container up, Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor keeps running EVERY dev agent terminal command via System.cmd INSIDE the engine's own process, against the shared folder (PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT) — exactly as it always did. The container sits idle: nothing in it is ever docker execed.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: When the project is in execution_mode: container with a REGISTERED running row in project_containers, the dev agent's terminal command now runs INSIDE the container, via docker exec (through the broker) — no longer via local System.cmd.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor already had FOUR outcomes (RN-423, ADR 0104, the routing to the local runner). It gains a fifth, :executar_no_container, conditioned on execution_mode == "container" AND Engine.Containers.ProjectContainerLifecycle.running?/1 — a new read-only read, directly on the project_containers table (same pattern as Engine.Projects.Project reading projects: the engine reads the column the api writes, without duplicating the derivation). mounted NEVER falls into that outcome: the broker refuses to bring up a container for that mode (ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError, deliberate policy until PR 1.7 revisits the three modes), so the question does not even make sense for it.
documents.s: The fifth outcome of decisao_de_execucao/1

documents.t: ContainerBrokerPort.exec (ADR 0130) already existed, with the whole scope validation on the broker side (DiretorioForaDoEscopoError outside /work) — but it had ZERO callers. It is closed with: A new internal route, POST internal/projects/:projectId/container-exec, in InternalProjectsController (not in InternalContainersController — see "Why not in the broker's controller", below) — the same EngineServiceGuard as always, called by the ENGINE, not by the broker. ExecutarComandoNoContainerUseCase: calls ContainerBrokerPort.exec and handles BrokerRecusouError/BrokerIndisponivelError by returning a TYPED failure result ({ sucesso: false, motivo }) — it never lets the exception leak through the HTTP route. Any OTHER error (a real defect) keeps propagating — it is not disguised as a command failure. Engine.Sessions.EngineApiClient.executar_comando_no_container/4 — the usual checklist (callback + delegator + Req.post impl + test fake), calling the new route. Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor gains run_no_container/4 (mold: run_via_runner/4), which calls the client above and maps the result to build_result/failed_result. A broker.exec failure NEVER becomes a crash nor a silent fallback to System.cmd outside the container. sucesso: false (the broker refused or did not answer) and an engine→api transport failure become a normal failed_result — clear message, exit_code: nil, exactly like any other command that failed. A container killed or removed from outside between the registered running and the moment of the call (RN-486: registered and observed never merge) IS that case — it is not a bug, it is the price of "registered" never being a guarantee. Falling back to System.cmd outside the container would reopen exactly the isolation-escape vector this PR exists to close.
documents.s: The new leg: engine → api → broker.exec

documents.t: InternalContainersController (the container-spec route) has an explicit comment: "sem @Post aqui, e isso não é esquecimento" — because whoever WRITES the container lifecycle is RegistrarTransicaoDeContainer, and giving the BROKER write authority there would confuse who decides the state. The new route differs on both axes that comment protects: the CALLER is the engine (not the broker reading from the api), and what it does is not write project_containers — it runs a command and returns the result. That is why it lives in InternalProjectsController, next to confirm-workspace-verification (another route the engine calls, not the broker).
documents.s: Why not in the broker's controller

documents.t: Hypothesis checked: confirmed. apps/broker/src/operacoes.ts, especificacaoDoProjeto/2, composes raizDoProjeto as ${PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT}/${workspaceDirName} — the SAME root (workspace_dir_name, RN-109) that Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/2 already uses to resolve <PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT>/<workspace_dir_name> inside the engine process. packages/docker-port/src/docker-cli.ts mounts that raizDoProjeto as the ONLY bind (${spec.raizDoProjeto}:${PONTO_DE_MONTAGEM}:rw, PONTO_DE_MONTAGEM = '/work'). That is: it is the SAME physical directory, only reached by two paths — from inside the engine, via PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT (a bind/volume on the engine side); from inside the freshly started container, via /work (a bind resolved by the daemon against PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT on the HOST). The worktree the dev agent already uses today — created the usual way, Workspace.ensure!/4 running System.cmd("git", ...) inside the engine process, writing to the shared volume — already appears INSIDE the container at /work, without Workspace.ensure!/4/ensure_remoto/2 changing AT ALL. The container is just one more observer of the SAME directory. This depends on PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT being configured correctly to point to the HOST path that makes the SAME physical folder that PROJECT_WORKSPACES_ROOT resolves inside the engine's container — that is the operator's responsibility (already documented in the comments of docker-compose.yml), and it remains so: nothing changes here.
documents.s: The dev agent's worktree ALREADY appears in /work — without changing Workspace.ensure!/4

documents.t: opts[:cwd] arrives at TerminalExecutor.run/3 as an ABSOLUTE HOST path (inside project_workspaces_root — the shared root, or the .worktrees/<agent_id> subdirectory of a specific dev agent, via Engine.Dev.WorktreeManager). run_no_container/4 translates that path into /work BEFORE sending it to the broker: it swaps the prefix <project_workspaces_root>/<workspace_dir_name> for /work, preserving the suffix. An absent cwd (runs at the workspace root) becomes nil — the broker defaults to /work. A cwd that is not inside that root (it should not happen for execution_mode: container) is sent as it came, without trying to guess — the broker refuses with DiretorioForaDoEscopoError if it is not inside /work, defense in depth instead of a silently fabricated path.
documents.s: cwd: translation from HOST to /work

documents.t: A terminal command whose scope is the project folder INSIDE the real container auto-approves — but that is a FLOOR, not a new ceiling, and the five absolute ceilings of decide.ts stay byte for byte as they were. Mechanism: ProposeActionUseCase.execute queries the SAME ObterCicloDeVidaDoContainerUseCase the execution uses (only when actionType === 'terminal' && project.executionMode === 'container' — sparing the query everywhere else) and builds containerExecutionActive in the DecideContext. Inside decide() (which remains PURE — zero IO), the INITIAL value of current stops being always { policy: 'require_approval', reason: 'default' } and becomes { policy: 'auto_approve', ... } when action.actionType === 'terminal' && ctx.containerExecutionActive. Why this is safe without duplicating the ceilings mechanism that already exists: every following stage (agent_autonomy, permissions.json) already REPLACES current when it has an explicit opinion — that is how the usual default require_approval could already be downgraded by an explicit deny or kept by an ask. Changing the INITIAL value does not change that property: an explicit agent_autonomy: deny, or a permissions.json with ask/deny matching the command, keep downgrading the container floor exactly as they already downgraded the default require_approval — it is not a new path, it is the same current with a different starting point. And the absolute ceilings (scope, git push/privileged command, protected merge, instruction_patch, parallelism) keep running AFTER, over current.policy === 'auto_approve' — including when that auto_approve came from the container floor, not from an explicit rule. The security justification is a boundary swap, not the absence of one. Outside the container, the terminal scope boundary (ADR 0055) is LEXICAL: terminalNoEscopo compares cwd/command against ctx.projectScopeRoot, a HOST path — and that check is what makes it safe to auto-approve by permissions.json allow today. Inside the real container, Docker's mount namespace is a STRONGER boundary: the process running the command physically does not see anything outside /work (it closes the symlink vector the comment of path-scope.ts records as open for mounted/runner, finding U — there there is no mount namespace at all, here there is). The /work validation the broker already does (DiretorioForaDoEscopoError, apps/broker/src/operacoes.ts) is the SECOND layer, over the already translated cwd. The lexical scope ceiling (terminalNoEscopo) keeps running on top of the floor, with no exception at all — it operates on the SAME HOST paths as always (the cwd/command that arrive at decide() are NEVER translated to /work; that translation happens only later, in the engine, when building the call to the broker) — it is defense in depth, not replacement: a command decide() would mark out of scope today stays marked out of scope with the floor on, and again requires a human decision. Why a FLOOR and not a seeded agent_autonomy rule: a seeded rule (like the auto mode of open_adr_pr) would need to be written/deleted every time the container goes up/down, and would diverge from what is REGISTERED in project_containers the instant the container fell from outside — the same two-sources-of-truth problem ADR 0130 already avoids by never merging registered and observed (RN-486). Querying the lifecycle at decision time is the SAME source the execution queries at execution time — zero synchronization between the two.
documents.s: Decision 3: autonomy inside the container

documents.t: ContainerBrokerPort.exec gets its FIRST real caller — the last of the five operations of ADR 0128/0130 without one. stop/remove remain without their own proposed_action, unchanged by this PR. mounted/runner still have no container at all — RN-421/RN-423 remain as they were; the structural containment gate of the join remains absent for those two modes (finding of ADR 0072, not closed here). The question "how many modules, a single container" remains as it is — project_id UNIQUE in project_containers, no change in this delivery. The lexical terminal scope (ADR 0055) loses no consumer. It remains the only boundary for mounted/runner (which have no mount namespace protecting them), and keeps running ON TOP of the container floor as a second layer — it was not replaced anywhere. Alternative considered and discarded: translating the cwd inside decide() too, to compare against /work. It would make the scope ceiling operate on the FINAL path, more "correct" in appearance — but it would move an INFRASTRUCTURE decision (where the broker mounted the volume) into a function the rest of the file deliberately keeps pure and without knowledge of any container, and would duplicate the cwd translation in two places (decide.ts and TerminalExecutor) that would need to agree forever. Discarded: the scope ceiling remains useful operating on the HOST paths it has always operated on — it is REDUNDANT with the mount namespace inside the container, not replaced by it, and redundancy that requires no synchronization is the defense in depth this ADR seeks.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Since PHASE 25 (ADR 0065/RN-105), a project's Code tab answers 409 while nobody has decided which container image it runs — artifact.project_image, emitted by the Arquiteto (Architect) (choose_project_image) and, since ADR 0133 (RN-491), also by Infra electing among candidates from the Arquiteto's own routing. The order is the user's: the container is what gives meaning to reading the code there, and releasing the read before there is somewhere to execute would teach that the gate is decorative. ADR 0072 (RN-169), revised by ADR 0104 (RN-421), exempted mounted/runner projects from that gate: since those two modes do not bring up their OWN container — the code lives in a user folder, mounted into the containers that already exist (mounted) or confirmed by a CLI running outside them (runner) — the original rule answered 409 forever in a project where the Arquiteto's decision was never going to happen. The exemption avoided closing the tab as a side effect. The original plan of this delivery ("Execution in a real container", Part 1) declared that exemption as decision #5 to reopen, already accepted before this PR existed: "RN-105 gate now applies in all THREE modes, container and Code tab. Accepted cost: exp001/exp002 lose the Code tab until the Arquiteto decides." This ADR executes that decision and records what it costs and what it does NOT change. The original exemption confused two questions that ADR 0130 (container broker) and ADR 0133 (Infra's election) separated, without the api having kept up: "does this project bring up a container on the SERVER?" (no, in mounted/runner — a question about MECHANISM) and "does it make sense to require that someone has decided the project's image before opening the code read?" (yes, in all three modes — a question about POLICY). The exemption answered the second question using the answer to the first.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: All THREE execution modes (container/mounted/runner) now require artifact.project_image decided before the Code tab opens. ReadProjectCodeUseCase.portaoDoContainer stops checking executionMode — the gate becomes unconditional, just as it already was unconditional within the container mode. ProjectCodeTab (web) stops treating mounted/runner as a special case: the three modes follow the same useQuery loading/error/sem_decisao/decided, which SIMPLIFIES the component — the modoLocal branch and the mode-conditional enabled disappear. Accepted cost, in so many words: every EXISTING mounted/runner project without a decided artifact.project_image — which includes real dogfooding projects of this repository, exp001 and exp002 — LOSES access to the Code tab the instant this PR is deployed, until the Arquiteto (or Infra) decides an image for it. That is an OPERATOR ACTION required AFTER the deploy, not a transparent fix users do not even notice — which is why the branch is born breaking/, not bugfix/, even though the content is a gap fix: the repository convention (CLAUDE.md) is explicit that content does not decide the prefix when the change requires operator action. The version goes up MAJOR as a mechanical consequence of scripts/ci/version.ts, not by manual decision — the number is not corrected afterwards. The container lifecycle (project_containers) also stops refusing by mode, but for a narrower reason. RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase answered 400 for any project outside the container mode — a check that actually belonged to the broker (which already refuses for its OWN, more specific reason), not to this use case. The 400 goes away; the table can now record a row for all three modes, through the SAME provisioning funnel that already read the image decision (now also required for mounted/runner). What remains IMPOSSIBLE, by deliberate decision, is mounted/runner actually reaching running. That is applied in a single place — ContainerBrokerPort.start() refuses with ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError (apps/broker/src/operacoes.ts): the broker runs on the SERVER and does not see the user folder where the code of mounted/runner lives, so composing a container there would be composing from an empty folder. That policy does NOT change in this PR — the error class's comment already pointed to this ADR ("o PR do portão nos três modos (1.7) revisita as duas ao mesmo tempo") and the review confirms it is right as it is. Investigated and decided, without a code change: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase calls ContainerBrokerPort.start() BEFORE any RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase.execute(..., 'provisioning') — if the broker refuses (the normal case for mounted/runner), the failure becomes container.start_failed with the reason named (BrokerRecusouError, NEVER a crash or a silent fallback) and the lifecycle transition is never called. That is: through the real approval path (container_start), no project_containers row is born for mounted/runner even with the per-mode 400 removed — the broker is already the effective gate, more precise than the old 400 (it knows WHETHER IT CAN compose the container; the use case only knew the MODE). That is why this PR does NOT add a second mode check in propose-action.use-case.ts nor in ExecuteContainerStartUseCase: duplicating it would create a second place to diverge from the first — the same lesson the broker's own comment already recorded. Also investigated: neither propose_container_start (the Infra Lead's tool, apps/engine/lib/engine/infra/tools/propose_container_start.ex) nor GetInfraContextUseCase restrict by executionMode today — the Infra Lead CAN propose container_start for a mounted/runner project, and the proposal only fails when someone approves and the broker refuses. That is a PRE-EXISTING gap (not introduced by this PR) that spends a human approval cycle on an action bound to fail — but it fails clearly, named, never silently. Fixing it would require touching the Infra Lead's prompt/instruction in the engine, outside the scope of this slice (API/domain); it is declared below, not fixed in passing.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: exp001/exp002 and any other mounted/runner project without a decided image lose the Code tab until someone runs the Arquiteto (or Infra's election) for them. This is the accepted cost of decision #5 of the original plan, not a side effect discovered later. The real containment against mounted/runner bringing up a container on the server did not change. It remains the broker (ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError), not a 400 from the api — in fact it BECAME more precise, because now a single place decides it instead of two. project_containers can, in theory, record a provisioning row for mounted/runner — but no production path today calls RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase.execute(..., 'provisioning') for those modes without first going through the broker, which refuses. If a new path some day bypasses ExecuteContainerStartUseCase (calling the use case directly), it inherits the same protection: obterImagem.execute still requires a decision, and nothing else changes here. The Infra Lead can propose container_start for a mounted/runner project knowing it will fail — a pre-existing gap, neither introduced nor closed by this PR, declared in CLAUDE.md ("Estado atual e aberto") so it is not lost. Alternative considered and discarded: adding the mode check in propose-action.use-case.ts or in ExecuteContainerStartUseCase, to refuse container_start for mounted/runner BEFORE calling the broker. It would avoid the wasted approval cycle cited above — but it would move knowledge about WHO can compose a container (today only the broker knows, via PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT) into the api, which lacks that context and would replicate a rule that already exists elsewhere. Discarded for now: the cost is an avoidable approval cycle, not incorrectness — and the failure message already names the cause. It stays recorded as a UX candidate, not as a bug fix, if the volume of futile proposals justifies it.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0130 (container broker) declared the five operations of the DockerPort — start/stop/remove/inspect/exec — and an explicit comment in ContainerBrokerPort: "stop/remove still have no caller: they are EXTERNAL EFFECTS and do not happen without their own proposed_action, which does not exist yet." ADR 0133/0134 (PRs 1.5/1.6) wired start/exec; this PR (1.8, the last of Part 1 of the "Execution in a real container" plan) closes the remaining gap, and delivers the screen that the comment on the ContainersController controller (per-project lifecycle route) already pointed to: "the global page that consumes it is another PR." Two concrete architectural decisions came up while designing that screen, and neither had a ready answer in the previous ADRs: The screen is CROSS-PROJECT — one row per workspace project that already has project_containers. The RECORDED state aggregates at no cost (it is a database read, same mold as ProjectsSummaryRepository), but the OBSERVED one — asking the broker for the current state, ADR 0130 — is a NETWORK call per project. Asking ALL of them without a ceiling would violate the CLAUDE.md rule: "a composite read that calls the provider N times has a budget and a cache, otherwise it becomes a traffic amplifier" (ADR 0060). container_remove is qualitatively different from container_start/ container_stop: it discards the container and forces reprovisioning from scratch. The original plan did not specify the exact caliber — only that the three actions are born as proposed_action.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: ObterVisaoGeralDeContainersUseCase only asks the broker (via ObterEstadoObservadoDoContainerUseCase, already existing) for rows whose RECORDED state is provisioning/running — a stopped/failed/removed container needs no confirmation from the daemon for the screen to make sense, and excluding them from the question is free (it is not the ceiling that protects them, it is eligibility). Among the eligible ones, at most TETO_DE_VERIFICACOES_POR_CARGA (20, a revisable NUMBER, not "all") are asked per load, in PARALLEL (Promise.all, never serially — chaining would multiply latency by the ceiling for nothing). Whatever falls outside either rule carries its OWN field, naoVerificado (fora_do_escopo_da_verificacao | teto_de_verificacoes_atingido) — never confused with naoObservado (broker-nao-configurado/broker-sem-resposta/broker-recusou, which already existed and means "the broker WAS asked and refused/did not answer"). A row outside the ceiling has all three observation fields (observado/ naoObservado/detalheDaObservacao) null — the screen never invents an answer the broker did not give. Why 20: today (PHASE 25b) no automatic provisioning exists — a container only comes up through a manually approved container_start — so the number of simultaneous provisioning/running containers tends to be small. 20 is a generous margin for the present, not a tight cut measured against real volume; revising the number is one line, not a migration.
documents.s: The ceiling on broker calls is by TWO rules, not one

documents.t: ContainersOverviewRepository/DrizzleContainersOverviewRepository follows the SAME mold as ProjectsSummaryRepository (RN-090): the first query joins projects with project_containers (INNER JOIN — only those that already HAVE a row enter, which is the screen's rule), the second fetches in batch the artifact.project_image events of the projects found (to resolve the image text of each FROZEN imageVersion — not the current one, which may have been revised after the container was born; decisaoNaVersao, domain/containers/project-container.ts, extracted from ObterContainerDoProjetoUseCase so as not to duplicate the validation/degrade logic), and the third fetches in batch the pending container proposed_actions of the same projects — which lets the screen swap the three action buttons for the inline ApprovalCard without a fourth query per project. A test (containers-overview.repository.spec.ts, same design as the ProjectsSummaryRepository one) proves the number of queries is EQUAL with 2 and with 20 projects.
documents.s: The RECORDED state aggregates in THREE constant queries, never one per project

documents.t: container_start (RN-491) and container_stop (RN-495) are maintainer, require_approval by default, and CAN be configured auto_approve — no decision is irreversible without reprovisioning: stopping a registered running container is a state one comes back from (stopped -> running). container_remove is different: it discards the container, and the state machine (container-lifecycle.ts) only leaves removed by PROVISIONING AGAIN — never "coming back to life". That is why container_remove enters the SAME absolute ceiling of decide.ts that already covers git push/privileged command (RN-418/ADR 0102): unconditional require_approval, even with "automatic mode" on, even with permissions.json configured — ApproveAlwaysActionUseCase refuses (400) to write the "always allow" pattern for it, closing the gap at the SOURCE, same mechanism as RN-418. ContainerBrokerPort.remove already was (since ADR 0128/0130, implemented in packages/docker-port) docker rm --force — it removes even a running container, in a single call. The state machine did NOT gain a running -> removed shortcut: ExecuteContainerRemoveUseCase records BOTH hops (stopped, then removed) when the recorded state still said running, reflecting what actually happened on the Docker side without widening the state machine by a route that would only exist for this use case.
documents.s: container_remove enters the absolute ceiling of decide.ts; container_stop follows the caliber of container_start

documents.t: Investigated and confirmed: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase already handles the complete dance from ANY state — provisioning/running (idempotent), stopped (jumps straight to running, without reprovisioning) and failed/removed/no row (reprovisions from scratch) — because it already exists to serve Infra's election (RN-491), which can also happen after the container has fallen. The screen (ContainersPage.tsx) builds the container_start payload from the project's CURRENT DECISION (GET .../container, the same route the Code tab reads) — image, network, resources — instead of inventing a new form; if the Arquiteto/Infra has not yet decided (it should not happen for a row that already exists, but the read degrades instead of assuming), the click fails with a named message, never proposes an empty payload. No backend change was necessary for this third button.
documents.s: "Bring it up again" REUSES container_start — it is not a fourth type

documents.t: The /containers page is the first cross-project read that combines the database (without N+1) with an external provider under budget (with an explicit ceiling). The pattern — eligibility first, ceiling after, an OWN absence reason never confused with the provider's reason — becomes available for the next composite read that needs the same discipline. stop/remove of the five operations of ADR 0128/0130 now have a real caller. Of the five, only inspect (read, without proposed_action) remains as it was; start/stop/exec already had a caller before this PR. container-lifecycle.ts had a docblock stating "no product service mounts /var/run/docker.sock" — false since ADR 0130 and even more false now; fixed in this PR, the same file it was already editing for another reason. The ceiling of 20 is a NUMBER, not a measurement. There is no production data about how many containers stay provisioning/running simultaneously — PHASE 25b never had automatic provisioning. If the volume grows, the number is revised; it needs no other architectural decision to change, only measurement that does not exist today (same rule declared for the RAG hybrid search weights, ADR 0080). container_remove is never auto-approvable, anywhere, forever — while this decision holds. This is deliberate: the only way to revert it would be another explicit architectural decision, not a configuration. Alternative considered and discarded: widening container-lifecycle.ts with a direct running -> removed transition. It would model what the broker DOES (remove forces), but would confuse what the state machine MODELS (the product's observable state) with what Docker allows as a mechanical shortcut — the machine would remain right about "what the api knows happened", and ExecuteContainerRemoveUseCase already solves this by recording both hops without touching the domain shared by the whole rest of the system (including container_start, which depends on the same machine). Alternative considered and discarded: a ceiling on broker calls based on cache/TTL instead of per-load counting. A cache would reduce calls on quick successive loads, but would introduce a window in which the observed state can be stale WITHOUT the screen knowing — which RN-468 forbids (an environment signal says what it KNOWS, never fakes freshness it does not have). The per-load ceiling is simpler and more honest: each load says exactly what it asked.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: The image gate (RN-105) has applied in all THREE execution modes since RN-494 (ADR 0135): mounted/runner need a decided artifact.project_image for the Code tab to open, exactly like container. What RN-494 left declared, in so many words: "what does not come up is the container itself — mounted/runner still have no container of their own on the server." This is the PR that closes that half, but not on the SERVER side — on the USER side. Today, a project in runner/mounted mode executes EVERY terminal command directly on the user's machine (child_process, no isolation at all) — the same brabo-runner that already keeps the Phoenix channel terminal:<projectId> (ADR 0103/0104) and already knows how to TALK to ITS Docker (@brabo/docker-port, proven by --self-test-docker since ADR 0128, with no real consumer until now). The broker (apps/broker, ADR 0130) already provides that isolation for the container mode, bringing up a container on the SERVER — but it will NEVER bring up a container for mounted/runner: their code lives in a USER folder the server does not see (ModoDeExecucaoNaoSuportadoError, apps/broker/src/operacoes.ts). The only process that sees that folder is the runner itself, on the machine of whoever has the folder.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: container_start/container_stop/container_remove gain a SECOND execution path, branched by the project's executionMode — container stays through the broker, mounted/runner now ask the connected RUNNER, via the SAME Phoenix channel that already exists.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: apps/runner/src/channel.ts already had the exact pattern for "server asks the runner something, runner answers, correlated by ref, with timeout": exec/exec_result, on the runner side; Engine.Runners.RunnerRouter.exec/4 + EngineWeb.TerminalChannel (handle_info({:dispatch_exec, ...}) + handle_in("exec_result", ...)), on the engine side. This PR REPLICATES that pattern, three times — it never invents a new one: container_start/container_start_result container_stop/container_stop_result container_remove/container_remove_result On the engine side, RunnerRouter gains start_container/3, stop_container/3 and remove_container/3, factored over a common private dispatch/5 (the three differed only in the event atom and the result atom — exec/4 keeps its own code, untouched). TerminalChannel gains four handle_info({:dispatch_container_*, ...}) (despachar_pedido/6, a mold common with dispatch_exec) and three handle_in("container_*_result", ...) (responder_pedido_pendente/3, which now also serves exec_result — the same pending_execs, a generic ref→from map that neither knows nor needs to know WHICH request is pending). On the runner side, channel.ts gains the three message types + enviarContainerStartResult/Stop/Remove; RunnerChannelHandlers gains onContainerStart/onContainerStop/onContainerRemove; index.ts gains tratarContainerStart/Stop/Remove, which call DockerViaCli — the SAME port the broker uses on the server side (packages/docker-port, ADR 0130), with the USER's Docker.
documents.s: Reuse of the exec/exec_result pair, three times

documents.t: ApiToEngineClient (the port the api already uses for executeTerminalAction, synchronous) gains startContainerViaRunner/ stopContainerViaRunner/removeContainerViaRunner. EngineWeb.ContainerCommandController (POST internal/projects/:projectId/containers/{start,stop,remove}) is the only caller on the engine side — it forwards to RunnerRouter and never writes project_containers (whoever writes remains RegistrarTransicaoDeContainerUseCase, on the api side, after the call returns). The engine's answer is ALWAYS 200 — same discipline as ActionCommandController/ExecutarComandoNoContainerUseCase (ADR 0134): sucesso: false in the BODY, never an HTTP error status, for the two causes that are NORMAL failure — no runner connected/timeout (motivoCodigo), and the runner having tried and refused (Docker unavailable on the user's machine, invalid specification). HttpApiToEngineClient throws RunnerNaoConectadoError only in the first case, RunnerRecusouContainerError in the second — the three use cases catch BOTH together (same reasoning as BrokerRecusouError/BrokerIndisponivelError) and record failed with the reason, never let it propagate.
documents.s: The new HTTP path: api → engine → runner

documents.t: ExecuteContainerStartUseCase (ADR 0133) elects a candidate image from the Arquiteto's routing and emits a new version of artifact.project_image (DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase, decidedBy: 'infra-lead') BEFORE asking the broker to bring it up — that is specific to the container path, and the mounted/runner path does NOT repeat that step. It only READS the CURRENT decision via ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase — the SAME use case that already composes GET .../container-spec for the broker (ADR 0130), called DIRECTLY, without HTTP, because ExecuteContainerStartUseCase and ObterSpecDeContainerUseCase run in the same api process. Without a decided image (RN-105), it fails BEFORE asking the engine — the same gate that already applies to the other three parts of the product. The payload that travels to the runner (EspecificacaoDeContainerParaRunner) is the SAME fields as EntradaDeEspecificacao (packages/docker-port) MINUS raizDoProjeto — the runner fills that field itself, with estado.dir. That is not bandwidth saving: it is the decision that NO host path travels from the server to the runner, for the same reason none travels from the server to the broker (apps/broker, ADR 0130) — whoever knows the REAL path is whoever is on the machine.
documents.s: The image: READ, never ELECTED again

documents.t: Finding confirmed by reading the code: decisao_de_execucao/1 already routes UNCONDITIONALLY every command of a VERIFIED and CONNECTED runner project to RunnerRouter.exec/4 (RN-423, ADR 0104) — it does not ask "is there a container?", only "is there a runner?". The decision "run on the host or inside the container I brought up" is INTERNAL to the runner, not to the engine, and so the engine does not need to know it exists. What changes is only apps/runner/src/index.ts: EstadoDoRunner gains containerAtivo: string | null (the NAME of the container THIS runner brought up — brabo-<workspaceDirName> — or null); tratarExec now checks that field — with an active container, it runs via DockerViaCli.exec(nome, { comando, cwd }); without one, it falls back to the usual path (executarComando directly on the host). cwd (already validated by validarCwdDentroDaRaiz against the project root) is translated into /work by PREFIX swap (cwdParaContainer(raiz, cwd, pontoDeMontagem), guard.ts) — same reasoning as cwd_para_container/2 on the engine side (RN-492, ADR 0134): the root becomes the mount point, the rest of the path stays the same. containerAtivo survives channel reconnections (it is part of estado, which persists across the while of main()) — the Docker container itself does not fall when the WebSocket falls, and the runner should not "forget" it because of a reconnection.
documents.s: Engine.Actions.TerminalExecutor did NOT gain a new outcome

documents.t: The original plan recorded the question: does the container's bind-mount need a second "valid mount path" validation? Confirmed it does not, by reading the whole of guard.ts. estado.dir ALREADY is the confirmed root — validated by validarDirDentroDoHomeNoLinux (RN-434, refuses --dir outside $HOME on Linux) and by garantirDiretorio (RN-435), both at CLI STARTUP, BEFORE any channel connects or any container comes up. The container mount IS estado.dir, period — there is not (nor does there need to be) a second check like caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido on the runner side. RN-434 "now also covers the mounted path" only because the mount uses the SAME variable it already validated, not because anything new was written.
documents.s: guard.ts/RN-434 already covers the mount, with no new code

documents.t: packages/docker-port gains REAL USE on the runner side — before only proven by --self-test-docker (ADR 0112/0128); now DockerViaCli.start/stop/ exec are actually called, with the user's Docker. The FIVE operations of the DockerPort still have no sixth — start/ stop/remove/inspect/exec remain the same five; this PR only gives them a SECOND consumer (the runner, besides the broker), never a new field in the specification. mounted gains the SAME path as runner — the branching in the three use cases is by executionMode !== 'container', not by executionMode === 'runner'; mounted can now also bring up its own container, as long as it has a connected runner (brabo-runner runs the same in both modes, RN-169/RN-421/RN-422). The structural containment of the join (broker, ADR 0055) remains absent for mounted/runner — the symlink vector ADR 0055 already recorded remains open; what this PR closes is the LACK of any isolation, not a boundary as strong as the server's. guard.ts remains best-effort, by invariant — not a gap of this PR. Exclusivity by {project_id, machine_id} remains deferred (gap already declared in CLAUDE.md, ADR 0104) — two runners connected to the same project remain impossible through the Registry's exclusivity (:global), not through a container check. Alternative considered and discarded: re-electing the image on the mounted/runner path too, calling DecidirImagemDoProjetoUseCase. It would make the two paths symmetric in appearance, but would force the container_start payload to carry network/resources/rationale even when nobody uses them (the runner does not need them: it only reads the current decision). Discarded: the mounted/runner path already has the image decision — someone decided EARLIER, through the Arquiteto or Infra, the usual way — and re-electing here would duplicate a decision that already exists, with no new candidate to elect between.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: ADR 0132 (Stage 2 of the measurable RAG program) closed with a declared Consequence: CI wiring is TODO(humano), same as QA. Without an API LLM secret or new infra (real Ollama in CI), the golden-set runs MANUALLY — mix golden_set.rag — and never in a normal mix test. And the rag-acertivo gate (docs/gates.yml) was born severidade: warn, with the comment saying exactly why: "there is no CI with an LLM... block would promise an automatic lock that does not exist". This is Stage 3, decided by the product owner in this session: wire the RAG golden-set into CI. The question that was still open — every PR or scheduled — was also decided in this session: scheduled, given the cost of pulling nomic-embed-text (~274MB) and running the real search against the curated corpus (a few minutes) in every CI window. The QA golden-set (ADR 0123) does not change at all here — it remains exactly TODO(humano), for the reason the next section makes precise.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The TODO(humano) of ADR 0123 lists the missing alternative: "a runner with a GPU, an Ollama pull step". That sentence hides a difference that matters: the QA golden-set calls a chat model doing judgment — expensive, it measures something inherently non-deterministic (ADR 0123 itself records real runs with qwen2.5-coder:latest varying from 1 to 5 hits out of 6, between executions). The RAG golden-set only calls the embedding model (nomic-embed-text, ~137M parameters) — CPU is enough, no GPU, and embedding does not sample: the same input always produces the same vector. ubuntu-latest, with no GPU at all, is enough infrastructure for this golden-set — it would not be for the QA one.
documents.s: Why the RAG one is tractable and the QA one still is not

documents.t: apps/api/scripts/seed-golden-set-rag.ts opens its own NestFactory.createApplicationContext(AppModule) — it never talks to an api already running as a server. The four secrets the api would refuse with an example literal in production (AUTH_JWT_SECRET, BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN, CREDENTIALS_MASTER_KEY, GIT_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET — RN-114, ADR 0059) are only checked when NODE_ENV === 'production' (apps/api/src/infrastructure/security/{oauth-state-secret,auth-key-material,service-token}.ts, envelope-encryption.service.ts). The script never sets NODE_ENV — neither it nor mix golden_set.rag, which invokes it via System.cmd — so the four fall into the development branch and use the dev literal without complaint. Unlike docker/smoke.sh, which brings up docker-compose.prod.yml with NODE_ENV=production ON PURPOSE and therefore needs to generate the four with openssl rand — this workflow needs no generated secret at all.
documents.s: The obstacle that did not exist: no secret needs to be generated

documents.t: A new workflow, separate from ci.yml. .github/workflows/ci.yml is deliberately pull_request only (comment at the top of the file itself): mixing schedule there would affect every existing job, with no per-job filter. .github/workflows/golden-set-rag.yml is born with schedule (daily cron) + workflow_dispatch (runs on demand — useful to validate this very change and after calibrating the search's weight/threshold, ADR 0080, or the curated corpus). services: postgres + services: ollama, the same pinned versions as the rest of the product. pgvector/pgvector:pg16 (same as the test-engine of ci.yml) and ollama/ollama:0.33.1 — the SAME version pinned in docker/docker-compose.yml. Ollama version parity is what keeps test/fixtures/golden_set_rag/floor.json (keyed by MODEL, not by environment) valid when running in CI: an Ollama different from the one that generated the local floor could produce subtly different embeddings and change the rank of a borderline case, without that being a real regression. The Ollama health-check uses ollama list, not curl. --health-cmd runs INSIDE the service container, and the official image does not guarantee having curl — it only guarantees having the ollama binary itself. docker/ollama/pull-models.sh (the reference logic, already validated with a real model download) uses exactly that waiting pattern (until ollama list >/dev/null 2>&1); this workflow reuses the same command as the health-cmd instead of inventing a new waiting mechanism. The model is pulled by a direct HTTP call, POST /api/pull, from the RUNNER side (not from inside the container). curl on the ubuntu-latest runner is guaranteed (already used in several ci.yml steps to download a gate binary). stream:false makes the call block until complete and return the final JSON — no polling loop. It is the SAME endpoint the ollama pull binary calls underneath (docker/ollama/pull-models.sh documents this: "a CLI ollama usa HTTP contra ${OLLAMA_HOST}/api/*"), just without going through the CLI wrapper, which is not installed on the runner. Explicit migration before the seed. main.ts/app.module.ts migrate nothing on their own at boot — confirmed by reading apps/api/src/db/migrate.ts, a separate script. The job runs pnpm --filter api db:migrate before mix golden_set.rag. docs/gates.yml: rag-acertivo remains severidade: warn. Deliberate, not forgotten — see Consequences. evidencia.tipo changes from teste to ci (same format as the backmerge gate), with workflow pointing to the new file.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: warn remains warn — by a cadence decision, not a technical limitation, and that difference is what this ADR changes relative to 0132. The gate actually RUNS in CI now; what does not exist is a PR blocked by it. A search accuracy regression shows up up to 24h after being merged (or right away, via a manual workflow_dispatch), never at PR time — a trade-off explicitly accepted by the product owner, given the cost of ~3-6min per execution (model pull + indexing + 17 searches) that running on every PR would impose. The QA golden-set (ADR 0123) does not change at all here. It remains entirely manual, TODO(humano) — the asymmetry (deterministic CPU embedding vs. expensive, non-deterministic chat judgment) is deliberate and explained above, not an inconsistency to fix later. The curated corpus gap remains open. The 17 questions keep measuring retrieval over the same 22 curated files of ADR 0132, not the 130+ real ADRs — this stage wires the MECHANISM into CI, it does not widen what it measures. Widening the corpus remains an embedding-cost decision in a manual run, declared separately. New risk, and where it lives. The business logic (seed script, accuracy criterion, ExUnit test) was already proven — 17/17, twice, according to ADR 0132. What is genuinely new here is the workflow ORCHESTRATION (two services, step order, model pull by direct HTTP), which cannot be tested end to end outside real GitHub Actions. Recommended to the user: trigger a manual workflow_dispatch as soon as this PR merges, to confirm the job is green before waiting for the first scheduled window.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: The policy has always said that promotion is --no-ff (branching-policy.md): "a squash would flatten the lower step's commits, and the stage's tag would end up pointing to a commit that no longer exists". The rule was broken three times — #367 (2026-08-24), #394 (2026-08-25) and #464 (2026-09-04) — and the third was the most expensive of all, because it was precisely the PR that fixed the first two. What was discovered while investigating was not a detection hole. It was the opposite: The check existed and worked. tag-release has failed a merge into qa without a second parent since 2026-07-27, and the log of the 2026-08-25 run says, in so many words: [tag-release] o merge em `qa` não é merge commit (1 pai) ##[error]o merge em `qa` não é merge commit (1 pai) It fired on both squashed promotions. And the history stayed broken all the same, for 293 commits, until the following promotion opened with 11 files in "conflict" that were not conflicts — only lost ancestry. What was missing was WHOM to alert. A push workflow that fails on a permanent branch has no PR where it can turn red: the merge already happened. What remains is a run in the Actions tab, which nobody opens because nothing says it exists. The repository had zero issues in its entire history — the channel did not exist. Detection without an address is an alarm ringing in an empty room.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: It was the first way out considered, and it is the only one with an absolute guarantee: allow_squash_merge: false makes the button cease to exist. It was measured and rejected, with the number in hand: the six most recent merges into dev are single-parent squashes — squash is the work-PR convention here —, and scripts/changelog.mjs generates the CHANGELOG with git log --no-merges, counting on that: today a squash is one line; with a merge commit, every intermediate WIP commit would become an entry. Turning off squash fixes promotion by taxing every work PR and touching changelog generation. The problem is the pipeline's; the bill would be paid by the work. It is recorded what also does not work, so nobody looks again: merge queue would solve it with a fixed method per queue, and CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids it; and GitHub's native per-branch control in this space is required_linear_history, which does the inverse — it forbids merge commits. There is no "require merge commit" per branch.
documents.s: Why not simply turn off squash

documents.t: 1. The alarm gains a job with a recipient. tag-release.yml gains avisar, if: failure(), which opens an issue naming branch, commit, run and the fix — and comments on the already open issue instead of opening a second one for the same branch, because a flood of identical issues is the fastest way to teach someone to ignore them. The title is a deduplication key, pinned by a test (tituloDoAlarme). It authenticates with github.token, never with the PAT: an invalid BRABO_BOT_TOKEN is one of the failures it needs to report (the checkout dies with could not read Username), and an alarm that depends on what may be broken is an alarm that goes silent exactly when it needs to ring. The body goes via --body-file, never interpolated into a run: — the text has backticks and $, and interpolating content inside bash -e is injection. 2. The rule now covers dev, and the coverage is NARROW. dev receives work all the time and by squash on purpose, so "one parent is a defect" does not hold there — it would fail every PR. What is a defect in dev is the PR that brought a new edge: its head was a merge whose second parent was not yet in the base. That was #464, whose entire delivery was that edge. The distinction matters because there is an almost identical and benign neighbor: the work PR that pulled dev into itself before merging also has a merge as head — but the second parent is already in the base, and the squash loses nothing. 3. The query that identifies the PR is by merge_commit_sha, and that is not style. gh api repos/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls returns every PR associated with the commit — and since dev is the head of the promotion PR that stays open the whole cycle, every dev commit comes associated with it. Reading .[0].head.ref would return dev (a permanent branch) for any work-PR squash, and the rule would fail the entire repository. The mistake was made and caught by checking against real data before shipping; it is written down so it does not come back. 4. null is an answer, and in dev it does not become a defect. Not being able to know whether there was an edge (API down, PR deleted, object missing in the clone) is different from knowing there was not. In dev it passes, because the base rate is legitimate work. In qa/main nothing changes: only the pipeline enters there, and one parent is a defect with or without a known origin. It is deliberately the inverse of the promotion-check doctrine ("an impossible check counts as failed") — there the universe is only promotion, here it is not.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: This does not prevent, and the distinction is the point. The method is chosen at the click; truly preventing it would require one of the two exits rejected above, or taking the merge out of the human's hand — which runs into the CLAUDE.md rule that a merge into a protected branch is always manual. What changes is the discovery time: from "in the next promotion cycle" to "one minute later, in an issue with an owner", when reverting is still trivial. Prevention remains open, and it is a product decision. The exit that solves it without taxing the work is promote.yml — which already exists, is already workflow_dispatch and already has the pipeline pair as input — performing the git merge --no-ff itself. That preserves authority (nothing merges without a human triggering it) and mechanizes only the method, but it requires deciding whether a human dispatch counts as a "manual merge" in the CLAUDE.md sense, and it would open a third exception to "never push directly to a permanent branch". It was not taken here. Verified against real data, not by reasoning. The rule was run against the three commits that motivated it: it fails bf6db00c9 (the squash of #464) and passes 1eb71c322 and 108d81cc7 (normal work PRs) — no false positive. A finding along the way, and outside this ADR's reach: BRABO_BOT_TOKEN has been invalid or expired since the night of 2026-09-03, and so no tag is being stamped on any branch — the tag-release checkout fails before any logic. Only rotating the secret solves it, and that is TODO(humano). Recorded in CLAUDE.md.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: On 2026-09-04 the npm advisories endpoint (POST registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/security/advisories/bulk) was intermittent for hours. The Auditoria de dependências job failed on four distinct PRs (#464, #466, #396, #468), always with the same signature: [WARN] POST .../security/advisories/bulk error (23). Will retry in 10 seconds. 2 retries left. [WARN] POST .../security/advisories/bulk error (503). Will retry in 1 minute. 1 retries left. TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout It was not the dependency tree, it was not the runner and it was none of the PRs. It was reproduced outside CI, hitting the endpoint directly from another machine: the same lack of response within 20s, while an ordinary GET on the same registry answered in 130ms. pnpm audit already retries three times internally (the two retry lines above); the service simply did not answer. The cost was not only time. It was the behavior the situation teaches: each such failure is resolved by re-running the job until it passes, and whoever learns to re-run until it passes also re-runs when the red is real. A gate that shouts without reason does not stay neutral — it erodes trust in the gates that shout with reason.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: Product owner's decision: three attempts without a registry response are an ACCEPTED RISK. The job stays green, with a loud warning in the summary. What the decision does not loosen, and is what makes it defensible: situation verdict retry pnpm audit exits 0 passes — vulnerability report fails none — the answer already came, and it is no request did not complete (timeout/5xx/DNS/socket) infra up to 3 3 infras in a row passes, declared — unrecognized output fails none Precedence is the heart of this. scripts/ci/auditoria-de-dependencias.ts classifies the output, and the FINDING markers are tested before the network ones: a report that happens to mention timeout — a package with that name, a timeout CVE — cannot be forgiven as unavailability. There is a test for exactly that case. An unknown failure fails (fail closed). If the output matches neither signature, the verdict is achado. The only thing worse than a gate that fails too much is one that approves what it did not understand. The warning says what the execution does NOT assert. When the risk is accepted, the job summary records that the tree was not audited — never that it is clean. Green due to unavailability and green due to a clean audit are different states, and the job does not confuse them in the text. The logic lives in a testable script, not in bash inside the YAML: the classification is a pure function with 11 cases, including the REAL outputs of run 33838507158 (the one that motivated everything) instead of paraphrases.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: There is a real risk window, and it is declared. During a long npm outage, PRs get in without a dependency audit. This is recorded in cadeia-de-suprimentos-do-ci.md, in the section "What is still trusted on faith", next to the other assumed trusts — not hidden in a workflow comment. The alternative was measured before being rejected. Staying red due to a third-party outage cost, on the day, four blocked PRs and several re-runs of ~5min each, without any of them discovering anything about the code. What this rigidity buys is the appearance of rigor; what it costs is the habit of ignoring red. Only the pnpm side changes. mix hex.audit and mix deps.audit (Elixir) remain as they were — the incident was the npm endpoint's, and widening the exception to those who did not ask for it would turn a one-off decision into a general policy. What remains unanswered: there is no alert when the risk is accepted frequently. Three timeouts in an isolated PR is third-party noise; three timeouts in every PR for a week is the gate turned off in practice, and today nothing distinguishes the two cases beyond someone noticing. It remains a declared gap, not solved here.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: The mounted mode (the old local, ADR 0072/RN-169, renamed by ADR 0104/RN-421) keeps the project's code in a USER folder, and that folder needs to be reachable from inside TWO containers: the api, which reads and writes the permissions.json and serves the Code tab, and the engine, which builds the worktree and writes the code. The mechanism, since the beginning, is a bind-mount. What was never decided is who creates that bind-mount, and when. What existed was an INSTRUCTION: docker/docker-compose.yml carried, in the api and engine services, a large comment teaching how to add by hand one line per project — - /home/voce/projetos/loja:/home/voce/projetos/loja — and project creation refused with 400 (RN-170/RN-422) when the folder was not there, with the message repeating that line. The refusal is good and still exists; the problem is the price of the remedy it teaches. One compose edit and one restart of api + engine PER PROJECT CREATED. Restarting those two services kills every agent turn in progress, every open terminal socket and every in-flight LLM call, across the whole installation — to onboard one project. That was tolerable while mounted was an escape hatch for those who already knew what they were doing. It stops being so the moment it becomes a first-class choice, offered on the creation screen with a suggested path. And there is a second problem, which the path suggestion makes concrete. The rule "the project folder cannot overlap the Brabo checkout", which is the heart of ADR 0055, is enforced by caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido comparing against raizDoBrabo() — which is process.cwd(), and inside the api's container is /workspace. The REAL checkout, on the developer's disk, the api has no way of knowing. Whoever clones Brabo into $HOME/brabo and points the project folder there passes every existing validation, and the dev agents start running commands inside the product's own tree — exactly the failure ADR 0055 exists to prevent, coming in through a door it does not guard.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: A SINGLE base, configured by the operator, mounted by IDENTITY in the api and engine services. # .env BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE=/home/voce/brabo # docker/docker-compose.yml — serviços api E engine - ${BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE:-brabo_projects_base}:${BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE:-/data/brabo-projects-base} The operator configures it once, runs docker compose up -d api engine, and nothing else is ever edited per project. Every mounted project lives inside the base. The ${VAR:-nome_de_volume} trick on the left, with an absolute and inert default on the right, is the SAME already used by PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR/ GIT_LOCAL_REPOS_HOST_DIR on the neighboring lines: without the variable, the left side is the name of a named volume declared at the end of the file, the line remains valid Compose, and nothing is mounted from the host. Without the variable, the api reports projectsBase: null (GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/projects-base, maintainer — the same minimum as POST .../projects, because this value exists to decide what that route offers) and the creation wizard does not offer the Mounted folder mode. Never offer a mode the installation does not honor.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: There is a variable that already swaps a managed volume for a real host folder, and the temptation to reuse it is great. There are three reasons not to, and the first has a data consequence. 1. Namespace collision, with git init in someone else's folder. A managed workspace is named by workspace_dir_name (RN-109), a UNIQUE column; a mounted project is named by the USER, who types the path. With both roots pointing to the same place, <base>/loja and a container project whose workspace_dir_name is loja land in the SAME physical folder — and Workspace.init_from_bare! would git init inside another person's project. Nothing in the schema prevents it: uniqueness is among workspace_dir_name values, never against the basename of workspace_path, and there is no way it could be, because one side is chosen by the product and the other by whoever types. 2. Opposite ownership semantics. /data/project-workspaces belongs to the PRODUCT: disposable, opaque, and that is what makes it acceptable for a container project to be deleted with the volume. The base belongs to the USER — it is where their code lives, open in their editor, versioned by them. Merging the two would make the documentation have to say "this folder is disposable and also is not". 3. The base is browsable; the managed root must not be. The folder browser served by the api (next PR) is scoped to the base, so the user can choose where the project will live. Conflating the two would expose the interior of every container project of the installation to anyone creating some project.
documents.s: Why a NEW variable, and not PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR

documents.t: A fixed mount — ${BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE}:/data/mounted — would be shorter to write, and it is wrong for two reasons that add up. The projects.workspace_path string is typed by the user and shown back to them (AmbienteDoProjeto). With host ≠ container, the product would have to choose which of the two to store, and any choice makes the screen lie to someone: storing the inside path would show a folder that does not exist on their machine; storing the outside one would require translating at every point of use. And it is precisely that translation that identity makes unnecessary. projectScopeRoot (api) and Engine.Actions.Workspace.workspace_dir/2 (engine) discriminate the mode by the path's leading slash and use the column's value as is. With host == container, both remain correct without a single new line of code — and the terminal scope of ADR 0055, which is derived from that same root, keeps authorizing exactly the folder the user sees.
documents.s: Why IDENTITY ($X:$X), and not a fixed mount point

documents.t: BRABO_PROJECTS_HOST_BASE enters the broker service derived from BRABO_PROJECTS_BASE (which is already a host path by definition — it is what api/engine mount by identity), next to PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_ROOT and for the same reason as ADR 0130: the -v of a docker run is resolved by the DAEMON, against the host filesystem, and a path coming from inside the api would mount an empty folder. Containment remains configured in the broker, never asserted by the caller — which is that ADR's real invariant. Nothing consumes this variable yet: whoever resolves a mounted project against that root is the PR that gives a container to the Mounted folder mode.
