Signing each binary would produce five signature artifacts to verify and five ways for the verification to end up half done; a signed manifest covers the set with a single verification, and it is the format any consumer knows how to read. checksums.txt is born in the same job that already waits for the Release to exist (build-runner-binaries.yml:213-221, the loop with a 600s ceiling), and the matrix remains fail-fast: false: a target that did not build does not prevent the others from publishing, but the manifest declares which targets it covers — a checksums that lists four binaries and is silent about the fifth would be worse than none.
documents.s: 2. One signed checksums.txt, not five signatures

documents.t: consumer verifies when it fails install.sh (ADR 0150) the image signature by digest; the signed checksums.txt before using the binary named refusal — says which artifact, which check, and stops GET /runner-releases/binary only the binary's SHA-256 against the checksums.txt of the same Release — not its signature (see below) 502 with motivo; never serves unverified bytes local build (ADR 0150) the git tag and a clean tree refuses before building A verification failure is a refusal, never a warning. A warning that can be accepted by clicking is a verification that does not exist — and the product already applies that rule elsewhere, when consentir-base.mjs:246-258 refuses to write and exits with 1 if sharing was not proven. Absence of what would be verified is also a refusal: a Release without checksums.txt makes the proxy refuse, and not serve while declaring it could not check — otherwise deleting 400 bytes from the Release would turn off verification for everyone. The api proxy verifies INTEGRITY, not provenance — and that is a decision, not an omission​ The second row of the table was born written as if the two halves were one. In session 3 they were separated, after measuring the two ways the api could verify a signature: path measured why not cosign inside the api image 155 MB (cosign-linux-amd64 v2.6.1) it almost doubles a runtime image that is Alpine + Node, published by digest on GHCR (ADR 0119), to verify an optional download @sigstore/verify + @sigstore/tuf 2.5 MB, 12 packages, no advisory size is not the cost. getTrustedRoot() refreshes TUF metadata against tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev (the package's seeds.json only seeds the root.json), so a @Public() route that today depends on ONE third-party host would come to depend on two — and it is the entry point of the onboarding of ADR 0118. Worse: by the rule of ADRs 0041/0042 — a capability is only declared when proven — there is no way to prove the path today, because no Release has a checksums.txt.bundle: the checksums job only runs on a final tag, and the gap is already declared in RN-524 on the signing side. Shipping a verification that cannot be proven in front of onboarding would trade a known weakness for a 502 on every platform, in every installation, discovered only in production So the proxy checks the hash and says it is only the hash — in the docblock, in the OpenAPI description, in the refusal message and in RN-525. Whoever verifies the signature is install.sh, which has real cosign through the path of decision 4. The consequence is recorded and not hidden: BRB-005 closes for producing the signature and remains open for the provenance half of this route — reopening it is the decision of a later session, with a real signed Release to prove against.
documents.s: 3. Who verifies, and what happens when it fails

documents.t: Verifying requires the cosign binary on the installer's machine, and downloading it without verification would recreate the problem one level up. install.sh solves this through the path CI already uses for every third-party binary: it downloads the pinned version and checks it with sha256sum -c against a hash written in the versioned script itself (ci.yml:201 is the precedent). Whoever trusts install.sh enough to execute it trusts the hash it carries; the chain does not get more fragile than the link that starts it.
documents.s: 4. The cosign that verifies also needs provenance

documents.t: A hand-managed key (own pair, KMS, GPG): custody and rotation of a CI secret, for a gain of nothing keyless does not give here. "Sign now, verify later." A signature without a consumer is one more file in the Release. The three consumers in the table above enter in this phase, and the install.sh one is what gives it meaning. Signing the image by tag. A tag is a moving pointer; the digest is what .release/images.json already records and what the overlay already applies. SBOM attestation and full SLSA provenance. Declared out of scope: they are another axis, with another consumer, and none of them removes BRB-005.
documents.s: What this ADR explicitly rejects

documents.t: BRB-005 closes for images and binaries — and only for them. The register (BRB register) receives the evidence when session 2 merges. And it does not close for the provenance half of the api proxy. By decision 3, GET /runner-releases/binary checks integrity against the manifest and refuses what it cannot check, but does not verify the manifest's signature — both ways of doing it were measured and rejected (155 MB of cosign in the image; a second third-party host on a public route, verifying what does not yet exist to be proven). The BRB register says so instead of announcing the item closed. The broker remains unsigned because it remains unpublished. docker-bake.hcl:81-83 has four targets and scripts/ci/images-manifest.ts:54 accepts four; brabo-broker:prod only exists built locally. The consequence belongs to ADR 0150 and is declared there: in a GHCR installation, the container-broker profile is unreachable — and the mounted mode brings up a container through the broker (ADR 0144). release.yml gains one more permission. id-token: write is scoped to the workflow and does not widen what it could already do with packages: write. Whoever installs without network access to Sigstore cannot verify — and, by decision 3, does not install. It is the accepted cost of verification not being optional.

documents.t: Proposed. Depends on ADR 0149: without a signature, this document proposes exactly what PHASE 28 refused.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: Installing Brabo today requires a checkout, five secrets exported by hand and knowledge that is nowhere — the three gestures that the phase document describes. Three facts on disk constrain any installer design: The production compose is not an installation manifest. All the services of docker/docker-compose.prod.yml point to brabo-*:prod with a local build: block (:102-105, :144-147, :253-256, :381-384); there is not a single reference to ghcr.io in docker/. The file's header says of itself, at :1 and :8, that it is the "compose de VALIDAÇÃO das imagens de produção" and that "o que este arquivo NÃO é: um manifesto de produção endurecido". The only consumer of .release/images.json in the repository is scripts/ci/aplicar-imagens.ts, which writes to a kustomize overlay (Makefile:35-36). There is already a consent mold, and it is rigid in the right place. scripts/dev/consentir-base.mjs:195-208: without a TTY, the script reports and returns 0 — it does not consent, does not write, does not create a folder. And its order is law: validarBase runs before any mkdir (:228-242), writing to the .env is the last step (:272), and a proof that fails refuses without writing (:246-258). The five secrets are already generated somewhere. docker/smoke.sh:31-57 generates the five with openssl rand, respecting an already exported value (${VAR:-$(gerar)}), including the detail that NEO4J_PASSWORD must be -hex because / breaks the parse of NEO4J_AUTH (:53-56). There is no need to invent that part, only to make it persistent.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: sh -c "$(curl -fsSL https://github.com/daneiel/brabo/releases/latest/download/install.sh)" And not curl … | sh. The reason is mechanical, not aesthetic: with the script arriving through the pipe, the process's stdin is the download, and a read to ask anything reads bytes of the script itself or hits EOF. An installer that cannot ask would have to choose on its own where to create folders on someone's computer — and the repository's rule is the opposite (consentir-base.mjs:195-208). Without a TTY the installer reports and exits, in the same format as the mold: it prints what it would do, what it found, and the command to run in a terminal.
documents.s: 1. The invocation preserves stdin

documents.t: install.sh is versioned in the repository and published as a Release asset. It carries its own version and, as its first act, downloads the signed checksums.txt of that Release, verifies the signature (ADR 0149) and checks its own hash against it. If it diverges, it stops. This extends — it does not cite as already said — point 5 of ADR 0146:195-212, which versions consentir-base.mjs with the argument that "a script that configures the user's host, creates a folder and writes to the .env is precisely the artifact whose provenance needs to be auditable", and whose corollary is that the api gains no route that emits a host script. install.sh is the same kind of artifact, with more reach; the corollary holds the same.
documents.s: 2. The script verifies its own origin before acting

documents.t: The marker lives in $XDG_STATE_HOME/brabo/install-state.json, with fallback ~/.local/state/brabo/ — the same idiom servico.ts:250-261 already uses for XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Not in ~/.brabo/, which is where the runner keeps things per project: installation state and project configuration are different lives, and putting them together would make deleting one erase the other. The marker is versioned (schemaVersion) and stores: installed version, source (ghcr or local), applied digests, paths (.env, projects base, compose directory) and the date. It is what makes the second execution a diff and not a guess. Without a marker — every installation prior to this version — the script looks for signals: a compose project with brabo-* services, brabo-runner-*.service units, a .env with the five keys. And it names what it found before any question. There is no "found something, decide on my own" path.
documents.s: 3. Detection names what it found, and only then asks

documents.t: deletes (with confirmation, listed beforehand) never deletes the compose's named volumes, pgdata included the user's projects base the generated .env the mirror folder (RN-516: the mirror never deletes, and neither does the installer) the runner's service units any folder outside the marker's paths the device key on disk what the key protects on the server — revoking is another action The second column is the point. A user folder is accumulation, not product state; deleting it would be the installer taking a decision nobody delegated to it.
documents.s: 4. Deletion says what it deletes, and what it never deletes

documents.t: --source=ghcr (default): reads the Release's .release/images.json, resolves each image by digest and verifies the signature (ADR 0149). --source=local: docker buildx bake with docker-bake.hcl:81-83, which produces exactly the four names the compose expects. It requires a clean working tree on a tag; otherwise it refuses, because an image built from a dirty tree is not the version it claims to be. The word "official" only appears in the output when the verification passed. Switching source afterwards is an image swap over the same volumes — the data does not move.
documents.s: 5. Two image sources, and "official" is the result of verification

documents.t: docker/docker-compose.install.yml is born, which consumes the digests of .release/images.json and has no build: block. docker-compose.prod.yml stays intact: it is the validation compose, it is what docker/smoke.sh uses (:19-20, building locally on purpose), and promoting it to installation manifest would break the use it already has and contradict its own header. The cost is declared: two files with the same service topology. What separates them is what each one answers — "does this tag build?" versus "does this machine run what was published?".
documents.s: 6. An installation compose of its own

documents.t: docker-bake.hcl:81-83 has four targets and scripts/ci/images-manifest.ts:54 accepts four; brabo-broker:prod (docker-compose.prod.yml:333) only exists built locally, and that is why the container-broker profile is unreachable from Release artifacts. The installer does not offer the profile, and says what that means: with --source=ghcr, a project in mounted mode — which ADR 0146 made the local default — does not bring up a container, because whoever brings it up is the broker (ADR 0144). Conversation and backlog work; dev agent execution in that mode does not. Publishing the broker as a fifth image is the fix, and it is small (one target in the bake, one id in images-manifest.ts, one more signature). It stays out of this ADR by scope, not by doubt: it enters as its own item, and while it does not, --source=local is the path that gives complete mounted.
documents.s: 7. The broker does not come up in this phase, and the consequence is stated

documents.t: As it already is in RN-518 (servico.ts:517-532): the installer names the platform, says it is out of scope by declared decision and points to the foreground path. It is neither a generic failure nor a silence.
documents.s: 8. Windows is a named refusal

documents.t: install.sh is bash, because it needs to run before any dependency exists on the machine. The decision logic (detect, compare marker, choose source, build the deletion plan) stays in pure functions, and the script exposes --print-plan / --print-state so a vitest spec can exercise them without executing anything — the precedent is real and from the same repository: scripts/dev/bootstrap.sh has --print-commands and is tested by scripts/dev/bootstrap.spec.ts.
documents.s: 9. Pure bash, with the decision testable

documents.t: docker/smoke.sh generates the five secrets (:31-57) and is the precedent of decision 5 — but calling it does not work: it starts with --build (it builds what this installation just downloaded by digest) and tears the stack down at the end, unless SMOKE_KEEP_UP=1. It is a CI test, and an installation is not a test. The installer does the honest minimum instead: after up --wait, it hits the /health of the api and the engine, and only then says it installed. --wait already waits for the healthcheck — but whoever announces a state has to have asked about it, which is exactly the lesson reset-total.sh cost (it announced "reset completo" with the api in Exited (1)). By the same reasoning there is no migrate step: the compose chains api → migrate-api with service_completed_successfully, and a second place ordering migration would be a second source of the same truth.
documents.s: 10. The post-startup check is its own, and smoke.sh is not reused

documents.t: curl | sh. By decision 1: it closes stdin and with it consent. Promoting docker-compose.prod.yml to installation manifest. It breaks smoke.sh, which builds locally on purpose, and contradicts the file's header. An api route that generates the script. An explicit corollary of ADR 0146 point 5, and it holds with even more force here. Guessed migration. A previous installation without a marker is not "probably the same": it is named, and the path is that of ADR 0152. Deleting anything outside the marker's paths.
documents.s: What this ADR explicitly rejects

documents.t: Installing no longer requires a checkout, and the five secrets are generated once and persisted with mode 600 — today smoke.sh generates them and discards them with the stack. Two composes with the same topology, and divergence between them becomes something to watch. The ceiling: the installation one gains no service the validation one does not have. With --source=ghcr, mounted has no container until the broker is published (decision 7). Declared in the installer's output, not discovered later. The installer's second execution becomes a readable diff. The first execution on a machine that already had Brabo remains the hard case, and is the only one that depends on another ADR.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Proposed. A deliberately narrow cut: the per-machine runner was left out of PHASE 29 and is declared as the scope of the next phase, with the measurement already done (see Consequences).
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The product direction is for the user to choose a project on the web and see the folder appear on their machine. Today that does not happen, and the reason is not a lack of an agent — brabo-runner already lives there. It is that it is born with no notion of where things live. The runner has no base. The only root is --dir, resolved by resolverDir (apps/runner/src/guard.ts:221-227) against INIT_CWD ?? process.cwd(); without --dir, the root is the cwd (apps/runner/src/index.ts:242-250). estado.dir (index.ts:366-368) is one path, singular, and it is what goes to validarCwdDentroDaRaiz, to the GerenciadorDePty, to cwdParaContainer and to the workspace_confirm (index.ts:725). There is no constant, environment variable nor base field in apps/runner/src/ — the word only appears in comments. The base exists, but in the api, and it is forbidden to go down. apps/api/src/infrastructure/filesystem/project-workspaces-root.ts has baseDeProjetos() (:68), dentroDaBaseDeProjetos (:93) and segmentoSobABaseDeProjetos (:116) — and the same file forbids in writing (:421-438) the base rule from entering caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido, because that predicate runs on every read and a legacy mounted project outside the base would explode when read. The base is a creation and conversion rule. There is an exact precedent of a sibling guard. apps/runner/src/espelho-guard.ts was born reusing the three helpers of guard.ts (:51) and implements the loop refusal by segment — dentroDoEscopo(destino, workspace) and dentroDoEscopo(workspace, destino) (:214, :223) —, never raw startsWith, with the reason written at :152-154: "/base-outra NÃO está dentro de /base". And there is an invariant this ADR cannot break. Since ADR 0130, no absolute path crosses the network: whoever has the root is whoever executes, and what travels is the relative segment plus a discriminator of which root it applies against (ADR 0144).
documents.s: Context

documents.t: install.sh (ADR 0150) consents one base and writes it to the runner's local configuration. Each project is a subfolder of it. --dir still exists and still means what it always meant — it is the legacy binary of RN-514, and breaking it would be breaking/ with no gain. The base is local, never received over the network. It is the same design as the broker (ADR 0144): the root belongs to whoever executes; the server sends the segment.
documents.s: 1. The runner is born with a base, consented in the installer

documents.t: Validation of the base and the subfolder reuses semBarraFinal, dentroDoEscopo and realpathMaisProximo from guard.ts — which are already exported precisely for that (guard.ts:33-43, when espelho-guard.ts was born) — and the per-segment loop refusal of espelho-guard.ts:208-233. No fourth copy of the rule is born: RN-515 already established that on the api side, when validarDestinoDeEspelho reused caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido (apps/api/src/application/services/workspace-location.ts:132-136) instead of rewriting it. It inherits in writing the same TOCTOU caveat of guard.ts:9-31 and espelho-guard.ts:30-39: this is best-effort and is not the security boundary, which remains authentication plus the approval pipeline.
documents.s: 2. The guard reuses the rule, it does not copy it

documents.t: A new pair on the channel, in the request with response mold (exec/exec_result, terminal_channel.ex:563-567 and :737-749), because whoever asks needs to know whether it worked: workspace_create — engine → runner: projectId and the segment relative to the base. Never an absolute path. workspace_create_result — runner → engine: success with the final path, or a named error. The runner does mkdir -p and then git init or clone. Having succeeded, it sends the workspace_confirm that already exists (channel.ts:577-582), and it is that which writes — through the path already built and tested: channel → engine → internal HTTP → ConfirmProjectWorkspaceUseCase, which revalidates the lexicon (confirm-project-workspace.use-case.ts:83), is idempotent (:93-95) and writes workspaceVerifiedAt. This is deliberate and saves a whole front: no new write route is born, the engine still does not write the table, and the only path that stamps workspace_verified_at remains a single one. A precision record, because the name circulated: workspace.verified does not exist in the repository — neither event, nor message, nor route. What exists is the project.workspace_verified event (confirm-project-workspace.use-case.ts:107) and the workspace_verified_at column. And workspace_confirm is unidirectional: terminal_channel.ex:356-373 answers {:noreply, socket} and pushes nothing back — which is why the new pair cannot be modeled on it.
documents.s: 3. The new message asks for creation, and the confirmation reuses what already exists

documents.t: workspace enters the vocabulary of Engine.Runners.Capacidades (capacidades.ex:72) in the session in which the code enters, never before — the lesson of RN-514, where declaring espelho without implementing it would be exactly the silent defect the negotiation exists to prevent. An unknown name is still ignored; a required and undeclared capability still refuses the join with the name of what is missing.
documents.s: 4. A capability declared only when implemented

documents.t: Two preconditions — runner connected, base consented — in its own module, in the mold of Engine.Runners.Espelho (espelho.ex:82-99). It does not require a container: creating a folder is a filesystem operation on the user's machine, with no container to fall from. The temptation and the refusal are written down, and this ADR adopts them literally (espelho.ex:19-24): A tentação óbvia seria RunnerReadiness.verificar(project_id, pular_container: true). O ADR 0147 recusa isso por escrito, e a razão é mecânica: uma função compartilhada com flag "pula container" é precisamente o caminho pelo qual a terceira pré-condição cai POR ACIDENTE para o exec numa refatoração futura — e o ADR 0145 existe para ela não cair.
documents.s: 5. Its own predicate, and RunnerReadiness stays byte for byte

documents.t: Creating the folder of the project the user just asked for is consented configuration, not an agent asking to act. None of this becomes a proposed_action, and no policy ceiling gains an exception — the same line the mirror already established (RN-516).
documents.s: 6. It is not proposed_action

documents.t: The creation picker in runner mode uses fs_list_dir, which exists on both sides (apps/runner/src/fs-browser.ts:53, terminal_channel.ex:489) and whose transport in the web (apps/web/src/lib/fs-browser-channel.ts:66) has had no effective caller since RN-504 — kept by a decision declared in apps/web/src/routes/NewProjectWizard.tsx:880-882. It gets its caller back. The mounted mode's path, which goes through the api (GET /workspaces/:workspaceId/project-folders), stays intact.
documents.s: 7. The web reads the base through the runner

documents.t: A per-machine runner in this phase. See Consequences: there are five independent couplings, and tackling them together with the installer would concentrate two big risks in the same phase. RunnerReadiness with a flag. By the quotation in decision 5. A fourth copy of the path rule. An absolute path crossing the network. Invariant of ADR 0130. Merging this with the mirror. They are different messages, with different directions and triggers; the mirror copies outside the base, this creates inside it.
documents.s: What this ADR explicitly rejects

documents.t: The user chooses the project on the web and the folder appears — no terminal, no manual git init. The runner remains paired per project. The five measured couplings, which PHASE 30 will have to cross: the terminal:<projectId> topic (channel.ts:422, terminal_channel.ex:172), the socket id runner_socket:<kind>:<project_id>:<user_id> (runner_socket.ex:71-73), the project-scoped ticket (socket_ticket.ex:10-13), the runner_device_keys.project_id NOT NULL column (apps/api/src/db/schema/auth.ts:325) and the unit name (servico.ts:263-265, :392-394). One of them is a migration; another is breaking/. Revocation still reaches {projeto, usuário} (RN-520), which in this phase keeps the current cost. When PHASE 30 unifies the runner per machine, revoking will bring down all the projects of that machine — declared here so it is not discovered there. The git credential discarded in docker exec in runner mode (ADR 0130/0145) is not affected: this message's initial clone runs on the HOST, through the path that carries the credential. The gap remains where it was.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Proposed. It exists because PHASE 29 needs to migrate a previous installation, and the path the documentation pointed to for that does not work.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The current backup covers one database and runs in one place: docker/backup/backup.sh does pg_dump --format=custom | aws s3 cp - (:124-140), straight to S3 without touching disk, with retention by count (:160-182) and a row in backup_runs on every execution, success or failure (trap registrar EXIT, :44-80). docker/backup/restore.sh restores into a test database (brabo_restore_test, :18), validates three things — the table list, the count of the critical ones within the backup window, and the dense continuity of the seq of session_events (:139-224) — and never touches the origin (:8-9). make test-restore → deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh, which requires kubectl, a cluster and the brabo-backup CronJob in the namespace (:56-58). Three consequences, all measured: Migrating a compose installation has no path. test-restore is Kubernetes; there is no equivalent target against compose, and docker-compose.prod.yml has no backup service (the image is built by the bake and used only in k8s). The backup covers only Postgres. Nothing in docker/backup/ touches neo4j_data, git_local_repos, project_workspaces, ollama_data or brabo_projects_base (docker-compose.prod.yml:474-486). It also requires S3 — five mandatory variables (backup.sh:11-15). In a single-machine installation, requiring a bucket in order to migrate is requiring infrastructure the installer just said it does not need.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The easy mistake is "back up all the volumes". The seven are not the same thing, and treating them the same costs space and hides what matters: volume nature decision pgdata source of truth — event log, actions, everything already covered by pg_dump; it remains the logical dump, not a file copy git_local_repos source of truth — the bare repos of the LocalGitProvider enters, and it is this ADR's finding neo4j_data derived — the graph is memory projected from the event log (ADR 0099), never a source of truth does not enter: what is missing is reprojection, not backup project_workspaces derived — worktrees the WorktreeManager recreates from the bare does not enter ollama_data re-obtainable — models that can be downloaded again does not enter brabo_projects_base the user's, not the product's does not enter, and the installer never deletes it (ADR 0150) git_local_repos is the real hole. A project with the local provider has its bare repository in there; losing that volume is losing the code the agents produced, and today no backup covers it. It is not rebuildable from Postgres — the event log keeps the narrative, not the git objects.
documents.s: 1. Classify the volumes before copying them

documents.t: The backup now accepts a disk destination besides S3. In a single-machine installation, a directory is the honest destination; requiring a bucket to migrate would be requiring infrastructure the installer does not ask for. The five S3 variables stop being mandatory and become what they already were in practice: the configuration of one of the destinations.
documents.s: 2. Local destination, S3 optional

documents.t: The equivalent of test-restore without a cluster is born: it brings up the backup image with docker compose run, restores into a test database and runs the same three validations of restore.sh:139-224. No new validation logic — what changes is the wrapper, not the judgment. deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh stays intact: they are two environments with two wrappers, and unifying them would make the compose one depend on kubectl.
documents.s: 3. A restore path that runs against compose

documents.t: Restoring neo4j_data from a backup would restore a possibly old projection next to a Postgres restored at another point — two derived states from different instants, with nothing reconciling them. The right answer for derived memory is to reproject from the source. This phase does not build the reprojection: it declares that it is the path and that, until it exists, a migrated installation is born with the graph empty — which is known degradation (RAG remains in pgvector, which lives in Postgres and comes in the dump), not data loss.
documents.s: 4. Graph reprojection is the answer for Neo4j

documents.t: The migration path of ADR 0150 is: backup → confirm → deletion → installation → restore, with the restore proven by decision 3. Without a good backup, the installer does not proceed to deletion.
documents.s: 5. The installer uses this, and does not guess

documents.t: Copying all the volumes. By decision 1: three of the seven are derived or re-obtainable, and copying them gives the impression of coverage without adding recovery. A file copy of pgdata. Copying the data directory of a running Postgres produces a backup that may not restore; the logical dump remains. Restoring neo4j_data. By decision 4. Running the restore against the origin database. restore.sh never touches the origin (:8-9), and that property is not negotiated for the convenience of migration. Unifying with deploy/k8s/test-restore.sh.
documents.s: What this ADR explicitly rejects

documents.t: Migrating an existing installation gets a proven path, and the installer earns the right to delete volumes — because it proved it can bring them back. git_local_repos enters the backup, and that is the difference this ADR makes outside the installation scope: today any loss of that volume is a loss of code, in any environment, and nobody had recorded it. A migrated installation is born with an empty graph until reprojection exists. Declared, with the effect named: the reads that depend on the graph degrade; RAG is not affected. The backup gains a second destination, and with it a second failure path — a full disk. The row in backup_runs is still written in both cases, by the trap that already exists.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Proposed. Awaiting the product owner's decision on Stage B (below), which is not an engineering choice. This document does not change the status of any role or gate by itself.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: DEPLOY_ENABLED is the declared trigger of everything missing in the platform layer. It is cited in ten documents: ADR 0091 and ADR 0092, in the Status field itself — "its activation stays synchronized with DEPLOY_ENABLED, which doesn't exist"; ADR 0089; docs/fluxo.yml, in three places — platform.ativacao ("sincronizada com DEPLOY_ENABLED"), area-infra.gate_saida (deployavel, status: planned, with the comment # DEPLOY_ENABLED) and BOTH gap deliverables of secops-runtime (resposta-a-incidente and postmortem-de-seguranca, both with motivo: exige tráfego de produção real (pós DEPLOY_ENABLED + platform ativo)); docs/gates.yml, in the operavel gate (backlog: deploy (DEPLOY_ENABLED + Environments)); and also business-rules.md, backlog.md, modelo-de-time.md, auditoria-fluxo-vs-codigo.md, historico-de-fases.md and CLAUDE.md. In the code it appears twice, both as a comment — apps/api/src/domain/actions/external-effect.ts:144 ("Estes não têm ação tipada ainda (DEPLOY_ENABLED está no backlog)") and apps/engine/lib/engine/harness/tools/listar_metricas_de_produto.ex:185. No definition, no read, in apps/, docker/, deploy/, scripts/, .env.example or Makefile. Ten documents point to a switch that has no wall.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: stuck where consequence platform fluxo.yml, status: planned the owner of the feedback loop does not exist; SLO, dashboard, runbook and postmortem have no author operavel gate gates.yml:312-321, status: planned declared, never evaluated deployavel gate fluxo.yml:247 is not in the registry — see the finding below resposta-a-incidente and postmortem-de-seguranca fluxo.yml:223-226 the two gap deliverables of secops-runtime, which is status: active
documents.s: What is stuck on it

documents.t: The deployavel gate is declared as the gate_saida of area-infra in docs/fluxo.yml:247 and does not exist in docs/gates.yml. ADR 0054 defines the registry as the place where the gates that exist are declared; a gate named by one piece of the team model and absent from the other is exactly the inconsistency the cross-check test between agent-areas.ts, gates.yml and fluxo.yml would catch — and that test is declared backlog in CLAUDE.md, not something that exists today. This is fixable without deciding anything about deploy, and it is the only part of this document that does not depend on anyone buying a server.
documents.s: A finding that is not about deploy

documents.t: Turning on the flag without a production environment with real traffic does not activate the roles: it creates gates that pass empty. A gate that approves because it has nothing to fail is worse than a gate declared planned, because it teaches whoever reads it that the loop closed. It is the same reason ADRs 0091 and 0092 refused to create an agent and delivered an on-demand script — and that refusal remains right.
documents.s: The tension that orders the decision

documents.t: Two stages, with a hard boundary between what is engineering and what is not.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: What has already been applied in this delivery: only item 1. It fixes a hole in the REGISTRY and does not depend on the deploy decision — it is the only part of this document that holds even if Stage B never happens. Items 2 and 3 describe what acceptance implies; item 3 (the prose of the ten documents) was not applied, because changing the wording before the decision would be asserting a choice that has not yet been made. deployavel enters docs/gates.yml with status: planned, dono: area-infra, severidade: warn and aprovacao_humana: false, in the exact mold of operavel (gates.yml:312-321). It closes the registry hole. warn and not block because the registry rule (RN-070/RN-071) requires verificacao: script to promote, and there is no script. The two anticipated scripts do not change. apps/api/scripts/relatorio-telemetria.ts and apps/api/scripts/relatorio-seguranca-runtime.ts are already active, already run on demand and already deliver what ADRs 0091/0092 promised. The prose stops treating DEPLOY_ENABLED as a variable. Where today one reads "synchronized with DEPLOY_ENABLED", one now names the milestone the expression always meant, with an objective criterion: there is an operated target environment, receiving real traffic, whose delivery pipeline someone maintains.
documents.s: Stage A — what is decidable today, and is little on purpose

documents.t: A production environment with traffic. Only after that does platform leave planned, operavel and deployavel stop being planned, and the two gap deliverables of secops-runtime become possible. The infrastructure is already ready and is not the bottleneck: deploy/k8s/ with local/staging/prod overlays, the four images published on GHCR by digest since ADR 0119, make imagens-do-release, bootstrap.sh, smoke.sh, rollout-test.sh and test-restore.sh. What is missing is someone to run and maintain it — and none of this deploys on its own.
documents.s: Stage B — blocked by an operator, not by code

documents.t: Creating DEPLOY_ENABLED now, as an environment variable with default false. It was the first design, and it pays off badly: a variable no code reads is the same empty promise this ADR exists to denounce, only now with a configuration line to sustain it. The repository already has the rule that solves this — a capability is only declared when proven by the suite; without proof, it is declared false and degrades (ADRs 0041/0042). The flag is born in the PR that has the first real consumer, and that PR is Stage B's. The name DEPLOY_ENABLED stays reserved: ten documents already use it, and renaming the milestone now would only move the debt.
documents.s: The alternative considered and rejected

documents.t: Creating a platform or secops-runtime agent in the engine. It would be inventing authority over a loop that does not close — the refusal of ADRs 0091/0092, repeated here because the question comes back. Promoting operavel or deployavel to block without a verification script (RN-070/RN-071). Marking as "not measured forever" what only depends on an environment: MTTR and change failure rate remain declared as a gap with a reason, not as an impossibility.
documents.s: What this ADR explicitly rejects

documents.t: The gate registry now contains every gate the team model names — deployavel stops existing on only one side. Nothing changes at runtime. No new variable, no changed default, no gate evaluated that was not before. The platform layer remains stopped, and now says honestly why: what is missing is not a flag, it is an environment. Whoever reads fluxo.yml stops looking in the code for a variable that was never there. It is recorded that the distance between "declared" and "existing" has already cost once: ten documents agreed among themselves about a mechanism, and the agreement survived because nothing cross-checked them with the code. The cross-check test between the three pieces of the team model remains in the backlog, and this is the second finding it would have caught.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted on 2026-09-27 (AT-108), after being implemented — the same path as ADR 0055. It was born Proposed in session 1 of PHASE 30 (2026-09-11) and was exercised by RN-543..552 in sessions 2 to 8, with the closing narrated in historico-de-fases.md and in fase-30-runner-por-maquina.md. Where the text below diverges from the code, the decision was NOT rewritten: the divergence is named in "Acceptance notes", at the end. First of the two decisions of PHASE 30. The other is ADR 0155, and it depends on this one: without a machine identity, there is nothing for the installer to register.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The product direction is that of PHASE 29: install Brabo in one line and have the local agent up. The installer already comes close — since RN-531 it downloads the binary, checks it against the signed checksums.txt and installs it with install -m 0755, without a manual chmod — and then stops. The last line of its output says why, in so many words: Não pareia o agente local com um projeto: o binário e a base ficam prontos aqui, mas a chave de dispositivo e o brabo-runner.config.json continuam vindo da tela do projeto (ADR 0118). The binary stays on disk, idle. Whoever wants to use it goes back to the project screen, chooses the folder, and ends up pasting into the terminal the command that apps/web/src/lib/runner-bootstrap.ts:398 builds — chmod +x ./brabo-runner && ./brabo-runner. The comment right above it explains why the screen cannot eliminate that step, and the argument is right: Uma página web não executa binário na máquina de ninguém: este passo é humano em qualquer desenho, e o que dá para fazer é encolhê-lo a UMA linha copiável. What the argument does not cover is that the installer is not a web page. It runs in the terminal, with a TTY, and already asks — it is the whole design of ADR 0150, which refuses curl | sh precisely so it can ask. The human step is unavoidable on the screen and avoidable there.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: brabo-runner service install has existed since RN-518 (ADR 0147 point 5) and installs the agent as a user service (systemd --user/LaunchAgent). Nobody calls it from install.sh, and it is not forgetfulness: it needs a projectId and a device key, and at installation time no project exists — no account, no workspace. The .env was just born, the compose just came up, nobody has signed up. PHASE 29 measured the coupling and named it: "one runner per project is imposed in five independent places". Measured again here, with arquivo:linha: # where what it imposes 1 apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/terminal_channel.ex:204 the topic is terminal:<projectId> 2 apps/engine/lib/engine_web/channels/runner_socket.ex:73 the socket id is runner_socket:<kind>:<project_id>:<user_id> 3 Engine.Runners.SocketTicket (runner_socket_tickets) the ticket carries project_id and the join requires it to match 4 apps/api/src/db/schema/auth.ts:325-326 runner_device_keys.project_id is NOT NULL 5 apps/runner/src/servico.ts:264,391 the unit is brabo-runner-<projectId>.service
documents.s: What blocks is not the binary: it is the identity

documents.t: The obvious cut would be to cross all five. Measuring the socket, it shrinks. RunnerSocket.connect/3 (runner_socket.ex:33) authenticates by ticket, and the ticket is requested from the api per project. The project_id arrives in socket.assigns and the atomic consumption happens in the join, against the topic's project_id. That is: items 1, 2 and 3 describe a connection, not a process. A single process that opens N connections — one per project it serves — satisfies all three byte for byte, without touching the topic, the socket id, the ticket, nor the refusal of a second runner in the same project, which remains the guarantee it is today. What remains is what genuinely belongs to the process: the credential with which it requests the N tickets (item 4) and the unit that keeps it up (item 5). Those two are what this ADR moves.
documents.s: Three of the five do not need to change, and that is this decision's discovery

documents.t: runner_device_keys.project_id is NOT NULL (auth.ts:325-326), and the key is generated by the browser inside a project's screen (ADR 0118, RN-464..466, RN-475). A machine with three projects in runner mode has three keys, three folders with brabo-runner-device-key.jwk.json, three service units and three processes — and the person went three times through the same browser flow to describe one machine.
documents.s: And today the credential is born tied to a project

documents.t: The local agent's identity now belongs to the MACHINE, not to the project.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: No new table is born. A machine key is a device key with project_id NULL — same table, same public_key_jwk column, same kid recorded inside the private JWK (RN-475), same revocation. A sibling table was considered and rejected: PatAuthGuard finds the public key by kid and does not need to know what kind it is; two tables would do two lookups, and the second would be forgotten exactly once. RN-519 (listing) and RN-520 (revocation that reaches the live connection) remain valid with no new code, with a consequence declared below. NULL and not a sentinel (project_id = '00000000-…'): the FK is real and a sentinel would require a fake row in projects to satisfy it.
documents.s: 1. runner_device_keys.project_id becomes nullable, and NULL means machine

documents.t: POST .../runner-ticket remains per project — it is what carries the project_id of item 3. What changes is what it accepts as a credential: a machine key of the same user becomes valid for any project in which that user reaches the role the route already requires. No new ceiling, and none loosened: authorization remains the usual one, resolved against the requested project. What the machine key does not do is widen reach: it gives the runner nothing its owner did not already have. It swaps "one credential per project" for "one credential per machine", and that is all.
documents.s: 2. A machine key is valid for the user's projects, resolved at ticket time

documents.t: A new route, GET runner/projects (the route's minimum is developer, the same as runner-ticket): the user's projects in execution_mode: runner, with the workspace_dir_name and the verification state of each one. The runner queries it at start and opens one connection per project it lists. It asks instead of sweeping the base: the base is the user's and may have a folder that is no project at all, and guessing by folder name is the class of error ADR 0141 rejected when it forbade PROJECT_WORKSPACES_HOST_DIR as the base.
documents.s: 3. The runner discovers the projects it serves, and does not guess them

documents.t: brabo-runner.service / dev.brabo.runner, without projectId in the name. The original argument of servico.ts:32-38 — "naming by the folder would allow installing two units that can never be up at the same time" — disappears along with the premise: with one process per machine there are not two. Restart=on-abnormal stays byte for byte, for the reason of RN-518: exit 1 is a fatal join refusal or an exhausted attempts ceiling, and restarting would be the loop the CLI refuses to do on its own.
documents.s: 4. The service unit becomes ONE per machine

documents.t: A new binary with an old unit installed does not break, and status answers about both. Whoever has three per-project units keeps three processes until running service uninstall on each one — and the machine unit's status says that they exist, instead of leaving six processes competing for three projects silently. Corrected in the implementation (RN-545). This ADR said that service install without --project would install the machine unit. Measured, it does not work: the absence of the flag already has a meaning — resolverProjeto falls back to the folder's brabo-runner.config.json, and the normal path of whoever uses the product today is to run install with no flag at all from inside the folder the browser configured. Taken literally, the rule would silently convert the installation of whoever already uses the product — the opposite of what this very point promises. The discriminator is the --machine flag, explicit. Edited instead of contradicted because this ADR is still Proposed: an accepted ADR is never edited, the new one references the old.
documents.s: 5. Per-project units keep working, and the conversion is stated

documents.t: Merging the topics into a runner:<userId>. It would be crossing items 1, 2 and 3 to gain nothing: N connections already satisfy them, and the refusal of a second runner per project — which is a real guarantee — lives precisely there. A machine key that crosses users. runner_device_keys.user_id remains NOT NULL. A machine shared by two people means two keys, and that is the right answer: the credential describes who acts, not only where. Discovering projects from the disk. See point 3. Per-key revocation. RN-520 reaches {projeto, usuário} by construction, and this ADR does not change it — it only makes its cost bigger, which is in Consequences. Any exception in decide.ts. The five absolute ceilings, the lexical scope of ADR 0055 and the auto-approval floor of RN-493 stay as they are. This ADR moves identity, never authority. RunnerReadiness with a flag. The three preconditions of RN-507 stay byte for byte, for the reason already recorded in ADR 0147 point 4: it is through such a flag that the third would fall by accident.
documents.s: What this ADR explicitly rejects

documents.t: Revoking now costs more, and that was foreseen. PHASE 29 declared: "when PHASE 30 makes the runner per machine, revoking will bring down all the projects of that machine. Cost declared here so it is not discovered there." That is exactly what happens, and the RN-519 listing now needs to say which kind each key is — a machine one is not "project X's key". One process instead of N. Less memory and fewer units, and a single point of failure where there were N independent ones: the service going down takes the local agent off all the projects of that machine. espelho and workspace_create do not change. Both are per project and travel in the grant of that connection's join (RN-516, RN-532). With N connections, each one keeps receiving its own — and project B's mirror destination remains impossible to reach through project A's connection, which is the guarantee RN-515 exists to give. The browser flow (ADR 0118) is not removed. It remains the path of whoever already has an installation, and becomes the second one. Deciding whether it should disappear is what BRB-031 calls the maintainer's decision, and it is not a consequence of this delivery. The workspace capability (RN-532) gains a second reason to exist. It already depended on STATE (consented base); with the machine agent, it is through it that the server knows that process can materialize the folder of a freshly created project — which is the "link the folder later" this phase pursues.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Checked against the code at acceptance. The decision stays as it is; these are the points where the text and the code diverge, and where the code resolved it: Point 1 — "RN-519 and RN-520 remain valid with no new code". They did not remain without code. The listing now includes machine keys in every project of the owner (apps/api/src/infrastructure/persistence/drizzle/runner-device-key.repository.ts:88) and says the kind, derived from project_id in a single place (:23); the revocation of a machine key now calls disconnectRunnerOfUser once per project in runner mode of the owner (apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/revoke-runner-device-key.use-case.ts:120). It is the consequence the Consequences already foresaw, paid in code (RN-543). Point 3 — "the route's minimum is developer". There is no @RequireRole on GET runner/projects: there is no project in the path against which to resolve it. The minimum is applied per ROW, with the project's effective role (apps/api/src/application/use-cases/runner/list-runner-projects.use-case.ts:75), and only a MACHINE credential gets in — one tied to a project is 403 with its own message (apps/api/src/interfaces/http/auth/pat-auth.guard.ts:279). The listed set is the same the point promises (RN-543). Point 4 — the unit's discriminator. Already corrected in the text itself, in session 4, while Proposed: it is the --machine flag (apps/runner/src/servico.ts:898, resolverEspecie at :912), never the absence of --project (RN-545). Point 5 — the two kinds coexisting. The text describes per-project units and the machine one installed together, with status pointing out the overlap. The code does not let it get there: install REFUSES when the OTHER kind is already installed, naming the uninstall of each unit, without removing anything and without --force (apps/runner/src/servico.ts:993, recusaDeSobreposicao at :1269). status still says in text that the other one exists — what remains of point 5 is the case of whoever installed before the guard (RN-545).
documents.s: Acceptance notes (2026-09-27)

documents.t: Accepted on 2026-09-27 (AT-108), after being implemented — the same path as ADR 0055. It was born Proposed in session 1 of PHASE 30 (2026-09-11) and was exercised by RN-543..552 in sessions 2 to 8 (the E2E on a clean machine, RN-549, is the end to end proof), with the closing narrated in historico-de-fases.md and in fase-30-runner-por-maquina.md. Where the text below diverges from the code, the decision was NOT rewritten: the divergence is named in "Acceptance notes", at the end. Second of the two decisions of PHASE 30. It depends on ADR 0154: without a machine identity, there is nothing to register here.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: install.sh ends with the compose up and the runner binary on disk. The person opens the browser and finds a login screen in an installation where nobody exists. And the way out of there is broken in a new installation. Measured: the .env the installer generates has no email variable at all (install.sh, the heredoc that writes the eleven keys); MAIL_TRANSPORT falls to the default log (docker/docker-compose.install.yml:200), and the compose says in the comment next to it that "o comportamento continua log-only mesmo aqui"; registration requires verifying email, and the docblock of apps/api/src/scripts/provisionar-usuario.ts already records the consequence in so many words: "o fluxo normal de registro exige verificar e-mail — que com o MailSender log-only não fecha sozinho". That is: whoever installs through the single line signs up, receives nothing, and the only way out is to go fish the link out of docker compose logs api. An installation that ends saying "Done" and lets nobody in. provisionarUsuario exists precisely for that hole — it creates a user with a password already verified — and today has two callers, the demo seed and the smoke. Neither of them is the real installation.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: The installer creates the first account, with explicit consent in the terminal, and brings up the local agent already paired.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: The step runs when the installation has no user at all. With any user present, the installer does not offer it — it is not an account creator, it is the closing of a new installation. In a migration (RN-530) the users come in the restore, and the step goes silent by the same criterion. The route is internal and authenticated by BRABO_SERVICE_TOKEN — the same secret the installer just generated and wrote to the .env, with mode 600 —, and refuses if a user already exists. No public "create the first owner" route is born: a public route that creates an owner is a race between whoever installed and whoever scanned the port.
documents.s: 1. Only the FIRST account, and only when there is none

documents.t: The account is born verified, through provisionarUsuario. That does not loosen normal registration, which stays byte for byte: what email verification proves is "this person controls this mailbox", and whoever is running the installer has already proven something stronger — they control the machine, the .env with the five secrets and the Docker daemon. Requiring the weaker proof from them, through a channel the installation knows is off, is theater. The installer says so in the output, instead of letting the person discover that their account is different from the others.
documents.s: 2. No email verification, and the reason is what authorizes it

documents.t: Same rule as RN-511 and consentir-base.mjs: the step asks for email and password, and without an interactive terminal it reports instead of deciding. There is no path in which an account is born with a password chosen by the script — neither generated nor default. The password is read without echo and confirmed. The minimum refusal (length) is the same as the domain's, called by the same code; the installer does not carry a second password rule, which would diverge.
documents.s: 3. Consent is explicit, and without a TTY the step does not happen

documents.t: With the account created, the installer registers a machine device key (ADR 0154), writes the private key with the kid inside (RN-475, the defect that made automatic mode never authenticate) and installs the service — the per machine unit of ADR 0154 point 4. The pair is generated on the machine; the private key never travels. It is the same design as the browser (ADR 0118), for the same reason, and keeps true the sentence RN-519 uses to refuse the maintainer view: "the private key of a device key never leaves the browser" — it becomes "never leaves the machine". Detailed in the implementation (RN-552). This point did not say with which credential the installer registers the key, and both candidates were real. The route — POST /internal/machine-device-keys — was born with the service token, the same as the first account: it is the same installer, in the same minute, and the token proves control of the MACHINE, which is what this step wants to prove. The alternative, the freshly created user's credential, would contradict point 5 of this ADR ("the installer logs in for nobody") and would give the password read on the TTY a second use, where the Consequences promise it is used and discarded. The cost — a leaked service token can now MANUFACTURE a durable access credential — is declared in docs/security-surface.md, and three containments live in the route: there is no userId in the body (the owner is the installation's SINGLE user, 409 with zero or more than one), registering REPLACES the owner's active machine keys (a reinstalled machine passes; a thousand keys do not exist), and a JWK with d is refused by name instead of written. Detailed instead of contradicted, and in writing because this ADR is still Proposed: an accepted ADR is never edited, the new one references the old.
documents.s: 4. The machine key is registered there, and the service comes up with it

documents.t: The installed agent queries GET runner/projects (ADR 0154 point 3) and finds nothing, because there is no project yet. It waits, and that is not an error: it emits no failure, does not exit with a non-zero code, and service status says "up, no project in runner mode" — one of the four states RN-518 already distinguishes, and not a fifth. When the person creates the first project in runner mode on the web, the agent is already there. That is the "link the folder later" the phase pursues, and it happens through workspace_create (RN-532), without anyone going back to the terminal.
documents.s: 5. The service comes up without a project, and that is the normal state

documents.t: Creating an account when one already exists. See point 1. A public first-owner route. See point 1. A password generated by the script, or a default. See point 3. An installer that chooses a password produces installations with the same password. Loosening normal registration's email verification. Point 2 creates a path for a named case; it does not touch the other. Turning on SMTP on its own. The installer does not ask for a mail server and does not write MAIL_*: MAIL_TRANSPORT=log remains the declared default, here as in production. What it does is stop depending on it for the installation to close. Asking for an LLM credential. It is out: the installation ends usable, and the provider key is the decision of whoever will spend (RN-058).
documents.s: What this ADR explicitly rejects

documents.t: The one-line installation now really closes: it ends with an account, login possible and the local agent up. Today it ends with a login nobody can get through without reading a container log. The installer now handles a password. It is read without echo, used and discarded — never written to the .env, never to the marker, never to the log. The marker ($XDG_STATE_HOME/brabo/) gains the created owner's email, which is identification and not a secret, and nothing more. A second user creation path now exists in production. It is narrow (first account, internal route, service token) and disappears as soon as the installation has people — but it is a new surface, and it is declared. provisionarUsuario gains a third caller, and the first that is not test automation. Its docblock says today that it exists for seed and smoke; it now also says for the installation. PHASE 29 becomes coherent with itself. It refused the one-line installer "while the artifacts are not signed" and signed before installing; this phase closes the other end — installing is not delivering bytes, it is leaving it usable.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Checked against the code at acceptance. The decision stays as it is; these are the points where the text and the code diverge, and where the code resolved it: Point 2 and Consequences — "the account is born verified, through provisionarUsuario", which "gains a third caller". The text did not face that the provisionarUsuario script REFUSES to run with NODE_ENV=production (apps/api/src/scripts/provisionar-usuario.ts:37), and the installer runs exactly in production. The resolution was to extract the core — the trio of writes that makes the account be born verified — into ProvisionarUsuarioUseCase (apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/provisionar-usuario.use-case.ts:43) and leave the refusal in the SCRIPT, which is what it protects (a known password created without human interaction). Whoever gained the new caller was the use case, through the first account route (apps/api/src/application/use-cases/auth/criar-primeira-conta.use-case.ts:85); the script keeps the previous two, seed and smoke, and BRABO_FORCE_SEED is NOT the installer's path (RN-546). Point 4 — with which credential the machine key is registered. Already detailed in the text itself, while Proposed: the service token, through POST /internal/machine-device-keys (RN-552). The pair is born in the terminal through two commands, brabo-runner device-key create and finish --id, because the kid is the record's id on the server and only exists after it (RN-551). Point 5 — "does not exit with a non-zero code". Waiting with zero projects exists (RN-550, which fixed RN-544's exit with 0 precisely for contradicting this point), but it has a ceiling of TEN consecutive queries without a useful answer, and then the agent exits with 1 naming the number (apps/runner/src/espera-de-projetos.ts:75, the exit at apps/runner/src/index.ts:1547). An empty list does not count as a failure — only an api that does not answer. Point 5 — "service status says 'up, no project in runner mode'". status does not know about projects: it answers from the disk and the manager, with the four states of RN-518 (apps/runner/src/servico.ts:246), and the waiting machine unit appears as rodando. Whoever says "no project in runner mode" is the agent's own LOG (apps/runner/src/index.ts:1529). The point about there being no fifth state is fulfilled; the text attributed to status, not.
documents.s: Acceptance notes (2026-09-27)

documents.t: Accepted. It closes the gap that ADR 0127 declared in writing and pinned in a test. It neither revokes nor revises it: the two ceilings of that ADR remain exactly as they are, and what changes is the set of DOORS through which ceiling 2 is evaluated. It corresponds to BRB-001, a security P1 of the maintainer's register.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: ADR 0127 put two ceilings on the WRITE path of project_members — nobody downgrades the workspace owner, nobody downgrades themselves — and deliberately chose not to cover a third move, leaving the reason and the cost recorded in the section "Still possible, by name": self-downgrade through REMOVAL. RemoveProjectMemberUseCase did NOT gain a ceiling (…) The premise that "removal is always benign" is false, and it stays written here so it is not rediscovered. Both cases are PINNED in tests (…), including the one that remains open, so the next person knows it is a decision and not forgetfulness. Closing it costs the signature of RemoveProjectMemberUseCase.execute, which today is called by list-projects-and-members.use-case.spec.ts with two arguments. This ADR is that next person, and the foreseen cost was exactly the one charged. The defect, measured. RemoveProjectMemberUseCase.execute received (projectId, userId) — it did not receive the actor — and the controller (@Delete(':projectId/members/:userId'), @RequireRole('maintainer')) called it with the two route parameters, without @CurrentUser(). Since ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject is projectRole ?? workspaceRole (RN-471), deleting the project row does not delete a role: it SWAPS the effective role for the second term. When the workspace role is lower, the net effect is the downgrade ceiling 2 exists to prevent, with the same irreversibility — going back is POST :projectId/members, which requires the maintainer one just abandoned. With no workspace role at all, the fall is to NO access. The case had been reproduced in a test since ADR 0127, with its name saying what it documented: "e a remoção SEGUE podendo rebaixar quem a chamou, quando o workspace não segura — lacuna declarada no ADR 0127". A maintainer whose authority came from the project row, viewer in the workspace, removed their own row and fell to viewer with no way back through the screen. Why it is the same rule, and not a new one. Ceiling 2 compares TODAY's effective role with the effective role AFTER, and never needed to know through which route the second arrived. In add the after-role is the body's; in removal it is the workspace's. Writing a second rule for the second door would be the fourth copy of a comparison that already lives in domain/iam/tetos-de-rebaixamento.ts — and copying a rule is the failure mode this repository pursues in several places (the generated list of areas, roleAtLeast with the same name on both sides, caminhoDeWorkspaceLocalValido reused instead of rewritten).
documents.s: Context

documents.t: 1. Removal now receives the actor and refuses the net self-downgrade. RemoveProjectMemberUseCase.execute becomes (projectId, atorId, alvoId) — the same order as AddProjectMemberUseCase — and throws ForbiddenException (403) when removing the CALLER's OWN row would leave them with a lower role than today's. The controller passes @CurrentUser(), as add already did. 2. The rule is ceiling 2 reused, with the workspace role in place of the requested role. remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento enters the same domain module, and it reimplements no comparison at all: it delegates to ehAutoRebaixamento passing papelPedidoNoProjeto: papelDoAtorNoWorkspace. It exists, instead of the use case calling ehAutoRebaixamento directly, because of ONE case the other's signature cannot state — an actor without a workspace role, where the after-role is "none", which is not a Role. That case is the maximum downgrade and refuses. 3. Ceiling 1 does NOT gain a pair, and the absence is a decision. Removing the project row of someone who is WORKSPACE owner can only RAISE their effective role, or keep it: owner is the top of ROLE_ORDER, so there is no workspace role for which the fall is a fall. More than harmless, the move is the ONLY way to undo the restriction that ceiling 1 of ADR 0127 prevents from being created — a workspace owner who already had a viewer row in a project (written before that ADR, or by a direct database write) reaches their own project again exactly that way. A ceiling there would refuse only benign moves, and would make permanent a state ADR 0127 was born to eliminate. The absence is written in the code, next to the function, and pinned in a test. 4. No threshold, like ceiling 2. The refusal is "oneself", not "below maintainer", and the declared price of ADR 0127 comes along: the self-removal that drops from project owner to workspace maintainer is reversible and ALSO FALLS. It remains reachable by another maintainer. That case used to pass and now refuses — it is the only behavior change this ADR introduces on a benign move, and it is the same trade ADR 0127 had already accepted for add: a clause with no number, against an exception that needs to be explained every time. 5. The message is ITS OWN, not add's. Whoever clicked "remove" did not ask to change any role, and a sentence talking about "downgrading oneself" would not explain what happened. MENSAGEM_TETO_AUTO_REBAIXAMENTO_POR_REMOCAO states the mechanism: without the project row the role falls to the workspace's, and going back requires the abandoned role. 6. The OpenAPI description now describes the code. The route's said only that "whoever has a role in the workspace keeps seeing the project by inheritance" — half true, and the missing half is the reason for this decision: the inheritance can be LOWER than the row. openapi.json and api-types.generated.ts come from the generator.
documents.s: Decision

documents.t: A workspace owner ceiling on removal. See point 3. It is not a forgotten symmetry: there is no removal that downgrades a workspace owner. A second role comparison rule. See point 2. The comparison keeps living in a single place. Touching ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase.forProject. projectRole ?? workspaceRole stays byte for byte, in both directions — it is the capability ADR 0127 refused to eliminate, and nothing here reopens the question. Extending the ceiling to the workspace. POST workspaces/:workspaceId/members is an upsert with no ceiling at all, as ADR 0127 already declared — and removal does not even exist there: WorkspacesController has no member @Delete (measured), so the equivalent move is not reachable over HTTP in that scope. Different scope, separate decision. Blocking the removal of ANOTHER person, even when they drop in role. It is the usual legitimate capability — the same that restricts a developer to viewer in a sensitive project —, and it applies to removal as it applies to writing. A gate on the screen. See Consequences.
documents.s: What this ADR explicitly rejects

documents.t: A benign move falls along, and it is the price already accepted. The self-removal of someone with owner in the project and maintainer in the workspace was allowed and becomes 403. It is reversible by another maintainer, and the test that pinned the permission now pins the refusal, with its name saying it is the price of the ceiling without a threshold. Whoever wants to leave a list in that situation asks another maintainer — the same outcome ceiling 2 already produced through add. The screen still offers the button the api refuses, and the refusal shows. MembersSection.handleRemove already has a try/catch with mensagemDaApi (RN-471), so the api's sentence reaches the toast without a single web line. Unlike ceiling 1, this gate IS computable on the client — userIdDaSessao() and the effective role are there —, but computing only it would produce a button honest about one refusal and silent about the other, which is exactly the half-gate ADR 0127 refused. It is left for the web PR that solves the whole problem. Two more queries per removal, even when the target is another person: the actor's forProject (which redoes the findById) and forWorkspace. It is the cost ADR 0127 had already accepted in add, on an administration route, and the alternative — an if (atorId === alvoId) before the reads — would repeat in the use case the clause the pure function exists to contain. The signature changed, and two tests called it. execute has three arguments now; list-projects-and-members.use-case.spec.ts and tetos-de-rebaixamento.use-case.spec.ts were updated. There is no other caller: the constructor gained ResolveEffectiveRoleUseCase, which was already registered in iam-use-cases.module.ts. The gap test became a ceiling test. The block ADR 0127 left pinning the hole ("removal STILL can downgrade whoever called it") was INVERTED instead of deleted, and the name keeps the origin. It is the form this repository already uses so as not to lose the evidence of why something existed. Still possible, by name: downgrading another person through the removal of their row; self-PROMOTION (unchanged); and the entire workspace scope, whose member POST remains without a ceiling.
documents.s: Consequences

documents.t: Accepted. It is the THIRD in the line opened by ADR 0127 and continued by ADR 0156. It closes the last move the two left declared in writing, and revises one sentence of 0127: self-PROMOTION, which it recorded in the Consequences as a capability that stayed, is now refused. An accepted ADR is not edited — this one references it and says what changed. It corresponds to BRB-002, a security P1 of the maintainer's register.
documents.s: Status

documents.t: The two previous ADRs closed the three doors of project_members — the two write ones and the removal one — and each of them pointed, in so many words, to what was left open. 0127: downgrading the workspace owner in the workspace. Ceiling 1 is about project_members. POST workspaces/:workspaceId/members remains an upsert with no ceiling at all — same class of defect, scope above, not addressed here. And 0156, reaffirming: Extending the ceiling to the workspace. POST workspaces/:workspaceId/members is an upsert with no ceiling at all, as ADR 0127 already declared (…) Different scope, separate decision. The defect, measured. AddWorkspaceMemberUseCase was a twelve-line pass-through: execute(workspaceId, userId, role) calling workspaces.addMember. It did not receive the actor, and the controller (@Post(':workspaceId/members'), @RequireRole('owner')) called it with the bare body, without @CurrentUser() — there was nothing with which to apply any ceiling, just as there was nothing on removal before 0156. It is the same class of defect one scope ABOVE, and it is more serious for two reasons that do not exist in the project: there is no level above to hold the fall. In the project, downgrading oneself drops the effective role to the workspace role, which often holds it. In the workspace the role is the role: an owner who writes themselves as viewer loses the whole workspace, and with it all projects, the LLM spend that is theirs by RN-060, and the very ability to invite whoever would replace them; there is no member removal route to undo it by another path. WorkspacesController has no member @Delete — 0156 had already measured that and used it as an argument not to extend the ceiling in that PR. Undoing is THIS same route, which requires the freshly abandoned owner. There is no way back through the screen, nor through the api. The second half: self-promotion. ADR 0127 wrote, in the list of what remained possible: self-PROMOTION. A maintainer can write themselves as project owner. It was already possible before this ADR and still is; the ceilings are about going down, and opening the question of going up here would have changed, in passing, a capability nobody asked to change. There was a test pinning this — "raising one's own role is not a downgrade and still passes" —, with a workspace maintainer writing themselves as project owner. The decision not to open the question in that PR was right by process, and the answer, now that it is open, is that it is a loophole. Both halves are the same move — a person deciding alone what authority they have —, and the upper one is the only one of the two that escalates privilege: 0127 could say its ceilings were not about escalation ("nobody gains a role they did not have"), and about self-promotion that is false. A maintainer becomes project owner without anyone promoting them, and in a workspace with sensitive projects it is the difference between restricting and being unrestrictable.
documents.s: Context

documents.t: 1. The workspace upsert receives the actor and refuses self-movement. AddWorkspaceMemberUseCase.execute becomes (workspaceId, atorId, alvoId, papel) — the same order AddProjectMemberUseCase has had since 0127 and RemoveProjectMemberUseCase gained in 0156 —, the controller passes @CurrentUser(), and changing one's OWN role there is 403. 2. The ceiling does NOT count owners. Refusing only when the caller is the last owner would be the obvious "safe" rule, and it is rejected by the literal criterion of ADR 0127: "it is stated in a clause, it has no number to age". A count ages in three ways — it introduces one more read that can fall out of phase with the write; it has to decide what to do when the second owner is a service account or a person who left the company, which the api cannot tell apart; and it makes the route's answer depend on the state of OTHER rows, so the same call with the same body passes today and refuses tomorrow without anything the caller controls having changed. Whoever wants to leave their own role asks another owner, which is the same outcome ceiling 2 already produced in the project. And there is an argument stronger than aesthetics: the clause already produces the invariant the count would exist to guarantee. A workspace never ends up without an owner, because the route requires owner and the only actor able to remove the last owner would be themselves — which is exactly the refused move. The number does not need to be counted because the shape of the rule makes it unreachable. 3. Ceiling 1 does NOT have a pair in this scope, and the absence is a decision. It was really considered, because here — unlike 0156's removal — the move EXISTS: an owner can downgrade another owner. The refusal comes from ceiling 1 being a rule about hierarchy inversion, and inversion not being possible in this scope: in the project, projectRole ?? workspaceRole makes the project row OVERRIDE the workspace one (RN-471), so a maintainer reaches whoever is ABOVE them. That is how 0127 described the damage: "the owner loses their own project (…) restoring requires maintainer, which the owner just lost in that scope". Whoever acted was BELOW whoever suffered; in the workspace that does not happen. @RequireRole('owner') is the top of ROLE_ORDER, so whoever calls the route is never below anyone it reaches. The precondition of ceiling 1 is absent — it is not a forgotten symmetry, it is a rule without a subject. And the cost of adding the pair anyway would be high and irreversible: added to the ceiling of point 1 and the absence of a removal route, owner would become an absorbing state — nobody would ever leave it over HTTP, neither by their own will nor by another owner's hand. Offboarding someone who leaves the company, ownership rotation and correcting a wrong invitation would come to require a direct database write. That is the class of state ADR 0127 was born to eliminate, assembled again with the sign flipped. Downgrading another owner, therefore, STAYS — and it is reversible through the same route, by any remaining owner, which the project move was not. 4. Self-promotion closes, on BOTH association routes. Ceiling 2 stops being "nobody downgrades themselves" and becomes "nobody touches their own role", in both directions, in the project and in the workspace. Rewriting the SAME role still passes: an idempotent upsert is not a move, and refusing it would break seed.ts, which rewrites roles on purpose. 5. The rule is not copied: the comparison becomes ONE classifier. The module domain/iam/tetos-de-rebaixamento.ts gains autoMovimentoDoProprioPapel, which returns the DIRECTION ('rebaixamento' | 'promocao' | null) instead of a boolean. It was this, and not a separate ehAutoPromocao, because the caller needs the direction: the decision of point 6 requires different messages, and two boolean predicates would make each use case ask the same comparison twice to find out which of the two answered. ehAutoRebaixamento still exists and becomes a reading of the classifier (=== 'rebaixamento'), byte for byte in behavior. It survives for a behavioral reason and not a compatibility one: whoever delegates to it is remocaoEhAutoRebaixamento, and REMOVAL only sees the lower half. Widening it would make removal also refuse self-promotion — and removing one's own project row that restricted someone is precisely how one undoes the restriction ceiling 1 prevents from being created, the benign move point 3 of ADR 0156 protected explicitly. Unifying everything would have changed, in passing, a door this ADR did not open. 6. The messages are specific by DIRECTION and by SCOPE. There are four, and none serves two things: whoever tried to promote themselves does not receive the downgrade sentence (it is not what they did), and whoever hits the workspace ceiling is not sent to talk to a maintainer — there the role that undoes is owner.
